Until then they were imported naming none, and the graph emits no barrier before a first write behind an import with no history, so frame N+1's first write of a buffer was ordered after frame N's last read of it only by whichever barriers happened to chain between them; the queue orders nothing between two submissions (`FrameContext::end_frame` waits on nothing from the frame before, and frames two slots apart overlap on the device). Most of the chain rode those barriers — a build's last read in frame N is followed by a build-to-compute barrier, which chains through frame N+1's compute-to-compute ones — but **a buffer last read at the fragment stage did not**: the resolve's shadow rays traverse the top-level structure, the bottom-level set and the cluster chunks and read the record-to-entry table, and in a traced frame no barrier between frame N's resolve and frame N+1's builds names the fragment stage in its source. That is a write-after-read hazard across frames, the class R171's fault was one level up, which no case has shown (a capture waits for its frame) and which a flight could show as shadows from a half-built structure or a lost device. The import naming the last use costs a barrier at each buffer's first use a frame (the counts are in [the audit](../experiments/pass-declarations-audit.md#r186-1-what-was-mended)) and makes frame N+1's chain wait for frame N's resolve, which it had to. **The scratch** (`GpuScene::rt_scratch`) is declared by all four builds ("clas cache", each "clas" chunk, "blas", "tlas"): every one starts its scratch at the same address, and between two chunks the only barrier had been the arrays' write-to-write one, whose destination named no read (R186 D1, gfx.md's rule for a declared build write). The other per-frame buffers a frame leaves for the next (the visibility buffer, the visible list, the deform pool, the Hi-Z) are the audit's class (c), still imported naming nothing; the graph carrying an import's last state across frames is their row.

### A step is made on the worker

Roadmap R152. **A step the policy asks for is made on the worker that frees the retired buffers, from a copy of what it needs of the scene, and taken by the frame's thread when it is ready** (`renderer.rt.step_on_worker`, true). What a swapped step still cost the frame was the driver's allocation, which R128 measured from 1 to 349 ms for the same step on a full card; the frame's thread now copies the inputs (`GpuScene::rt_step_inputs`), schedules `GpuScene::make_rt_step` — allocations and size queries, nothing of the scene read or written — and goes on recording into the chain it has. The first `begin_frame` that finds the step made takes it (`GpuScene::take_rt_step`: a handful of assignments, the replaced buffers to the slot's retired list as a swapped resize's are). One step at a time, on the one thread that frees, so an allocation never runs beside a free and the memory a free returns is there for the step behind it. The step's types are `rt_step.h`'s and its functions live in `gpu_scene_rt_step.cpp`, out of the hub.

**Only a frame the chain is already short for waits.** A step asked for by the headroom rule, by the slope or by a shrink lands a frame or more later and costs no frame anything. When the demand read back has already passed what the chain holds, the frame waits for the worker rather than record into too little: what it pays is the allocation of the chunks it lacks, never a free and never the device. A step made for a chain that has since been laid out again (`GpuScene::rt_step_current`) is dropped; whoever resizes on its own thread — a frame somebody waits for, the first capacity, `renderer.rt.swap_resize=false`, `renderer.rt.step_on_worker=false` — waits for a step in flight and drops it first. An allocation the device refuses leaves the chain as it is and says so; the policy asks again when the demand next does. `RtStats::worker_steps`, `worker_step_ms` and `peak_worker_step_ms` count them, and a step that took the worker more than a slow frame is logged at info with its parts, since it is the time the chain went on at its old capacity and not a frame's.

**What a step made ahead holds** (R133, 2026-11-15). The step stands beside the chain it replaces from the moment the worker makes it until the frames that read the old buffers have completed — taken by the next `begin_frame`, its replaced buffers on that slot's retired list until the slot comes round — so for three or four frames the device holds `GpuScene::rt_step_bytes` more than the chain: the chunks the new capacity lacks (one chunk, at most 598 MB with micromaps, for a growth by the headroom; the whole chain while it is one chunk), the bottom-level set, and the references when they move. The capacity itself never passes the budget, so the transient is at most the budget again; on a 12 GB card up to 570 MiB beside a chain of up to 1.1 GiB. **The worker does not ask the device's room**: a step on the frame's thread asks the memory budget first and waits, frees and makes when the two sets will not fit (R116, which measured a growth made beside a card another process held 20 GB of at 524 ms in the driver against 37 waited), while the worker makes beside the old set whatever the budget says. On the worker that time is not a frame's unless the frame is short, and whether the driver's eviction costs the frames after it was not measured, so the rule is R152's and such a step is counted (`RtStats::worker_steps_past_budget`) and logged at info (`the ray tracing chain's step is made past the device's budget`, with the step's bytes, the used bytes and the budget) for a recording on a full card to settle. Measured on the streamed forest at 3840×2160 traced with the bounce, worker on and off alternating in one binary: a step made ahead costs its frame 0.37 ms at the median (most 2.9) where the frame's thread made it in 2.7 to 3.1 (most 10.2), and a step the frame is already short for costs it the allocation either way, 2.1 to 2.8 ms ([the measurement](../experiments/rt-step-ahead-2026-11-15.md)).

**The shrink window is two minutes** (`renderer.rt.shrink_seconds`, 120; ten until R152). The walk looks at the forest, away and back within half a minute, and a ten-second window halved the chain at every look away: 18 shrinks, and 16 of the 17 growths after them went back to a capacity a shrink had just given up. Replayed through `RtCapacity` on the CPU, the walk's own demand under a two-minute window shrinks once, at its end, and no growth undoes a shrink; the chain holds 2.86 GB on average where it held 2.13 ([the replay](../experiments/rt-chain-walk-2026-11-12.md#the-policy-replayed)). `rt capacity: a two-minute window holds the chain between a walk's views of the forest` holds the shape. What it costs is the memory a sparse view keeps for two minutes instead of ten seconds, on a scene whose first capacity is the budget: the endless desert's surround holds its 2.3 GB for the first two minutes where it held it for ten seconds.

### A guess is not a demand

Roadmap R81 (2026-11-17; [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-the-traced-chain-holds-what-frames-asked-for.md), [the measurement](../experiments/rt-structures-memory-2026-11-17.md)). **The first capacity of a chain that does not hold its whole union is provisional, and is given back once its first frames have said what they build.** A scene too large to hold whole starts at `first_rt_capacity`: every pair a frame could build, clamped to the budget. No frame asked for that, and the rules above treated it as if one had: held for the shrink window (two minutes since R152), then halved once a window, the floor kept for a peak that never was. The village's walk at 3840×2160 under traced primaries and shadows builds at most 6,457 structures a frame and references 8,233 cached ones; its chain held the budget's 330,125 clusters — 2.1 GB on the RTX 5090, the "ray-tracing structures" of batch 67's 3.7 GB — for the whole flight, and would have held half of it after two minutes and a quarter after four. The budget is a share of the card, so that number said what the card is and not what the scene needs.

**The rule** (`RtCapacityConfig::first_seconds`, `renderer.rt.first_seconds`, 10; `RtCapacity::provisional`). While the capacity is the first one and less than the union, its window is `first_seconds` from the **first observed frame** — a load before it is no part of it — and the shrink window's frames (240). When that window closes, if its peak demand with the headroom is at most half the capacity, the capacity goes to that fit at once: no floor, and `hold` does not remember the guess, so a growth afterwards goes to what the frames want and never back to the budget. A window whose frames wanted more than half leaves an ordinary capacity, as does any growth and any frame somebody waited for (`grow_to`); from then on every rule above holds unchanged. **A chain that holds its whole union is not a guess** (`RtCapacity::first_is_guess`): no frame can want more than it holds, which is a guarantee worth the ordinary window, and it is every scene the tests draw. **A world still arriving starts the window again**: while what a frame could build (`rt_frame_estimate` plus `rt_reference_estimate`) has risen by more than the headroom since the window began, the renderer says so on the tail's change (`RtCapacity::scene_grew`), so a load that outlasts ten seconds is not judged by its own fast, empty frames — the case R116 found on the v25 walk, whose load's frames wanted a tenth of what the world then did. A walk's tiles come and go and the estimate stays about where it was; a load's only come. The give-back is asked again every frame until the step has landed (a frame that is taking another step cannot start one), with whatever the frames since have wanted, and the renderer logs it once: `the ray tracing chain's first capacity was a guess`, with what was held and the fit.

**What it changes for a frame.** Nothing in a frame somebody waits for, which is drawn complete as before. A frame in flight after the give-back stands where every frame stands once a chain has shrunk: a demand that jumps past the headroom before a growth lands is short for the two frames the read-back takes, and the growth is a step made on the worker. The guess used to cover a session's first two minutes against that; it no longer does. `first_seconds` 0 is the rule before, the comparison. `rt capacity: a first capacity that was a guess is given back after its first window`, `... a guess the frames wanted half of, or a whole union, is held`, `... a world still arriving starts the guess's window again` and `... a give-back stands until the caller has resized` hold the arithmetic on the CPU.

**The pair** ([the measurement](../experiments/rt-structures-memory-2026-11-17.md#stage-1-the-pair); the village walk at 3840×2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt`, the bounce, main's copied-out release build against this rule's, alternating in one lease on the RTX 5090, the session locked and half the CPU others'): the chain's structures **2,088.0 → 152.3 MiB**, the process's device memory **4,017 → 2,135 MiB**, the GPU frame 5.965 and 5.956 ms on main against 5.947 (`clas` 0.145 → 0.123 ms, one chunk to build into where the guess had six), and no frame short of its demand: the guess went back at measured frame 902, to 8,192 clusters, and one growth took the chain to 12,288 as the walk's demand rose to 7,161. With the budget a card of 8 GB or 4 GB has (`--rt-budget-mib 512`) the same walk ends on the same 152.3 MiB, where the guess was 652. The streamed forest's guess (330,936 clusters, 2.8 GB of chunks) went back two frames into its flight with none of 9,003 frames short; that flight is also where a capacity held before any frame stopped being remembered as a peak (`RtCapacity::resized`): the chain is made for a streamed world's prefix and made again when its first tiles arrive, and the growth after the give-back went back to the prefix's 56,466 for a demand of 10,119.

**What is left after it** is on that page, by kind (`place.structures`): the resident cache's slots, allocated whole at their ceiling (506 MiB on the streamed forest for 3,045 occupied), every slot at the driver's most, and a chain that holds its whole union at that reservation whether or not its frames build (a static world's 15 MiB of set and 15 of scratch for no build at all).

### A guess past the budget is not made at it

Roadmap W51 (stage 3, W51-6, 2026-11-19; [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-a-chain-past-its-budget-starts-at-its-floor.md), which supersedes where [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-the-traced-chain-holds-what-frames-asked-for.md) made the first capacity; [the measurement](../experiments/start-commit-by-owner-2026-11-18.md#w51-6-the-peak-at-the-first-frame)). **A scene whose estimate passes the budget starts at `renderer.rt.initial_clusters` (65,536), not at the budget, and grows by what its frames ask** (`first_rt_capacity`). The budget is a share of the card (a sixteenth, scaled for micromaps: 337,597 clusters on the RTX 5090) and says nothing of the scene, so a first capacity there was a guess of the card's size: on the forest's staging at 3840 × 2160 under traced primaries and shadows it was made at `create` — six chunks, 2.8 GiB, and a bottom-level set sized by it — held through the rest of the load, made again at the budget when the world's first tiles arrived, and given back ten seconds into the frames for a first frame that built 6,306 structures. That hold was the load's maximum: the commit's peak sat on the first frame, where the guess met the world's first commit. A scene inside its budget is untouched (allocated for every pair it could build, and so never drops anything), and so is every scene the tests draw.

**What a frame does instead.** The frames before the first read-back record into the floor; one that wants more keeps whole instances, drawn before casters, and counts what it dropped (`RtStats`, the flythrough's `rt_built` and `rt_wanted`), exactly as any frame past its capacity does ([below](#past-the-capacity-by-size-on-screen)); the read-back's growth is a step made on the worker, and a frame already short for it waits for that allocation ([above](#a-step-is-made-on-the-worker)). A frame somebody waits for (`render_offscreen`, every capture and test) is drawn complete as before. The floor is still a guess where the union is larger, so the first window gives it back as it gave the budget back. `renderer.rt.initial_clusters=16777216` is the rule before for the frame's own capacity, the comparison; the pair is on the experiment page.

**The cache's references start at the floor too** (`first_rt_references`), whatever their estimate, which is every cached pair in every view. A reference costs mostly its share of the bottom-level set (334 bytes on the RTX 5090 with micromaps, `rt_bytes_per_reference()`), and on the staging the estimate was inside the references' ceiling, so the world's arrival took them from the floor to it before the first frame: a waited resize that freed and made the whole chain again, chunks and all, for a bottom-level set of 650 MiB where the floor's is 279, given back ten seconds later for frames that referenced 50,016. A frame whose references pass the floor drops whole instances, counted, as one past the frame's own capacity does; a union under the floor is held whole, as before, so every scene the tests draw starts where it did.

### The budget follows the device

Roadmap R107 (2026-10-27). **With nothing named, the budget is a sixteenth of the device-local memory, never under 512 MiB nor over 4,096** (`resolve_rt_budget`, `rt_device_budget_mib`, `k_rt_budget_device_share`, `k_rt_budget_floor_mib`, `k_rt_budget_ceiling_mib` in `rt_capacity.h`): 2,025 MiB on the 32 GB RTX 5090, 1,536 on 24 GB, 1,024 on 16 GB, 768 on 12 GB, 512 on 8 GB and below. `RenderSettings::rt_budget_mib` (`--rt-budget-mib`, the protocol's `rt_budget_mib`) overrides it, and so does the `renderer.rt.budget_mib` tunable when it is not zero — its default is now 0, which is the rule; an explicit budget is taken as given, floor and ceiling or not. Until then the default was 1,024 MiB on every card, chosen on the desert overlook, whose chain peaks at 134 MB; the forest proof of concept's expanded forest at 11520×2160 wants 243,604 structures a frame (1.46 GiB at 6,426 bytes, a capacity of 1.84 GiB with the headroom) and **dropped instances' structures on every frame at 1 GiB, which cost it 29 ms**: the one-thread drop rule in `ranges_main` runs whenever a frame is past its capacity, and was 35 ms of the `rt` pass's 43.6, where the chain that fits is 8.1 ms ([the measurement](../experiments/rt-chain-forest-2026-10-27.md)):

| budget | capacity | dropped (instance events over 600 frames) | `rt` | `clas` | `resolve` | GPU frame (median) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 MiB (the old default) | 167,093 | 206,836 | 43.55 ms | 3.47 ms | 31.62 ms | 90.29 ms |
| 1,536 MiB | 250,640 | 0 | 8.16 ms | 5.51 ms | 37.46 ms | 61.03 ms |
| 2,048 MiB | 334,186 | 0 | 8.10 ms | 5.50 ms | 37.52 ms | 61.01 ms |
| **the device's, 2,025 MiB** | 330,433 | 0 | 8.06 ms | 5.39 ms | 37.71 ms | 61.15 ms |

(RTX 5090, `msvc-release`, offscreen, each run under the GPU lock with `--wait-quiet 120`; the 1,024 and the device rows were quiet by the harness's rule, the other two had other processes on up to 20% of the CPU at their end, so they are upper bounds; the page has every row's machine state.) **What the 243,604 are**: the swaying plants of the inner two rings — full meshes the pool deforms, so never cone-tested, never a static form and never cached — 223,795 drawn and 15,741 off-frustum casters (98%); the ground 4,062 (1.7%); rigid casters 6. The rings past them are 2.35 million drawn pairs of static forms built once.

**Why a sixteenth, why the heaps.** A sixteenth is the smallest power-of-two share that holds that frame with its headroom on the card it runs on; a larger one costs the scenes past it, because a scene past its budget holds the whole budget from its first frame (`first_rt_capacity`) and the shrink rule leaves it while the frames want more than half of it. The rule reads the heaps' size (`gfx::MemoryBudget::device_local_bytes`, known with or without `VK_EXT_memory_budget`), not the driver's budget, which moves with what other processes hold, so a card gives the same capacity and the same drops every run. The floor is the desert overlook's first capacity with room; it lowers a 6 or 8 GB card's ceiling from the old 1,024, which is the direction a card that small wants. The ceiling is about 670,000 structures at the 5090's cost, past which the builds' time and not their memory is the limit. `RtCapacity`'s headroom, growth and shrink are unchanged, so a scene that wants less settles where it did. **What it costs a scene past its budget at load**: one whose first estimate (every pair it could build, in every view) is past the budget starts *at* the budget, which is now larger — the endless desert's and the erg's surround budget runs, whose estimates count every terrain slot in three views, start at 330,125 and 331,827 clusters (2.31 and 2.51 GB of chain) where they started at about half that, and their first shrink window (240 frames) brings them to 16,384 and 8,192 (293 and 434 MB), exactly as before (since R116 they halve once a minute on the way there, [above](#a-view-that-comes-back-regrows-once)). Their frames are unchanged: the five frame budgets pass, the endless surround's `rt` at 1.067 ms median against the 1.064 ms main measured with the cache off ([the measurement](../experiments/rt-chain-forest-2026-10-27.md#the-frame-budgets)).

**The budget follows the micromaps** (R120, batch 53). A scene that bakes opacity micromaps sizes and builds every set with `ALLOW_CLUSTER_OPACITY_MICROMAPS`, which raises the driver's worst case for a CLAS from 6,144 to 8,832 bytes on the RTX 5090, so a sixteenth of the device held 231,909 clusters with them where it held 338,115 without — below the 250,964 the v25 walk builds at 11520×2160, and a default that dropped structures the picture had. So **the device's rule is multiplied by the slot growth before the floor and the ceiling**: `GpuScene` runs the budget's two driver probes (65,536 and 131,072 clusters) a second time without the micromap flag, and `rt_device_budget_mib(device_local_bytes, slot_bytes, base_slot_bytes)` scales the sixteenth by the slope with the flag over the slope without (`rt_bytes_per_cluster()` over `rt_bytes_per_cluster_plain()`; measured, not read from the two worst-case sizes, so the records, addresses and the bottom-level set's share are in both), and the chain holds as many clusters with micromaps as it would without. A 32 GiB device at the bare slots' 1.4375 is 2,944 MiB; the RTX 5090's 32,404 MiB of heaps, at the v25 walk's measured 9,156 bytes a cluster against 6,280, takes **2,952 MiB** where the rule gave 2,025 (+927 MiB), and the walk's capacity is 338,072 clusters where it was 338,115 (the test scene's two probes measure 9,130 against 6,399: 2,889 MiB). The ceiling (4,096) admits it on a 32 GB card and binds from about 45 GB up, where the sixteenth alone is already past the v25 walk's need; the floor (512) is reached first on cards of under about 5.7 GB. **Only the device's rule is scaled**: `RenderSettings::rt_budget_mib` and `renderer.rt.budget_mib` are taken exactly as named, so a measurement that names a budget compares like with like, and a scene that bakes no micromaps (no alpha-tested material, the extension absent, the opaque proxy on, or `renderer.shadow.micromaps=false`) keeps the rule as it was. The source says which: `device-micromaps` beside `setting`, `tunable` and `device`, and the "ray tracing ready" log line carries `bytes_per_cluster_plain` beside `bytes_per_cluster`. `rt capacity: the device's budget is scaled by the micromaps' slot growth` holds the arithmetic on the CPU, and `alpha mask: micromaps are the default where the device has them, and the budget follows` on the device.

**Where it says so.** `GpuScene::rt_budget_mib()`/`rt_budget_source()`, `RtStats::budget_mib`/`budget_source`, the flythrough summary's `rt` block (`FlythroughRt` version 5: `budget_mib`, `budget_source` — `setting`, `tunable`, `device` or `device-micromaps`), engine-view's windowed summary, the "ray tracing ready" log line (with the device-local MiB it was taken from), and `engine.budgets`: the process reports `source: "device"` with no limit when the tunable is 0, each scene its own budget and source. **What holds it**: `rt capacity: the default budget is a sixteenth of the device, 512 to 4096 MiB` (the rule and the precedence, on the CPU) and `rt capacity: a scene with no budget named takes the device's, and says so` (a scene's limit and statistics with nothing named, a setting and the tunable).

### Past the capacity, by size on screen

**Since R174** (2026-11-18; [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-a-frame-past-its-capacity-keeps-by-size-on-screen.md), proposed, which holds the reasoning and what was weighed). **What a frame past its capacity keeps is a function of the scene, the camera and the capacity, never of the order the layout lists the instances in**, for a frame whose cache built every miss ([below](#the-caches-misses-and-the-guarantee)). Until then the capacity was spent first-fit along the layout's order, and the same placements handed over in another order (G205's hand-off cells against the whole hand-over, the engine meadow, `--raster rt`) dropped 19,674 instances' structures in both runs with traced pictures 3.5% apart at 3840 × 2160 ([world](world.md#a-hand-off-placement-is-held-by-its-band)).

**The key.** Past the capacity `ranges_main` keys every instance that wants a structure (`keep_key` in `clas_records.slang`; `gfx::rt_keep_key` is the same on the CPU):

- `q`, 15 bits, **its size on screen**: `u = asuint(d²) − asuint(r²)`, with `d²` the squared distance from the eye to its mesh's sphere's centre and `r` that sphere's radius times `scale_max`, then `q = (u + 8·2²³) >> 13` clamped to 0..32767 — 1,024 steps an octave of (d/r)², d/r from 1/16 to 4,096. Smaller is larger on screen and kept first. The centre is its own fixed-order expansion, one `precise` operation a line, not `instance_point` (whose dots a driver may fuse), so the CPU computes the same bits. **The sphere is the GPU's** (`CullParams::mesh_bounds`, made by `mesh_bounds_main` through `length()`): the CPU takes it as an input and a test that holds the two hands it the GPU's bits, never a sphere computed on the CPU. With the instance pass off there are no spheres: every instance takes the top `q`, and the hash alone orders them.
- `h`, 16 bits: the high half of lowbias32 over its cell relative to the eye's and the twelve words of its 3×4, seeded as `fade_seed`, so a scene moved by whole cells keys alike and nothing of the record's place enters.
- The eye is view 0's: a set's views share one ([gfx](gfx.md), "What a pass is given").
- An item's key: on the ray path (`k_cluster_records_drawn_first`) `kind << 31 | q << 16 | h`, every drawn structure before any caster; otherwise `q << 17 | kind << 16 | h`, the drawn before the casters at one size. A caster's key is above its drawn key, so casters never stand without their drawn clusters.

**The cut.** For each capacity — the frame's own structures, the cache's references — `K` is the least key at which the structures keyed at or below it pass it; every item keyed below `K` is kept, every other dropped, equal keys together. An instance spends one capacity only (both its counts carry the one cached mark). The passes past the ranges are dispatched from the drop words, so a frame that fits dispatches none of their groups; they are one timer zone, "ranges drop", as the walk was:

| pass | groups | does |
|---|---|---|
| `ranges_main` | the instance blocks | past the capacity: each key into the keep keys, each item's structures added at its key's top 16 bits to its capacity's level-1 histogram |
| `keep_cut_main` | one | each capacity's crossing level-1 bin, and the structures below it |
| `keep_ties_main` | the instance blocks | the crossing bin's items added at `h` to the level-2 histogram |
| `keep_fine_main` | one | the crossing `h`: `K`, and the room the cut leaves |
| `ranges_kept_count_main`, `ranges_kept_main` | the instance blocks | keep what is keyed below `K`, count the instances dropped (words 2 and 3), the prefix sums and bottom-level records |

#### The guarantee is at one capacity

The capacity is an input of the cut and depends on history and on time: a growth lands when the worker has made it ([a step is made on the worker](#a-step-is-made-on-the-worker)) and the shrink windows are seconds. So the guarantee is that at one capacity two orders of the same placements keep the same set. A frame somebody waits for (`render_offscreen`, a capture) is drawn complete up to the budget, at the limit when it wants more, so its capacity is a function of the scene, the camera and the budget; a two-orders case compares such frames and asserts `capacity` and `limit` equal before a pixel. There is no hysteresis.

#### The cache's misses, and the guarantee

Past its free and evicted slots the cache builds a frame's misses in the frame's own set in the order the emit pass appended them, and a miss with no room there either draws nothing (`cache_assign_main`, R114; word 11): which clusters those are follows the atomics and the cache's history. How many is a function of the inputs: a slot drawn this frame is never evicted and the eviction frees every other one a frame needs, so the unbuilt misses number `max(0, D − (S − 1) − (capacity − built))`, with `D` the distinct keys the kept cached instances reference and `S` the slots with slot 0. **The guarantee holds for a frame with no unbuilt miss**; `RtStats::cache_unbuilt_frames` counts the others, a case of this rule with the cache on asserts it is zero, and keying the overflow is [R190](../roadmap.md). Bounding the misses inside the cut was weighed and not taken (ADR-0074, decision 6): `D` over the prefix is a distinct count, two passes over the cached pairs and a word a key, on fitting frames too.

#### The cut's tables are cleared every frame

The keep block (`GpuScene::rt_keep_tables`: the `gfx::ClusterKeepTables` with the frame's eye and the addresses, the cut words, and four histograms of 65,536 words) is written and cleared by the frame's reset transfer pass whenever the chain runs, and every pass that touches it declares its read and its write. One block serves the frames in flight; it is imported naming its last use (all commands, a write), so the reset's barrier waits for the frame before. No frame's cut reads what another left.

**What it holds, and when.** The keys are two words an instance slot inside `instance_counts`, which grows with the slots: 8 bytes a slot where the drop order's sequence held 32 and each frame slot's copy of the order 12 more, so 1.75 MB on the forest's 219,166 slots against 7.0 MB and 2.6 MB a copy before. The histograms are 1 MiB, made once with the chain before its first frame whatever the scene's size, and needed from the first frame past its capacity, which can be the first. A scene that never passes its capacity pays the 1 MiB and the clear. The CPU no longer lays an order out at every tail change.

#### A cut can keep nothing at a small named budget

The prefix keeps the largest on screen first, so one near instance first in key order and past the capacity alone — the scene's grid, a ground tile — keeps nothing, and on the ray path no caster either; first-fit had skipped it. At the device's budget (its floor holds about 60,000 structures) that is no concern; at a named one (`--rt-budget-mib 1` is about 165 clusters) it can be the whole set. A second round over the key-sorted groups past `K`, against the room left, keeps the guarantee and is the next step if R174's measuring run finds kept structures under half the capacity at 1 or 16 MiB.

#### The kept set moves with the camera

The instances keyed near `K` enter and leave the traced set frame to frame as the camera and the demand move — a popping hole on the ray path, a popping shadow under traced shadows — and when the eye crosses a 64 m cell every member of the crossing level-1 bin is picked again, since `h` hashes the cell relative to the eye's. The pops are of the smallest instances on screen. Nothing decides from the last frame's kept set; a counter of the instances whose kept state changed is R174's measuring run's.

**What holds it.** On the CPU, `rt keep: two orders of the same placements keep the same set at a capacity that forces a drop`, `rt keep: the kept set is a prefix of the keys, ties kept or dropped whole` and `rt keep: the size key is monotone in distance and radius, and a scene moved by whole cells keys alike`. On the device, `clas records: past the capacity the cut keeps what rt_keep keeps` (word for word and the keys to the bit given the same spheres, over 84 cases with and without the cache, both layouts of the key, equal keys and one size of several hashes straddling the capacities, and drawn first at exactly the drawn total), `clas records: two orders of the same instances keep the same instances`, `clas records: consecutive frames past and within the capacity cut from cleared tables`, `clas records: a set sized under the frame keeps whole instances, casters last` (whose sphere-less instance at the eye showed on a device that a zero radius must be the top `q` before the difference, not after), `engine-view: past the budget the chain drops the same structures every run`, and over the whole chain the same placements in two orders: `rt chain: past the budget the traced picture follows the placement, not the order` (the grid listed in reverse, on the ray path and under traced shadows, past 1, 2 and 3 MiB, waited-for frames compared once both stand at one capacity and one limit; at 1 MiB its first run on the RTX 5090 kept nothing, 0 of a capacity of 164 against 551 wanted, which is the small-budget case above, so the case asks that one of the three keep something) and `engine-view: past the budget the chain drops the same structures in either order` (2,400 listed trees under traced primaries past 16 MiB, with the cache off, and with it on and the trees swaying, where the summary's `cache_unbuilt_frames` must be zero; swaying trees under the cache draw differently in the two orders inside the budget too, 61,874 pixels of 230,400 on the RTX 5090 on 2026-11-18 with the same command giving the same bytes twice, which is not the keep's, so that mode asks that no pixel part past the budget that a whole chain kept). Whether the frame budgets' runs drop is not checked by their gate, which holds timing zones only.

### Static structures for rigid forms

Roadmap R94 (2026-10-25). **The chain built a structure for every visible pair every frame, including the ones whose cut never changes.** A streamed forest's far rings are distance forms ([Authored instances per tile](#authored-instances-per-tile)) — tens of thousands of instances of a few dozen meshes — and every frame rebuilt each one's cut: the proof of concept's grass clearing at 11520×2160 under `--raster rt` wanted **475,281** structures a frame against a 1 GiB budget of 118,214, so every frame dropped about 60,000 instances' structures; the v8 forest's hardwoods view wanted 56,510 at 1600×900 under traced shadows. Most of them were forms ([the experiment](../experiments/rt-static-forms-2026-10-25.md)).

**A rigid form is drawn at a fixed cut, and its structures are built once.** A form is the top of its source's DAG, so the cull still chooses among several of its levels by distance — it is not a fixed cut by itself, and a structure built once from all of it would hold overlapping levels (the shards [One cut for every view](#one-cut-for-every-view) describes). Its **frontier** is: the clusters `extract_lod_form` left at level 0, one on every path of the form's DAG, the finest cut any camera in the ring can ask for ([geometry](geometry.md#distance-forms)). With `ResolvedSettings::static_forms` — the chain, the cull's cut, `RenderSettings::rt_static_forms` and the `renderer.rt.static_forms` tunable (both on by default), build records rather than templates — `GpuScene` (`plan_static_forms`) takes every mesh that is a form (`SceneData::form_source`) and rigid (`form_rigid`), and:

- **patches the GPU's copy of its LOD data** so the cull selects the frontier at every distance: the frontier's parent error is terminal, so it never coarsens, and every other cluster's own error terminal, so it never draws; the coverage words follow, so the foliage threshold cannot move it either. The scene's own copy is untouched. The raster picture and the rays both see the frontier, so **the ray path's picture is still the rasterized one word for word** and a traced shadow is still cast by exactly the cut the picture draws — no second cut, no bias.
- **builds one structure per frontier cluster and one bottom-level structure per mesh**, at create, in one blocking submission (`build_static_forms`): the CLAS records as the frame writes them (opaque, or not where the material is alpha-tested), but with the cluster's **index within its mesh** as the cluster id and base geometry index, since there is no visible entry to name. The bottom-level set has a record per mesh of the scene — empty for a mesh with no static form, whose address the build writes as zero — so `ClusterBlasSet::addresses` is the per-mesh table the top-level dispatch reads, with no copy.
- **flags every tail instance of such a mesh** `gfx::k_instance_static_rt` (`write_slots`). `clas_records.slang`'s bucketing pass leaves its entries out before it counts them, so the frame neither builds, wants nor drops them, and its own bottom-level structure is empty; `tlas_references.slang` gives its top-level record its mesh's static address instead (`TlasReferenceParams::static_addresses`, 88 bytes). The transform and custom index are written as for any instance, so a move or a tile's change costs what it did.
- **decodes a static hit by its instance**: a hit whose instance carries the flag names `{instance, mesh.first_cluster + geometry index}`, any other the visible entry (`hit_pair` in `scene.slang`), in the ray path's primary rays and tie scan, the resolve's alpha-tested shadow loop and the reference path tracer. A static structure holds no caster run: the frontier is built whole, so its clusters that face away from the camera and those outside the frustum are in it too — opaque, which a primary ray can meet only through an open mesh's back, where a closed mesh's front face is always nearer — and a shadow ray meets exactly the geometry the caster volumes would have added, and the rest, which is beyond any receiver the view shows.

**What it costs the picture: far trees are drawn finer.** The frontier is the cut a camera at the ring's inner edge asks for, so a form farther out draws more clusters than its distance needs — never fewer, so never a coarser tree. At a ring's inner boundary the frontier is about what the source draws there (the form keeps a frontier cluster only where some camera that far needs it), so a tile handed to its next ring's form under the chain can sharpen where the source had coarsened and never blur; R91's handover measurement is the distance-cut one without the chain. At the hardwoods view the raster cut went from 56,510 to 234,563 pairs and the hardware raster from 0.20 to 0.47 ms, while the structures the frame builds went from 56,510 to 36,884 and the chain from 2.30 to 1.76 ms; at the clearing's 11520×2160 ray path the frame wants **110,282** where it wanted 475,281, which fits the budget, and the chain went from 18.2 to 3.9 ms (the one-thread drop path over 60,000 instances, every frame, was most of the 18). Without the chain nothing changes: a scene with `--shadows csm` or none draws its forms cut by distance as before. `renderer.rt.static_forms=false` restores the per-frame build of distance-cut forms; `renderer.rt.static_build=false` keeps the fixed cut and builds it every frame, which is what the test compares against.

**What holds it.** `engine-view: a rigid form's structures built once trace the per-frame build's bytes` (`authored_view_tests.cpp`): a streamed world of oaks with card levels and spruces in three rings (16 m tiles, radii 1.5, 3 and 6), low across the trees, under traced shadows and under the ray path: 0 pixels differ between the structures built once and the per-frame build of the same cut, with three forms of 53 clusters built once and 56 instances referencing them. `Stats::rt` carries the forms, their clusters and bytes, and the instances and pairs that reference one (`RtStats::static_*`, the flythrough summary's `rt.static_*`, `FlythroughRt` version 2).

**At the size they are** (roadmap R143, 2026-11-10). The forms' cluster structures were built with implicit destinations, which reserve the driver's most for every cluster — 8,832 bytes each where the build allows opacity micromaps, 6,144 without — and a set built once and kept does not need the reservation a set rebuilt every frame does. They are now sized first and packed (`gfx::create_packed_cluster_set`: the build in COMPUTE_SIZES mode, the sizes packed back to back on the host at the device's cluster alignment, the build again with explicit destinations into exactly that sum; what `create_packed_cluster_templates` does for templates), in three blocking submissions at load where there was one. The proof of concept's v40 world keeps 250,832 such clusters in 4,698 forms: 2,113 MiB reserved, **382 MiB packed**, the bottom-level set and the tables included — a form's cluster occupies about a sixth of the reservation ([the measurement](../experiments/rt-small-instances-2026-11-10.md#the-rigid-forms-at-the-size-they-are)). `RtStats::static_reserved_bytes` (the summary's `rt.static_reserved_bytes`) is what the old reservation would have been, beside `static_bytes`, and the "static ray tracing structures built" line says both. The same test holds the picture: the structures are the same builds at other addresses. The resident cache's slots are still the driver's most each ([below](#the-resident-cluster-structure-cache)); packing those needs sizes before a frame's misses are placed, which is a pass on the device and not a loop on the host, and is the next step.

**No LOD bias for the rays.** A coarser cut for the structures than for the picture (asked for as `renderer.rt.lod_bias_px`) was not built: a coarser surface beside the picture's own receivers shadows them where it stands above them, the shards of [One cut for every view](#one-cut-for-every-view), and the cascades measured the same self-shadowing at a coarser cut. With the forms built once the frames that wanted it fit their budget; [the experiment](../experiments/rt-static-forms-2026-10-25.md#what-was-not-built) has the reasoning.

**The KHR fallback** has nothing to split: its bottom-level path is not wired into this module (above), so the static structures are cluster structures only, and a device without them has no chain to build them for.

### The resident cluster structure cache

Roadmap R101 (2026-10-26), which is R63's "cluster structures shared across rigid instances". **The chain built a cluster's structure for every visible (instance, cluster) pair, every frame**, so the same rigid cluster of the same mesh was built again for each instance that drew it and again the next frame. A forest is a few dozen meshes placed tens of thousands of times: the proof of concept's expanded forest at 11520×2160 under traced shadows wanted 222,455 structures a frame against the 1 GiB budget's 166,937, dropped instances on every frame, and spent 33.9 ms of its 98.5 ms in the chain. R94 took the rigid distance forms out by building their frontier once; the prefix's rigid instances and the inner ring's full meshes still rebuilt. The cluster extension is made for the other arrangement — a structure is built once and **referenced** by any number of bottom-level builds, which take only addresses — and this is that.

**What is cached.** A **cached instance** is rigid — `InstanceDesc::deform` invalid, so nothing in the pool moves its vertices and every instance of its mesh traces the same clusters — traced (or, since R152, untraced in a frame whose picture is traced, where its drawn entries are in the chain at all; and a field instance the frame's eye puts [at rest](#the-far-field-at-rest), which the pool gave no block), not a static form, and of a **cached mesh**: every mesh of the scene's own (`SceneData::parts`; a ring slot's mesh is rewritten as the camera moves and is never cached) but a static form's, with at most `gfx::k_cluster_cache_max_clusters` (2^22) clusters. Decided per instance on the GPU (`instance_cached` in `clas_records.slang`), from the mesh's entry in the cache's `bases` table and the instance's own deform word, so a tree that starts to sway stops being cached the frame it does. A cluster has three **keys**, one per form its structure can take: drawn opaque, drawn alpha-tested (non-opaque, so the ray loops test its mask) and shadow caster (non-opaque, and named as one) — and since R120 a fourth, drawn alpha-tested inside a cross-fade band, which names no opacity micromap ([Opacity micromaps](#opacity-micromaps)); `keys` holds each one's **slot**. A slot is the driver's most for one cluster (6,144 bytes at 124 triangles and 64 vertices on the RTX 5090, as an implicit build reserves for each), a fixed piece of one buffer, so a structure built into it stays at the same address for every later frame's bottom-level build. **What is still per frame**: everything a deforming instance draws (skinned, morphed, swaying, every terrain level; built or instantiated from the pool as before), the bottom-level build over every instance, the top-level build, and the cache's misses.

**A frame** (`clas_records.slang`, `gfx::ClusterCacheTables`): the bucketing pass is unchanged; the ranges keep two prefix sums — the frame's own records and the cached instances' **references** — each against its own capacity, and point a cached instance's bottom-level record into the cache's `references` instead of the frame's CLAS addresses; the emit pass writes no record for a cached entry but looks its key up: a resident one has its slot stamped with the frame and its reference addressed at once, a missing one is claimed by exactly one thread (a compare-exchange) and listed as a **miss**, and every reference whose key was not resident is listed as **pending**, its key parked in the reference itself. Then four dispatches, a graph pass each: `cache_scan_main` lists the free slots and counts the occupied ones the frame did not draw by age (frames since they were drawn, 63 buckets and the rest); `cache_evict_main` finds the oldest ages that make room for the misses (each of its groups from the scan's 64 words) and frees them — **least recently drawn first, never a slot this frame drew**; `cache_assign_main` gives each miss a slot, writes its build record (the rest-pose float positions, as a rigid entry always had) and its destination — and a miss it has no slot for a record in the frame's own set ([below](#an-overflow-is-built-in-the-frames-own-set)); and, after the frame's own build, `cache_references_main` writes every pending reference's address. The misses are built with **explicit destinations** (`gfx::build_cluster_set_explicit`, the "clas cache" pass), before the frame's own build, which shares the scratch and which the graph orders after it. A frame that drew nothing new builds nothing there: its count word is zero.

**An idle cache costs nothing** (2026-10-27, roadmap R106). The four dispatches take their sizes from the cache's `args` block (`gfx::k_cluster_cache_args_*`), which the ranges' first dispatch empties every frame and the emit pass grows — the slot scan and the eviction by the frame's first miss, the misses' slots and the pending references by every 64th — so a frame that misses nothing walks no slot, and one whose references are all resident addresses none after the emit pass: the passes are recorded and dispatch no thread. They are timed as one zone, `cache`, beside the build's `clas cache`. **A frame of a scene the cache serves no instance of records none of it**: `GpuScene::rt_cache_instances()` counts the instances it would serve whenever the instances change (`policy_counts`, and at the cache's creation), never per frame, and with none — the endless desert's ring slots, a forest whose every tree sways, every terrain level — the frame records none of the cache's passes and the records chain's plain entry points, `ranges_count_main`, `ranges_main` and `emit_main`, which never read an instance record to ask; with one, their `_cached_` twins (`SceneRenderer::Pipelines::record_*[1]`). The choice is the frame's, from the instance table the CPU already holds, so it never lags the picture: a tail block that brings a rigid rock in turns the cache's passes on in the frame that draws it, its keys and slots still where the last such frame left them. Before R106 the cache was six passes a frame whatever it had to do, and the endless desert's surround run measured its `rt` pass 0.971 → 1.151 ms for a scene that caches nothing; [the experiment](../experiments/rt-cluster-cache-2026-10-26.md#2026-10-27-an-idle-cache-and-the-ranges-scan-r106) has the numbers after.

**How a hit resolves.** A cached structure is every instance's and every frame's, so it cannot name a visible entry. Its cluster id and base geometry index are the cluster's **index within its mesh** with `gfx::k_cluster_cache_geometry` (bit 23) set, and `gfx::k_cluster_cache_caster` (bit 22) for the caster form. `hit_visible_entry` (`scene.slang`) hands such an index on with bit 31 set, which no visible entry reaches, and `hit_pair` decodes it — like a static form's — to `{instance, mesh.first_cluster + index}`, with the instance the top-level record's custom index: exactly the pair the rasterizer drew, so the ray path writes the same id word. The ray path's caster test reads bit 22 (`hit_cached_caster`) where it read the caster run's range, and a cached hit needs no pool block, being rigid. The frame's own records keep their compact dense indices (R100, [below](#the-ray-tracing-chains-index-space)) and `hit_entries`, now bounded under bit 23 — `rt_capacity_limit()` and every resize clamp at 8,388,608 while a cache exists. **Traced visibility still matches the rasterized cut word for word**: the cached structure is built from the same floats, indices and flags as the per-frame record it replaces, and only its name differs.

**The budgets.** The cache is **scene-sized and made once**: as many slots as its meshes' clusters twice over (the drawn and the caster forms; the alpha-tested form is a mesh's drawn one where its material is masked) plus the inactive slot 0, up to its ceiling — a sixty-fourth of the device since R114 ([below](#the-caches-ceiling-follows-the-device)), 506 MiB and 86,357 slots at 6,144 bytes on the RTX 5090, or `renderer.rt.cache_mib` when that is not zero — beside `rt_budget_mib` as the static forms are ([the frame budget](#the-ray-tracing-chains-memory)): a ceiling a scene that needs less never reaches. A cache holds the distinct clusters recent frames drew, not every instance's copy: the desert overlook's whole path touches 11,867, the forest with its forms cut by distance 8,527, the clearing 331. Its slots are allocated whole at create, so the proof of concept's forest, whose chain references 20 cached clusters a frame, pays its 266 MB too; growing it with demand, or packing its slots by the size each structure has (about half the worst case, as the templates showed), is what would stop that. It never grows: **a cache that fills evicts**, which costs the frame builds and never a reallocation in a flight. `renderer.rt.cache_slots` puts a ceiling in slots beside it, for a measurement or the eviction and overflow tests. A frame whose own new clusters outnumber every slot it did not draw keeps what fits — which misses those are follows the atomics, like the pool's overflow — and **builds the rest in its own set** ([below](#an-overflow-is-built-in-the-frames-own-set); until R114 it pointed them at slot 0 and they drew nothing). `RtCapacity`'s budget now bounds **the frame's own builds** only — those misses among them; the **references** have a capacity of their own, sized by the frames with the same arithmetic (a second `RtCapacity`, the `renderer.rt.reference_mib` ceiling, 256 MiB, over `rt_bytes_per_reference()` — eight bytes of address, four of key and the bottom-level set's slope from the same two driver probes) and the same drop rule: an instance whose references do not fit is dropped whole, counted with `dropped_instances`. The bottom-level set holds both. The first capacities come from the scene, as before: the frame's estimate leaves the cached pairs out (`rt_frame_estimate`), the references' is the cached pairs in every view (`rt_reference_estimate`). Everything is counted in `RtStats` (`cache_*`, `references*`, `reference_*`) and the flythrough summary (`FlythroughRt` version 4, `FrameRecord` version 12: `rt_references`, `rt_cache_built`, `rt_cache_evicted` per frame).

**Warm-up is a cost, not a hitch.** The first frame that draws a cluster builds it; the frames after reference it. So the first frames of a flight build what they see and a steady flight builds what newly enters its cut, which `rt_cache_built` per frame shows; the cache's memory is all allocated at create, so a frame never waits for a reallocation of it.

**On by default** (`renderer.rt.cache`, true; false from 2026-10-27 until R106 the same night). Batch 42's frame budgets had found the chain's `rt` pass on the endless desert's surround run — a scene that caches nothing, its ground all ring slots — at 1.151 ms with the cache on against 0.971 ms before R101 (over its 0.951 ms median budget), and 1.064 ms with the cache off: the cache's six passes with nothing to do, and the records chain the cache had restructured (`ranges_main`'s second prefix sum in a 256-thread instance loop, `emit_main`'s key path), which ran with the cache off too. R106 made the idle cache free ([above](#the-resident-cluster-structure-cache)) and the ranges a scan, and the same run measures 0.866 ms with the cache on and 0.864 with it off (1.163 and 1.061 on the tree before, flown beside it); the erg walks are where they were, and the forest proof of concept's traced chain, which references 20 cached clusters a frame, measures the same with the cache as without it ([the experiment](../experiments/rt-cluster-cache-2026-10-26.md#2026-10-27-an-idle-cache-and-the-ranges-scan-r106) has the table and the machine states). `renderer.rt.cache=false` is the per-frame build of every pair, which the tests compare against and the cache is held to byte for byte. Off too under `--rt-templates`, whose point is instantiating every frame; under geometry streaming, whose pages move a cluster's vertices; on a device whose geometry indices stop short of 24 bits; and for a scene read whole none of whose instances could be served — every mesh's instances deformed, untraced or static forms — which makes no slots at all (the erg's terrain mesh had taken the whole 256 MiB ceiling for an instance the terrain stage deforms). A scene whose instances come and go keeps a slot for every mesh, since its tail may place any of them rigid. **The KHR fallback** has no cluster structures to cache, and is not wired into this module ([above](#static-structures-for-rigid-forms)); `domain/gfx`'s cluster acceleration test still holds the per-frame CLAS path pixel-identical to it, and the cache is held to that per-frame path byte for byte.

**What holds it.** `rt cache: rigid structures built once trace the per-frame build's bytes` (`rt_capacity_tests.cpp`): the rigid grid under traced shadows and the ray path, four distances, colour and ids against `renderer.rt.cache=false`, 0 differing; no per-frame structure built; and a **second flight over the same cuts builds nothing**. `rt cache: a full cache evicts the least recently drawn and the picture holds`: a cache sized from the near and far cuts to hold either and not both, near and far in turn — evictions counted, no overflow, the per-frame build's bytes. `rt cache: a frame wanting more than the cache holds builds the rest itself` (R114): a cache of 200 slots under a quarter-pixel cut of several hundred distinct clusters, two frames running on the ray path and under traced shadows — colour and ids the per-frame build's, `cache_overflow` counted, the frame's own `built` the misses and all of its wanted; before R114 it failed on all three. `rt capacity: the cache's ceiling is a sixty-fourth of the device, 256 to 1024 MiB`: the rule and the tunable, on the CPU. `renderer: a rigid instance's cached structures beside skinned ones trace the same bytes` (`renderer_tests.cpp`): a rigid bar between two skinned ones, hw and the ray path. `engine-view: a streamed world's cached structures trace the per-frame build's bytes` (`authored_view_tests.cpp`): the oak and spruce rings under traced shadows, the ray path, and with the static forms off (the forms cut by distance and cached). [The experiment](../experiments/rt-cluster-cache-2026-10-26.md) has the numbers.

**What it bought, and what it did not** (RTX 5090, `msvc-release`, offscreen, each run under the GPU lock; [the experiment](../experiments/rt-cluster-cache-2026-10-26.md) has the machine states). **The forest's 222,455 structures a frame are not rigid copies**: they are its ground — the world's tiles and far levels, every one a terrain level the pool's terrain stage deforms (R107 corrects this for v18: there they are the inner rings' **swaying trees**, 98% of them, and the ground is 4,062 — [The budget follows the device](#the-budget-follows-the-device)) — and R94 had already taken its trees' forms out; its cached instances reference 20 clusters a frame, so its frame and its drops are what they were (97.1 → 95.9 ms at 11520×2160, the chain 33.7 → 34.9 ms, still 619 frames over the capacity) and the cache costs it 266 MB. The chain's 34 ms there is `ranges_main`'s one-thread drop rule over 55,442 instances, run because the ground alone outgrows the budget. (R106 made that rule a scan, [above](#the-ray-tracing-chains-memory): the same flight on the proof of concept's v18 world measures 43.4 ms of chain on the one thread and 5.8 ms on the scan.) Where rigid copies are the cut the cache is the whole saving: the same forest at 1600×900 **with its forms cut by distance** (`renderer.rt.static_forms=false`) went from a 38.8 ms frame, a 33.1 ms chain and 2.9 million dropped-instance events over 644 frames to **9.3 ms, 3.4 ms and none**, 102,150 cached references a frame over 8,527 structures built once; the desert overlook's chain went from 0.35 to 0.24 ms at the median (CLAS build 0.13 → 0.00 ms), the frame 0.54 → 0.42 ms, its first flight building 9,378 structures over 1,559 of 2,401 frames (at most 68 in one) and the two flights after it none. The clearing and the forest with static forms are unchanged within their noise.

#### An overflow is built in the frame's own set

Roadmap R114 (2026-11-01). **The picture never depends on the cache.** The owner's v24 walk through the forest proof of concept saw polygons vanish and come back in front of the player; the chain's budget had dropped nothing (`rt_wanted == rt_built` on every frame of it), but the forest references 53,000 to 55,000 cached clusters a frame against the old fixed ceiling's 43,690 slots, and a frame whose new clusters outnumber every slot it did not draw pointed the rest at slot 0, the inactive structure: those clusters cast and drew nothing, and which ones they were followed the atomics and the walk, so the holes moved. Every other rule in this module that keeps the structures smaller — the cone, occlusion, the LOD, the static forms, the cache itself — is held to the picture it would otherwise draw; an overflow was the exception, and it is no longer.

**What a frame does with a miss the cache cannot place** (`cache_assign_main`, `clas_records.slang`): it writes the record the cache would have built — the rest-pose positions, the form's flags, named as the cache names it, the cluster within its mesh under bit 23 — into the **frame's own records**, after the ones the ranges kept, and marks the key with that record's index (`gfx::k_cluster_cache_frame`). Thread 0 raises the frame's count (word 0, which the "clas" build reads) and its wanted (word 1) by those misses, so the per-frame build the chain already runs for deforming instances builds them too, and `RtCapacity` grows the frame's set for them as it does for any demand. `cache_references_main` now runs **after** the frame's build, the one pass the change moved: a reference to such a key takes the address the build wrote into `clas_addresses`, where one to a slot takes the slot's. A hit on such a structure decodes exactly as a hit on a slot does — same name, same bit 23, same pair — so traced visibility is still the rasterized cut word for word. The scan copies the frame's own record count into the cache's scratch (`gfx::k_cluster_cache_scratch_built`) so the assign pass can place the misses while its thread 0 raises the count. The misses' list is now as long as the references (a frame claims a key once, for a pending reference, so it never has more misses than references; it had more than slots on v24), sixteen bytes a reference in `rt_bytes_per_reference()`.

**Only a frame whose own set is full too draws a miss as nothing** — the chain's budget question, not the cache's: the miss takes slot 0, counted in word 11 (`RtStats::cache_unbuilt`), its wanted already counted, so a frame somebody waits for (`render_offscreen`) grows the set and draws again as it does for a dropped instance, and a frame in flight lives with it for the frames a growth takes, like every other budget event. `RtStats::cache_overflow` still counts every miss the cache had no slot for, now a cost — the per-frame builds the cache exists to save — and the frame's `built` includes them.

**Why not something else.** A transient region of slots for the overflow would be built with explicit destinations in the cache's own pass, so the references could be written where they are; but its size would be a second budget, and past it the overflow would be slot 0 again. The frame's own set is already sized by the frames, with headroom, under a budget that follows the device. The cost is the one moved pass (the references after the build instead of before it) and the misses' list; a frame that misses nothing dispatches none of it, as before.

**What it costs** ([the measurement](../experiments/cluster-cache-overflow-2026-11-01.md); RTX 5090, `msvc-release`, 1920×1080, v24 at the owner's marker 3 walking 1 m/s): at the old 256 MiB ceiling the walk's 46,323 distinct cached clusters overflow by 2,550 a frame, which drew as nothing — 21,045 pixels of the ids, 1% of the frame, differ from the picture without the overflow — and are now built in the frame's own set: 64,579 → 67,148 structures a frame, `clas` 1.359 → 1.494 ms and `rt` 3.631 → 3.774 ms at the median, and the ids the same as the larger cache's to the pixel. At the device's ceiling (86,357 slots) nothing overflows and nothing is evicted, at 265 MB more of slots than the old ceiling.

**No admission rule.** Admitting a cluster to the cache only once it had been drawn some frames in a row was considered, so that a wanted set larger than the slots would settle on the clusters that stay. The cache already settles: a slot drawn this frame is never evicted, so at a standing camera the clusters resident stay resident and the frame builds the same rest every frame, and as the camera moves each new cluster takes the slot of one that left the cut — 0 to 17 a frame along the v24 walk at the old ceiling, against 2,550 misses a frame the cache had no slot for. A counter per key would cost a word a key and a pass, for a churn the walk did not show. (The same rule is why the old overflow's holes stood still at a standing pose and moved as the cut changed: which of a frame's misses wins a freed slot follows the atomics.)

#### The cache's ceiling follows the device

**With `renderer.rt.cache_mib` 0, the default since R114, the ceiling is a sixty-fourth of the device-local heaps, never under 256 MiB nor over 1,024** (`rt_device_cache_mib`, `resolve_rt_cache_mib`, `k_rt_cache_device_share`, `k_rt_cache_floor_mib`, `k_rt_cache_ceiling_mib` in `rt_capacity.h`); the tunable, when it is not zero, is taken as given. The heaps' size, as the chain's budget reads it ([The budget follows the device](#the-budget-follows-the-device)), so a card gives the same cache every run:

| device-local memory | the chain's budget (a sixteenth) | the cache's ceiling (a sixty-fourth) | slots at 6,144 bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 GB (the RTX 5090's 32,404 MiB) | 2,025 MiB | **506 MiB** | 86,357 |
| 24 GB | 1,536 MiB | 384 MiB | 65,536 |
| 16 GB | 1,024 MiB | 256 MiB (as before) | 43,690 |
| 12 GB | 768 MiB | 256 MiB (the floor; as before) | 43,690 |
| 8 GB | 512 MiB | 256 MiB (the floor; as before) | 43,690 |

**Why a sixty-fourth.** The cache's slots are allocated whole at create for every scene whose cached clusters twice over pass the ceiling, and v24's 1.39 million do many times over, so the ceiling is memory such a scene always holds — unlike the chain's budget, which is a ceiling the frames grow to. A sixty-fourth is the smallest power-of-two share that holds v24's wanted set — 46,323 distinct cached clusters over the marker-3 walk at 1080p, 53,000 to 55,000 references a frame at the owner's 3840×2160 — with room on the card it runs on: 86,357 slots on the 5090, where a hundred-and-twenty-eighth (253 MiB) is under the old ceiling. Beside the chain's sixteenth the two take at most five sixty-fourths of the card. On the owner's v24 run at 3840×2160 the process held 14,013 MiB of the 5090's 32,404: the chain 2.94 GB of it (the static forms' 0.89 GB within it), the deformed-vertex pool 0.81 GB, the textures 3.59 GB and the old cache 0.29 GB; the cache's 0.27 GB more leaves the scene's own buffers their room. The floor is the old ceiling, so no card's cache got smaller; past 16 GB the cache grows with the card, and the 1,024 MiB ceiling (174,762 slots) is reached at 64 GB. Where it is too small the frame builds the rest itself (above), so the share decides a cost, never the picture. The log line "cluster structure cache ready" says the ceiling, where it came from and the device-local MiB it was taken from; `GpuScene::rt_cache_ceiling_mib()`/`rt_cache_ceiling_source()` hold them.

**A second set for clusters that hold few triangles: designed, not built** (T138, 2026-11-15). T129 measured the driver's reservation as linear in the triangles a set allows a cluster and independent of its vertices — with micromaps 8,832 bytes a cluster at 124 triangles, 6,912 at 96, 4,736 at 64, 3,712 at 48, 2,560 at 32 ([the measurement](../experiments/memory-commit-accounting.md#the-traced-chains-storage)) — so the frame's chunks, 2.85 GB on the forest's staging, would hold the same structures in about half if the clusters of 48 triangles or fewer were built into chunks created at 48. The rule is the cluster's own triangle count (`geometry::ClusterDesc::triangle_count`), measured from any asset; the load logs the population (`clusters by triangles`, up to 32, 48, 64, 96 and more). **Why it was not landed in one night**: a frame's records are written in instance order because each instance's bottom-level structure references one contiguous run of the addresses the builds write at the record's own index, and a build reads one contiguous run of records. Splitting by size therefore needs (1) the emit pass to write each record at a class position — the small class's region past the large one — while its geometry index stays its dense index, so `hit_entries` and every hit reader are untouched; (2) a gather pass after the builds that copies each built address to the instance's run (`references[dense] = addresses[class position]`), which the bottom-level records then point at instead of the build's array; (3) `clas_chunks.slang` to give each class's chunks their counts from that class's counter; and (4) **the capacity rule made class-aware**: `ranges_main` and the drop scan keep whole instances while *both* classes fit, and `renderer::RtCapacity` keeps two capacities a step above what recent frames built of each. (4) is the part that cannot be approximated: with one capacity the large class must still be able to hold every record, which is the reservation the split exists to remove. The cluster acceleration structure test (pixel-identical against the KHR path) and the ray query test decide it, and a frame pair at 3840 × 2160 rt/rt with the bounce on what it costs (one more dispatch of a thread a record). On a 16 GB card the chain's budget is a sixteenth of the card (1 GB), so the split would hold about twice the clusters in the same budget there rather than give memory back.

## The ray tracing chain's index space

**The frame names compact records** (2026-10-26, R100). `emit_main` writes a dense record index
as the cluster geometry index and a `hit_entries` word mapping that record to the original
visible entry. The ray visibility pass, masked shadow queries and reference path tracer resolve
that word before reading a pair or a deformed pool slot. A static form still names its cluster
within its mesh and bypasses the map. Low-level gfx callers that supply no map retain their
original record bytes. The raster and traced cut therefore still name the same pairs. A
**cached** structure (R101, [the cache](#the-resident-cluster-structure-cache)) names its cluster
within its mesh with bit 23 set and bit 22 for a caster, and bypasses the map too; while a cache
exists the frame's own dense indices stay under bit 23.

Drawn and caster entries are disjoint within each view. A caster has four sources since S86
(2026-11-08): the cone test, a shadowing light's caster volume, the water's **mirrored caster
volume** ([water](water.md#reflections-of-the-scene); R129) — the view's frustum reflected in the
water's plane — and the water's **submerged caster volume** ([water](water.md#what-is-under-the-water))
— what the view refracted at the surface reaches under the water outside its frustum. Each is one
more volume in the same block, so a pair one holds goes to the same run, once, and the partition
stands. Their compact bound is
`views * eligible_pairs - 1`, with no factor for the unused visible-list runs. Eligible pairs
exclude static forms, and untraced instances unless the picture is traced (R110: on the ray path an
untraced instance's drawn entries are built and named). The actual set names `capacity - 1`, bounded by
`DeviceFeatures::cluster_max_geometry_index` (16,777,215 on the RTX 5090); even a reference
frame asking to exceed the memory budget cannot exceed that index bound.

`GpuScene::create` computes the [pair account](#the-pair-accounting) with the terrain capacities
and passes it to `resolve_settings` before allocating. RT reports name the allocated maximum
`geometry_index_max`, the account's eligible admission bound `geometry_index_required`, and the
device's maximum `geometry_index_limit`; `geometry_index_need` remains the old maximum's
deprecated compatibility spelling. Preliminary settings resolution defers
this decision: the file prefix alone cannot decide whether the rings fit. If the eligible bound
exceeds the device, casters go first, traced shadows stay, `Stats::rt.caster_index_fallbacks`
counts the fallback and one `shadow casters off` warning names both numbers. Capacity drops are
counted separately. The placements consumer then withholds tiles against the visibility budget;
only an immutable prefix that cannot fit that budget refuses the scene.

This replaces the old sparse geometry indices, which were the visible entries themselves:
`3 * views * pairs - 1` with casters. The v13 file's 6,578,247 pairs alone asked for 19,734,740
against 16,777,215, disabling casters before the terrain was counted. Static and untraced pairs
and the empty run all inflated that old bound. The CPU index-space case now pins a 1,000-pair
surround at 2,999, its counted caster fallback at 2,998, and continued traced rendering.
## Built textures

The texture upload (`GpuScene::upload_materials`, the only place in the module that knows) takes
a mesh's images one of two ways. **Built**, when the load reads the derived-data cache and every
image the resolve samples — base colour, metallic-roughness, normal, occlusion, emissive — has a
`.tex` in `<ddc>/textures/` whose recorded identity matches: the container's records say where
(`SourceMesh::textures`, section 32 of the `.clusters` file; [geometry](geometry.md#built-textures-where-each-images-texture-is)),
an image the container carries by its recorded key and an image named by path by the file's bytes
as they are now, so a repainted file finds its new texture or none. Those upload as stored, every
level (`gfx::upload_image_2d_levels`), sample through mipmapping, anisotropic samplers ("Materials"
below), and carry `k_material_mipped` — plus `k_material_normal_rg` for a BC5 normal map — so the
resolve samples them with the UV derivatives it computes from the triangle
([texture](texture.md#mip-selection-without-quads)). **Decoded** otherwise, as before: the image
decoded on the CPU, uploaded RGBA8 at one level, level-0 reads, flags zero, through samplers that
read level 0 alone — with the file's wrap and filters since 2026-09-24, where the decoded path used
to clamp, so a decoded texture's picture moved within half a texel of its edges and wherever its
UVs leave [0, 1]. It is **all or nothing per mesh**, so no material mixes the two, and the log says which and why
(`mesh textures`, `from: built|decoded`, `reason`). A device without `textureCompressionBC` gets the
decoded path and a warning naming the feature. `GpuScene::texture_bytes()`, `textures_built()` and
`textures_decoded()` report what happened — distinct textures, since one upload serves every mesh
that samples the same image ([below](#one-upload-per-distinct-image)) — and engine-view prints them
as `"textures":{"built","decoded","distinct","shared","bytes","bytes_saved","sharing","normal_variance",
"normal_variance_bytes"}` (the last two R97's: the normal maps uploaded with a normal-variance chain, and
the chains' bytes, inside `bytes`; [Normal filtering](#normal-filtering-r97)).

**The renderer builds them itself on a cold cache.** A load through the derived-data cache
(`SceneDesc::cache`) runs the content build's texture step (`content_build::run_texture_step`,
the function `engine-content build --cache` runs) once, after every mesh is in, over whatever of
its meshes' textures is missing — beside a container it wrote when it clustered a glTF itself, or
behind a cache hit. A texture already built is trusted from its header and its source is not read
([What the load reads](#what-the-load-reads)); until 2026-10-24 a warm load paid a read and a hash
per image per mesh, and the upload the same again. Until 2026-09-24 only engine-content built textures, so a scene
flown without running it first — every `engine-view --mesh <file.gltf>` on a fresh cache, and every
scene file whose meshes the renderer clustered itself — drew its textures decoded at one level,
with no mips, and shimmered at a distance; the session-diagnosis run on the desert overlook is
where that was seen. The `.tex` it leaves is byte for byte engine-content's (`texture_tests.cpp`,
"a glTF on a cold cache"), because the step, the records and the keys are the same code. A texture
that cannot be built is a warning (`texture not built`) and its mesh draws through the decode.

**A scene may size them by the asset** (G14; [texture](texture.md#sized-by-the-asset)). With a
density stated — a mesh's `Mesh.texel_density`, else `renderer.textures.texel_density`, 0 by
default — the load measures each mesh the scene's instances place from its own level 0
(`cap_scene_textures`, scene.cpp), takes its largest instance's scale and its fit, and asks each
image for the level 0 that density can use (`SourceMesh::texture_caps`). The scene's density caps
only a mesh whose every placement the load knows: not a streamed entry's, a prop's, an actor's or a
procedural mesh, which the tail, a module or `actor_scale` may place larger, and nothing in a scene
with no instances of its own ([texture](texture.md#sized-by-the-asset), "Who states the density");
the texture pass gives
every reference to one texture the largest need of the meshes that share it and builds it with
its top levels left out, under a key of its own. The levels kept are the uncapped texture's, so a
frame that reads them draws the same pixels; a scene that states nothing keeps every key it had.
The load's log counts `capped` references.

The reference path tracer samples the same textures at level 0, as it always sampled everything: it
is a compute pass with no derivatives, and a converged reference is not the place for a filter
footprint. Its BC5 normal maps go through the same z reconstruction as the resolve's.

## One upload per distinct image

**A scene uploads each distinct texture once, however many of its meshes sample it** (since
2026-09-25). `upload_materials` keys every (mesh, image) a material samples by what the texture is
made from, and a key the scene already holds hands back the bindless slot of the texture already
uploaded instead of uploading again:

- **built**, by the `.tex` build key, `texture::texture_cache_key(source hash, options)`: the
  image's encoded bytes and everything the build was told about them — format, colour space, the
  edges its samplers wrap with ([texture](texture.md#the-derived-data-cache-and-the-containers-records)).
  Two images with one key are one file in the derived-data root, so they are one texture.
- **decoded**, by `hash_bytes` over the encoded bytes — embedded, or the file as it is now — and
  the format the image goes up as (sRGB for colour, UNORM for data): the decode is a function of the
  bytes, and the format is the rest of what the device holds.

Each mesh still chooses between the two on its own, all or nothing, so a built texture and a
decoded one never share (they are different images on the device). A key the scene already holds is
not read from the derived-data root again — `find_built_textures` skips the read, since the mesh
that uploaded it checked its identity — and not decoded again: a repeat costs a hash on the decoded
path and nothing on the built one. The entry keeps both halves of its key and is compared whole, so a
64-bit collision between two different images uploads the second again rather than drawing the
wrong one.

**Why the key is the content and not the path.** The duplication this removes is a kit's. E33's
ashlar kit is nineteen GLBs exported one by one, and each embeds the same six images — the block's
and the mortar's base colour, normal and ORM, 16.2 MB of JPEG — so each member uploaded its own
copy of them: 99 textures for 6 images, and one building could hold the atlas nineteen times
([E34](../experiments/e34-ruin-blocks.md), [ruins](ruins.md#the-kit)). An embedded image has no path
at all. Where images are files, a path is both too strict and too loose: two paths name the same
bytes whenever each member's folder carries its own copy, and one name holds different bytes in
every kit that calls its atlas `atlas.png`. The content is the identity the derived-data cache
already addresses a texture by ([ADR-0036](../adr/0036-built-textures-in-the-engines-own-container.md)),
so on the built path the key costs nothing new — the container's record carries it for an embedded
image, and a file is hashed as it is now anyway, which is also why a repainted file finds its new
texture — and on the decoded path it costs a hash over bytes that were about to be decoded.

**What it keeps.** The picture: every material reads the same texels through the same sampler,
from a slot another mesh made. `texture_tests.cpp` holds a kit's picture — ids, depth and colour —
to the byte against every member's own upload, from the decoded images and from the built textures,
and so do the captures below. The bindless set spends one sampled-image slot per distinct image
rather than per member. **Samplers were already shared this way**: one per distinct description
(wrap s, wrap t, filters, mipmapped), scene-wide ([Materials](#materials)).

**Lifetime: the scene's.** The textures are made with the `GpuScene`, owned by it and destroyed
with it, and nothing counts them per instance. A streamed world's tail of instances
([Instances that come and go](#instances-that-come-and-go)) takes its mesh's material base and
nothing else, so a tile's buildings arriving and leaving uploads no texture; the test gives a scene
of one instance the rest as a tail between frames and requires the same two textures, the same bytes
and the same picture, and the E35 world below uploads the kit's six once and none in the 62 tails of
its flight. **Nothing is shared across scenes**: two scenes engine-host holds at once
each upload their own, because a texture's lifetime is its scene's and a host-wide table would
need an owner that outlives every scene and a rule for when an entry dies, neither of which exists.

**What it reports.** `GpuScene::textures_built()` and `textures_decoded()` count distinct textures;
