version of this change — moved the error to the horizon instead: `shredded-atlas`, a torus with
every normal in it, went from 0.0424 to **0.0651** FLIP and `flighthelmet` from 0.0128 to 0.0144.
With two uniform halves the blend is exact, so in open space the two integrators' diffuse ambient is
one number and what is left between them is occlusion, interreflection and the specular lobe's shape.
The upper half keeps the ramp's old top, so a surface facing up draws exactly what it drew before.

**What the comparisons say** (RTX 5090, `msvc-release`, the same day and the same binary but for the
change; the corpus at its files' samples and bounces, the agreement cases at 512 samples and one
bounce, [Reference renderer](#reference-renderer)):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `flighthelmet` FLIP / p95 | 0.0128 / 0.0924 | 0.0132 / 0.0907 |
| `heightfield` | 0.0268 / 0.1249 (direct-only 0.0281) | **0.0235** / 0.1315 (direct-only **0.0209**) |
| `helmet-grid` | 0.0037 | 0.0037 |
| `shredded-atlas` | 0.0424 / 0.1339 | **0.0390** / 0.1138 |
| `thin-geometry` | 0.0036 | 0.0035 |
| `wide-frustum` | 0.0010 | 0.0010 |
| agreement: diffuse plane, sun and two point lights | 0.0131 (44.7 dB) | **0.0051** (55.5 dB) |
| agreement: diffuse plane, sun only | 0.0140 (43.7 dB) | **0.0055** (54.5 dB) |
| agreement: a cube over the plane, shadows traced | 0.0215 (37.7 dB) | **0.0157** (39.5 dB) |
| agreement: the emissive plane | 0.0034 (59.3 dB) | **0.0015** (64.6 dB) |

Every scene agrees with the reference as well or better except `flighthelmet`, 0.0004 worse on the
mean and better on the p95, which is about a third of the reference's own noise floor on that scene at
1024 samples (0.0011, [Reference renderer](#reference-renderer)). The plane cases gain most because an up-facing plane's ambient,
0.35 of the sky in the resolve, was 0.317 in the reference and is now 0.35 in both. The `heightfield`
row's full number is now *above* its direct-only one — the reference's second and third bounces off
the hills are light the real-time path does not have, which is what the two columns are there to
show — where before the ramp's error had been larger than the whole indirect share. The thresholds
were left where they were.

**What it costs**: the ground's radiance is a dozen arithmetic operations per shaded pixel and the
block one float4 row more. Over the owner's dune flight replayed as a benchmark (8,903 frames at
1920×1080, `--shadows csm`, two runs of each binary, alternating, under the GPU lock but not quiet —
other processes 4–15% of the CPU — so upper bounds) the resolve's median went from 0.0713 and
0.0713 ms to 0.0716 and 0.0719, half a percent, and the frame's total did not move (0.1958 and
0.1957 against 0.1946 and 0.1953).

**What it does to the dunes, and what it does not.** The shaded slopes of the owner's markers warm by
two to three levels in red (a foreground slope in the cascades' shadow: 182, 170, 150 → 185, 173,
151), and a genuinely steep face near the horizon by up to nine (109, 112, 106 → 118, 117, 108). The
**grey seams do not move**: 13,093, 7,212 and 6,653 seam pixels at the three markers before and after,
their mean colour 112, 115, 109 before and 113, 115, 109 after, FLIP 0.003–0.007 between the two
pictures. They were never the slip faces in shade. Read against the markers' normals captures, their
shading normals point nearly straight up (n.y 0.97–0.99 on average, none under 0.77) and every one of
them faces the sun (N·L from 0.42 to 0.92, mean 0.73), with shadows on or off; yet every one has the
same colour, the sky ambient of an up-facing normal with nothing else — the signature of `brdf_eval`
returning zero for the sun because **the interpolated shading normal faces away from the camera**
(n·v ≤ 0) while the triangle under it faces towards it, which happens wherever a grazing view
crosses a crest whose smooth vertex normals lean away. The hard, angular edges are where n·v crosses
zero inside a triangle.

## Indirect light: the world-space cache

**The hemisphere above stands for a scene it cannot see** (roadmap R69, stage 1; 2026-11-07): the
ambient of the last two sections is the whole indirect term, and nothing in it knows the scene — a
forest floor under a closed canopy is lit as if under open sky, a trunk's shaded side is flat, a box
with one opening is lit inside as if it had no walls. `renderer.gi.mode` (read at load; `off`, `sky`,
`bounce`) puts a **world-space radiance cache** in front of it, fed by rays against the frame's own
acceleration structures — the traversal the sun's ray already pays — and read per pixel in its
place ([the measurements](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md)). It is the first stage of the
plan's GI ([04 §4.4](../plan/04-renderer.md#44-ray-tracing)): a hash grid in the manner of NVIDIA's
SHaRC (spatially hashed radiance cache) and of Binder et al., "Massively Parallel Path Space
Filtering" (2019), whose cells are found from a point's position and normal alone, so nothing in
it is a screen-space history and nothing swims when the camera turns.

**The key** (`domain/gfx/gi_cache.h`, mirrored by `shaders/gi_cache.slang`) is never a float of the
world (ADR-0053): each axis of the point is `eye.cell * 64,000 + round((eye.local + from_eye) * 1000)`
in 64-bit millimetres — the eye's cell in integers, the rest a float the size of the distance from
the eye — floor-divided by the cell's size. **Sizes** are 25 mm at level 0 doubling to 6.4 m at
level 8, every one a divisor of the 64 m world cell, so a scene moved by whole cells moves every key
by whole cells of its own; **the level** is the smallest whose cell is at least
`renderer.gi.cell_scale` (0.004) times the distance from the view's eye, about ten pixels at
3840×2160 and 90°: 25 mm to 6 m, 10 cm at 20 m, 40 cm at 100 m, 6.4 m past 1.6 km. **The face** of
the normal's dominant axis (±x, ±y, ±z) is in the key, so a wall's two sides, a floor and the wall
standing on it never share a cell; the dominant axis rather than the octant because a floor's
interpolated normals straddle every octant boundary of +y and none of its faces'. The hash's low word
names a bucket of eight slots, its high word (low bit set) the key in the slot; a lookup scans the
bucket whole, so a slot the fold frees breaks no other key's chain. **The keys live apart from the
cells** (stage 2): the buffer is a 64-byte header, then one 4-byte key a slot — a bucket's eight
keys are one 32-byte block a lookup reads in two 16-byte loads — then the cells; stage 1 kept the
key in each cell's first word, which spread a bucket over 256 bytes and made a lookup eight
dependent scattered loads.

**A cell** (32 bytes) holds its measured spread and its bucket's pressure in one word (R171: the
spread a half in the low 16 bits; the pressure, the first cell of a bucket only, the last frame an
insert found the bucket full, in the high 16), the frame's sample count and fixed-point sums (10 bits of fraction), the
running mean as three halves and the samples it averages, and the stamp of the last frame that
reached it. What it averages is **a ratio to the sky's harmonics**: each sample is the radiance one
ray brought back over the luminance of the nine-harmonic ambient at the sample's normal, and the
resolve reads `ratio × luminance(harmonics)` at its own normal. The ratio keeps the colour of what
the surface actually sees — a gap towards the horizon brings the horizon's colour, not the zenith's
— and the harmonics carry the hour, so a sky that changes reaches every cached cell in the same
frame; in open space the ratio is the harmonics' own chromaticity and the read is the harmonics. A
scalar visibility times the harmonics was the alternative and would colour a shaded surface with
the part of the sky it cannot see.

**The frame's two passes** (`gi_update.slang`, between the half-rate sun pass and the resolve, both
reading each view's own `ResolveParams`):
- **`gi sample`** (`FrameRecord.gpu_ms.gi_trace`): one pixel in every `gi_stride` of every view's
  visibility region, at an offset that turns with the cache's own frame count, so a frame traces at
  most `renderer.gi.rays_per_frame` (two million; 1.66 million at 3840×2160, stride 5). The pixel is
  decoded and reconstructed as the resolve does it, its cell found at its level **and the next
  coarser one** (inserting them), and **one cosine-weighted ray** traced from it — the shadow rays'
  own query (`shadow_ray_blocked`, the same masks, micromaps, opaque proxy and caster bit, offset by
  the same `ray_offset`). A ray that escapes carries `sky_environment` along its direction — the
  sky-view table above the horizon, so the air's Rayleigh blue reaches the shade through the cache,
  and the ground the sky's frame lights below it, which is what the reference tracer's escaped rays
  carry — and one that hits carries nothing (stage 1a: the sky's visibility). The ratio is added in
  integers to both cells' sums. **One pass touches and traces** because a trace pass over a list of
  the frame's touched cells would trace from whichever pixel won each cell's slot in the list — the
  order threads reach an atomic — and the picture would depend on it; integer sums of every sampled
  pixel's ray are the same in any order, and `gi cache: a scene moved by whole cells draws the same
  bytes with the cache on` holds the result to the byte.
- **`gi fold`** (`gpu_ms.gi_fold`): a thread a cell folds the frame's sums into the mean with an
  exponential average whose rate is the frame's samples over the history's (`n / min(N + n, 256)`),
  so a new cell takes its first frame whole and an old one moves a frame's share; a cell nothing
  reached for 240 frames is freed. The cache's first frame clears the buffer with one more fold
  first (`gfx::k_gi_step_reset`) and then pre-rolls ([stage 5](#stage-5-the-light-is-already-there));
  until stage 5 that frame's sample pass added nothing and it drew the harmonics.

**The read** (`scene_ambient` in `material.slang`, one call in the resolve): trilinear over the eight
cells of the point's level round it on the point's face, each weighted by its share of the point and
by its samples, and the coarser levels for whatever share the samples behind that do not earn (the
walk up the ladder, [stage 5](#stage-5-the-light-is-already-there); stages 1 and 2 read the next
level only where the first had nothing, then by a confidence), and the harmonics, **to the bit**,
where no level has a sample or where the frame does not read the cache. The material's ambient occlusion still multiplies it, as it multiplies the
harmonics: it stands for occlusion below a cell's size. Only the opaque path's ambient reads it; the
water's own ambient is the harmonics still.

**The buffer** is `renderer.gi.cache_mib` (128 MiB since stage 4: four million cells and their keys,
144 MiB made; it was 32 MiB, a million cells, which v37's held view — 384,000 to 414,000 cells —
filled unevenly enough to turn 2,600 inserts a frame away, and many more on a turn, below), made once at load and never by a frame (`gi cache: the frames with the cache on
make no buffer and allocate as the mode off`). The mode is `off` without traced shadows, whose query
the sample pass is. `ResolveParams` grew two rows, 496 to 528 bytes (544 with S97's wet-band row after them).

**What it buys, judged by the reference tracer** at one bounce — direct light plus the environment
through the scene's real visibility, which is what stage 1a estimates — at 128×128 after 64 frames
(RTX 5090; [the page](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md) has the method):

| fixture | FLIP, `off` | FLIP, `sky` | PSNR, `off` | PSNR, `sky` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a closed 4 m box with a 1.6 m opening and a sphere inside | 0.626 | 0.089 | 10.6 | 26.8 |
| a field of 28 cubes on a slab | 0.093 | 0.056 | 30.0 | 33.6 |

`gi cache: the cache moves the picture towards the reference path tracer` holds the order. At one
pose the change from frame to frame falls from 71,000 colour steps over the first frames to 21,700
by frame 20 and 11,600 by frame 40 (`... falls and does not grow back`): the noise left is the
average's, 1/√256 of a sample's.

**Stage 1b: the bounce** (`renderer.gi.mode=bounce`, `k_gi_bounce`). `sky` alone knows where the
scene is but not that it is lit: a ray that meets real ground brings back nothing where the
harmonics' lower half assumed the sunlit ground, so on an open field `sky` is *further* from the
real light than the harmonics. With the bounce, the sample's ray finds the **nearest** surface (the
shadow rays' masks, proxy and micromaps decided as they decide them, kept nearest rather than
first), decodes it as the reference tracer decodes a hit — `hit_visible_entry`, `hit_pair`,
`fetch_triangle`, `material_of`, the base colour at level 0 — and brings back its light towards the
ray: its emission, the sun through `brdf_direct` under one shadow ray from the hit, and its albedo
times **the cache at the hit's own cell**, which carries the bounces before it, so the cache
converges to more than one bounce. Where the hit's cells are empty the ambient there is **nothing**,
not the harmonics: only the picture's pixels sample, so a surface out of every view has no cells,
and taking the open sky there lit the inside of the box as if it had no walls (FLIP 0.44 against
0.13). It errs dark instead, by the bounces past the second off surfaces nobody sees. Against the
reference at **three** bounces — the light as it is, the sun off the floor onto the walls and back —
after 64 frames:

| fixture | FLIP, `off` | `sky` | `bounce` | PSNR, `off` | `sky` | `bounce` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the box with one opening | 0.573 | 0.200 | **0.125** | 11.9 | 22.1 | 27.1 |
| the field of cubes | 0.065 | 0.109 | **0.048** | 33.0 | 26.9 | 35.5 |

(`gi cache: the bounce moves the picture towards the reference at three bounces` holds `bounce`
below both.) A hit's albedo is the material's base colour and texture at level 0, not a terrain's
layers or the ground's detail; a hit costs a nearest-hit traversal, a material fetch and a shadow
ray where a `sky` sample costs a first-hit one. Stage 2 is ReSTIR GI over the cache (R68).

**Stage 2: the fill, the blocks, the brightness, the read** (R69 stage 2, 2026-11-08; [the
measurements](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-2-the-fill-the-blocks-the-brightness-the-read)).
The owner walked v35 under `bounce` and saw the light load in "like a checkerboard" over five to ten
seconds, a little dark, with blocks on the rocks. Each change below is a knob whose stage-1 value
reproduces the stage-1 read, so every lever was judged on its own against the reference
(`gi cache: stage 2's levers one at a time, ...`):
- **The young cell reads its parent** (`renderer.gi.confident`, 32; **replaced by stage 5's walk**,
  which takes a level by the samples behind its mean, reads four levels and is read whole at 128;
  what follows is stage 2's rule as it stood). A level's read sums its eight
  cells as before and also their confidence, the trilinear weights times `min(samples / 32, 1)`;
  the read takes that share from the point's own level and the rest from the next coarser one,
  which every sample also reached and which holds four to eight times the samples
  (`gi_read_face`; `gfx::gi_blend_levels` is the same arithmetic on the CPU, held against a
  brute-force blend). A new cell starts from its parent's mean and sharpens as its own samples
  come, instead of taking its first frame's few rays whole; a converged neighbourhood reads one
  level, so the second level's eight lookups are paid only while something is young. The fold's
  rate is unchanged and stated: `n / min(N + n, 256)` is the plain mean of every sample for a
  cell's first 256, then an exponential average of that length.
- **A full bucket frees its stale cells** (`renderer.gi.evict_age`, 16 frames). A walk fills the
  cache with what it passed; a bucket of eight slots that is full turned every new key away until
  one of its cells aged out at 240 frames. An insert that finds its bucket full now stamps the
  bucket (its first cell's first word), and the fold frees any cell of a stamped bucket that no
  sample has reached for 16 frames — a cell in view is sampled every few frames, so only what the
  walk left behind goes.
- **The rays go where the cells are young** (`renderer.gi.young_rays`). The sample pass's stride is
  now half the budget's (`gfx::gi_trickle_stride`: one pixel in nine at 3840×2160): that pixel is
  the trickle every cell keeps. Each thread also looks at a second pixel half a window on and takes
  a ray for it only where its own cell is young (under `k_gi_young`, 8 samples, or no cell), out of
  the other half of the budget, claimed one atomic a wave (`k_gi_ray_count` in the header), so
  together they never pass `renderer.gi.rays_per_frame`. A converged view spends half stage 1's
  rays; a newly seen region gets stage 1's density until it has filled. Which young pixels get rays
  when their half runs out is the order waves reach the count; below it the picture does not
  depend on order (the translation test still holds the bytes).
- **A bounce's hit reads coarser, then a bounded fallback** (`renderer.gi.hit_fallback`). Every
  sample reached three levels and a hit read four from its own (four and four since stage 5,
  `k_gi_ladder`), so a wall behind the eye finds the light of a coarse cell some pixel in view
  reached. Where none has samples it takes the harmonics times the ray's openness
  (`gfx::gi_openness`: nothing for a hit within a metre of the ray's origin, which is enclosed, all
  of it past ten metres, smooth between) — never the raw harmonics, which lit the box's inside as
  open sky.
- **The faces blend** (`renderer.gi.face_blend`). Where the normal's second-largest component is at
  least 0.6 of its largest (31° from the axis, the boundary at 45°), the read takes the next face's
  cells too, weighted from nothing to a half at the boundary (`gfx::gi_face_blend`), so a rounded
  rock or a trunk does not step where its normal's dominant axis changes. It costs a second face's
  lookups in that band only.
- **The far lift** (`renderer.gi.far_lift`, 0: off). A stated lever for the distant crowns: a cell of
  level 6 and up (1.6 m, past 400 m) read towards the harmonics by the lever times a third a level
  past the fifth. It stays off: see the experiment page.
- **What the passes counted** (`Stats::gi`, `gfx::k_gi_stat_*`): the header's first eight words —
  rays, stride samples and those whose own cell was young, inserts a full bucket turned away, cells
  held and young after the fold, cells freed for a full bucket and for their age — are copied into
  the frame's statistics block behind the fold (the `gi stats` transfer pass) and the header is
  cleared for the next frame; `renderer.gi.log` writes them as one log line a frame
  (`--log info`: a record must pass the global level and its category's both, so
  `--log warn,renderer=info` prints nothing at info, which stage 4 found), which is how a walk's
  fill is read.
**What it costs, and why it is off.** On the owner's v25 walk at 3840×2160 (`msvc-release`, median
of 301 frames, a shared machine; [the page](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#the-v25-walk-at-38402160-what-it-costs-and-what-it-looks-like)):
the sample pass is 1.62 ms under `sky` and 3.88 under `bounce`, the fold 0.01, and **the read adds
2.8–2.9 ms to the resolve** (5.05 to 7.8–7.95) — sixteen scattered bucket scans a pixel. The frame
goes 17.8 → 22.4 (`sky`) → 24.7 ms (`bounce`). The picture under `bounce` has the shaded crowns,
trunks and understory the harmonics could not give, and blocks a cell wide on rounded rocks, whose
normals the face key splits. `renderer.gi.mode` stays `off` until the read is cheaper and the blocks
are gone; `bounce` is the mode to turn on.

### Stage 4: the light round the eye

The owner's v37 walk under `bounce` (2026-11-09): a turn still showed the indirect light filling
in, about a second of it, "instead of having the indirect lighting already applied when turning".
Every shipped real-time GI keeps its bounced light in a store that exists in **every direction
round the player**, so that where the view looks is not an input to what is lit — DDGI's probe
volume traces every probe every frame against structures holding the whole neighbourhood, Lumen's
surface cache and world-space radiance cache cover the region round the camera and are traced
against a scene representation that does not depend on the frustum (the sources and what each keeps
warm are on [the experiment page](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-4-the-light-round-the-eye)).
This cache's key was already independent of the view; its **coverage** was not, for two reasons:

- **A cell existed only where some view's pixel had sampled it.** Nothing behind the eye was ever
  sampled, so the cells a turn reads were the ones its own frames and the young-cell rays filled
  on the way round.
- **There was nothing behind the eye for a ray to find.** The frame's structures hold the
  frustum's cut and the casters its light and its water ask for. A trunk three metres behind the
  eye and outside the sun's sweep is in none of them, so a cache ray that leaves the frustum
  sideways or backwards meets nothing where the forest stands and brings back sky.

Stage 4 keeps the cache as it was (the key, the levels, the fold, the read, stage 2's levers) and
adds two knobs whose 0 is the frame as it was:

- **The volume round the eye** (`renderer.gi.shell_m`, `eye_shell.h`): one more caster volume in
  the view's cull block, the cube of six planes round the sphere of that radius with the sphere as
  the volume's `reach`, so the cull pass's existing test is the sphere test and no shader learns a
  new kind of volume (`cluster_cull.slang` and `cluster_cull.h` are unchanged; the block's five
  volumes hold the sun's, the water's two and this one). Its pairs are casters like the others —
  the camera's cut, built non-opaque, so primary rays pass through them and the cache's and the
  shadow rays stop on them — fitted **behind every other volume**, so a block the lights and the
  water fill leaves the cache what the frame's cut holds, since a missing shadow is worse than a
  slower fill. In the chain's capacity its casters are casters of their rank, dropped by the
  existing rule (a rank's casters before its drawn clusters, the farthest rank first); they are not
  a separate class below the lights' and the water's casters, which would need a third kind in the
  records' scan. It is fitted wherever the cache is made, in every resolve mode, which is how
  `gi cache: the volume round the eye changes no shadow, id or depth` holds the direct picture: a
  caster outside the sun's sweep can shadow no receiver in view.
- **The samples round the eye** (`renderer.gi.shell_rays`, `ResolveParams::gi_shell_rays`): the
  sample pass's threads past a view's trickle windows, from the next whole workgroup, trace that
  many directions a frame from the view's eye over the whole sphere — a stratified equal-area grid
  (`gfx::gi_shell_columns`) jittered by a hash of the cache's frame count, never of a position, so
  the translation test holds — skipping the directions the view's frustum covers. Each finds the
  nearest surface with the shadow rays' masks (`trace_scene_hit`, `hit_shade.slang`), decodes it
  as a pixel is decoded (`surface_at` towards the eye, so its cells' faces are the ones the view
  reads after it turns that way), and is then sampled **exactly as a stride pixel is**
  (`gi_trace_and_add`): the cells at the level its distance gives and the two coarser inserted, one
  cosine ray, the bounce. Two rays a direction come out of the young half of the budget, of which
  every view's shell takes at most half (`gfx::gi_shell_ray_cost`), so the young cells in view keep
  the rest; without `renderer.gi.young_rays` there is no young half and no shell sample.
  `Stats::gi` counts the directions traced, those that met a surface and those that met one within
  50 m (`k_gi_stat_shell*`), which is how much of the sphere the frame's structures hold.

**The rate's arithmetic.** At the default `cell_scale` a cell at distance d is between 0.004 d and
0.008 d wide, 1.6 × 10⁻⁵ to 6.4 × 10⁻⁵ steradians seen face-on, so a sphere whose every direction met
a surface would hold 200,000 to 785,000 cells at their own level, a quarter of that at the next and
a sixteenth at the one past it; the view's frustum (55° by 86° at 16:9) is a tenth of the sphere,
and the sky is not sampled at all. A cell is read whole at 32 samples (`renderer.gi.confident`) and
younger cells lean on their parent, so warming the sphere means about 32 samples for every parent
cell: 50,000 to 200,000 of them, 1.6 to 6.3 million samples. The measured setting, 65,536 a frame,
is 3.5 million samples a second outside the frustum at 60 frames a second — the parents' level warm
in about one to two seconds of a still eye, the grandparents' in a fraction of a second, the own
level at 5 to 20 samples a second.

**The stats fold.** `SceneRenderer::collect_slot` — the pipelined frames' collect, which every
engine-view flight uses — now folds the cache's counts as `render_offscreen`'s did; until stage 4
only the blocking path filled `Stats::gi`, so `renderer.gi.log` printed nothing on a camera path,
which stages 2 and 3 both met.

**What it measured, and why both knobs are off** ([the page](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-4-the-light-round-the-eye)
has the curves and the costs). On v37's `south-lake` turn (180° over 30 frames at 1920×1080) the
samples took four fifths of the turn's bias away (the first frame's mean error in the term −0.094 →
−0.018 of a luma step) but not its distance from the held frame (1.68 → 1.76, against 0.43 for a
control held at that pose with no turn): what is left is the variance of cells holding a few
samples, which 65,536 directions a frame do not out-sample the young cells' rays on a 30-frame
turn; the walk and the flight were a
little worse, the samples' rays coming out of the young half the cells newly in view need. Of the
directions outside the frustum, 2,968 met a surface within 50 m in main's structures and 25,366
with the 48 m volume, which added only 4,200 casters to the 388,000 the frame keeps. On a flick (the
same turn in 6 frames) main's first frame stood 3.31 from converged, the larger cache alone (below)
1.77 and the samples with it 1.74: the size did it. In the box seen from inside, turned in four frames,
the first frame after the turn stood 0.018 of the term from its converged picture with both, 0.071
under main; the box's converged picture moved towards the reference (FLIP 0.105 → 0.092). At
3840×2160 the two cost 0.8 ms a frame at 48 m. The brief's rule was on under `bounce` where they
met its target on the forest; they did not, so `renderer.gi.shell_m` and `renderer.gi.shell_rays`
default to 0, and `48` and `65536` are the measured setting. Their counts said why: with them the
cache held 943,000 to 970,000 of its million cells, turned 13,000 inserts a frame away held and
246,000 on the turn — the sphere round the eye is a million cells more than the view's — and at
four million cells it held 1.55 million, 849,000 of them young: 65,536 directions a frame are about
a tenth of what would warm the sphere's own level, as the arithmetic above says.

**What did move the turn: the cache's size.** The same counts on main's frame show a million cells
too few for v37 at all (2,600 inserts a frame turned away on a held view). At 128 MiB the turn's
first frame stands **1.30** from its converged picture against **1.68** at 32 MiB (the no-turn floor
0.43), with no insert turned away, so `renderer.gi.cache_mib` defaults to 128: 108 MiB more device
memory where the cache is on, and a fold over four times the cells (stage 2 measured 0.01 ms for a
million; four million was not timed).

### Stage 5: the light is already there

The owner, a third time (v40, 2026-11-10): "it's down to about 1 second to fill, but **the problem
is the filling being visible at all** ... maybe it needs to be baked into the scene somehow?" The
target is therefore not a rate: **a viewer sees no change in the indirect light that the world did
not cause**, on a turn of any speed, on a walk, in flight, and in the first frame after a load or a
cut. ([The measurements](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-5-the-light-is-already-there),
with the curves against a long-held reference and the answer about baking.)

**What the eye was catching.** Stage 4 found the turn's error to be variance, not bias, and that is
the whole of it: a cell's estimate *arriving*. A sample is one cosine-weighted ray, and under
`bounce` its value spreads about as widely as its mean (a sunlit patch of ground or the dark
underside of a crown), so the mean of n samples carries a sample's spread over √n. Stage 2 read a
cell whole at 32 samples (a sixth of a sample's spread of noise, four times what a converged cell
keeps) and handed whatever weight was left to the next level **whole, whatever it held** — on the
first frame a surface is seen that level holds 44 samples. The picture then settles to an
exponential average of 256, a spread over √511: the eye watches the noise fall by four over a
second, a cell at a time, and reads it as light loading. Stage 4's samples round the eye could not
help: they filled cells behind the eye to five or twenty samples, which the same read then showed.

**The ladder** (`gfx::k_gi_ladder`, `gi_cache.h` and `gi_cache.slang`). Every sample is added to
its surface's own level and the **three coarser**, and every read walks the same four, finest
first. A surface's cells are a quarter as many a level up, so a cell l levels up takes about 4^l
times the own cell's samples. At 3840×2160 the trickle samples one pixel in nine and a cell is
about ten pixels wide, so in the **one frame** a surface is first seen:

| level | cell at 20 m | samples in the first frame | frames to 255 |
|---|---|---|---|
| own | 10 cm, ~10 px | 11 | 23 |
| +1 | 20 cm | 44 | 6 |
| +2 | 40 cm | 178 | 2 |
| +3 | 80 cm | 711 | 1 |

There is always a level that is quiet on the first frame; stage 2 added to three levels and read
two, so the level with 178 samples existed and was not read. The four are consecutive on purpose:
a surface that crosses to a finer level as the eye comes nearer finds the cells that were its own
and its parents' a frame before, converged, under its new empty ones.

**The walk** (`gi_read_level`, `gi_read_face`; `gfx::gi_blend_levels` is the same arithmetic on the
CPU, held against a brute force from the cells). One level's read sums, over the eight cells round
the point, each cell's share s = trilinear weight × min(n / 255, 1): Σ s·mean, Σ s, Σ s² and
Σ s²/n. The level's mean is the first over the second, and Σ s² / Σ s²/n is **the samples a cell
of that mean holds** — the cells' counts averaged as the mean's variance weighs them: a cell's own
count at its centre, eleven between eight cells of eleven. The level takes that count over 255
(`renderer.gi.confident`, 32 before; the history's own length) of what the finer levels left, at
most all, and passes the rest up; the walk stops when a thirty-second or less is left. Three
things follow:

- **No level adds more noise than a mean of 255 samples carries.** With m samples a cell a level
  takes m/255 and adds at most a sample's spread times √m/255 (less where several cells share the
  point: the variance of its mean is Σ s²/n over (Σ s)², Kish's effective sample size inverted),
  at most 1/√255 — **√(511/255) = 1.42 times a converged cell's noise** for the whole read,
  whatever its cells hold (`gi cache key: no cell's next sample steps the read` computes it over
  random neighbourhoods). And one more sample moves a filling cell's share of the read by 1/255,
  which is what it moves a converged cell's mean by (1/256): **frame to frame, a cell that is
  filling changes as one that has filled.** That is why the count is the history's length and not
  less, and why it is a cell's count and not the pooled count of the eight: the first build read
  a level whole at 128 samples behind its mean, pooled, so a point between eight cells took a
  third of its own level in one frame, and the box's turn stood at exactly the twice its
  arithmetic gives and changed between frames at up to four times the steady rate.- **Nothing steps.** Every sum is continuous in every cell's count, so neither a cell's first
  sample nor a level's hand-over is an event, and each level is trilinear, so the read is
  continuous across cells. A corner the surface never passes through (the layer above a floor) has
  no cell and counts for nothing, where stage 2's confidence counted it as unknown and sent up to
  half of every floor's read to the parent for good — so stage 2 read two levels at most pixels,
  and this read one where the neighbourhood has converged: eight lookups. (That did not make the
  read cheaper on the forest, as it was expected to: the crowns' leaf-sized cells never hold 255
  samples, so their walk reads two to four levels for good, and the resolve is 0.6 to 1.6 ms
  dearer at 3840×2160; the page has the pair.) One guard: where the cells that are there hold under an eighth of the
  weight between them (a point's own cell holds that alone) the level is taken by that much less,
  or a mean extrapolated from one far corner would be taken whole until the point's own cell
  appeared.
- **What is shown first is coarser, not noisier — and on the forest that is seen.** A surface
  first seen is lit from the 40 and 80 cm cells and sharpens to its own over twenty-three frames,
  a 255th of the read a sample. In the box the change is under the cache's steady floor. On the
  v40 forest's turn it is not: a far crown's coarse cells (3 to 6 m) average the canopy's lit
  outside with its darker inside, the light's detail in a forest being mostly occlusion, so the
  far forest stands in the turn's first frame as **one band a little brighter than it will be**
  (+0.58 of a luma step over the picture) and darkens over twenty frames, where main showed
  speckle of the same mean size. The speckle is gone and the band is new; the count a level is
  read whole at is what sets how long it lasts, it was set on the box, and the page has the
  forest's numbers at the other counts.
**A cell remembers 256 samples or sixteen frames of them, the longer** (`gfx::gi_history`,
`k_gi_history_frames`). The fold's average was capped at 256 samples, and a cell that took more
than that in one frame kept none of its past: its mean was a fresh draw every frame. That is every
coarse level of the ladder (178 and 711 a frame above), which is what a filling surface, a crown
whose leaf-sized own cells never fill, and a bounce's hit read — quiet each frame, and flickering
at sixty a second. Sixteen frames is a little under what an own cell's 256 samples are at eleven a
frame, so no level remembers less time than the finest.

Where all four levels together hold under a sixteenth of confidence (a twig's worth of pixels on
its first frames) the read leans on the harmonics in proportion (`k_gi_read_floor`,
`gi_confidence_weight`); with no cell at all it is the harmonics to the bit, as before. A bounce's
hit walks the same ladder and leans on its bounded fallback the same way, so a hit's light does
not step when its first cell appears either. Between **levels** the read still steps where a
surface's distance crosses a power of two (one pixel reads level l, its neighbour l+1): the two
are each converged and differ by the light's detail between 10 and 20 cm cells, which nobody has
reported and the page's captures do not show; blending the two levels by the distance's fraction
would make it continuous and double the read, so it is not built.

**Warm round the eye** (stage 4's volume and samples, on by default now: `renderer.gi.shell_m`
48, `renderer.gi.shell_rays` 65,536). The ladder alone removes the *noise* of a fill and not the
fill: in the box, turned with nothing round the eye, the first frame stood twenty floors from the
turned pose's long-held picture with the ladder as without it — the turned view's bounce meets
hits behind the eye and in the half never seen that have no cells, so its first samples carry
the fallback and the answer iterates in view (the bias stage 4 measured). And 240 frames after the
turn the cells the first view had filled aged out and **the light moved again, four seconds after
anything happened** — on main too, which no stage had seen because no stage held a turn that
long. The volume and the samples keep the sphere's cells sampled, so both go: the turn's first
frame starts from the light that was there, and nothing behind the eye ages out while the eye
stands. Stage 4 built them and they did nothing measurable, because the read showed their five to
twenty samples a cell whole; with the ladder, their samples are added to the three levels
**above** the surface's own (the own level took a million cells of the cache for nothing a read
would take).The arithmetic, at the default `cell_scale`: a cell at
distance d is 0.004 d to 0.008 d wide, so a sphere whose every direction met a surface holds
196,000 to 785,000 cells at their own level whatever its radius, and a quarter as many a level up.
Of 65,536 directions a frame the frustum's tenth is skipped and, on the forest, about half of the
rest meet a surface (the sky and the far lake are not cells): 30,000 to 59,000 samples a frame.

| level | cells on the sphere | samples a cell a frame | frames to 255 |
|---|---|---|---|
| +3 | 3,100 – 12,300 | 2.4 – 19 | 13 – 106 |
| +2 | 12,300 – 49,000 | 0.6 – 4.8 | 53 – 420 |
| +1 | 49,000 – 196,000 | 0.15 – 1.2 | 210 – 1,700 |

So after a second or two of a still eye the coarsest level is quiet over the whole sphere, the
next within seven, and they stay so (a cell is kept while a sample reaches it every 240 frames). A
turn's first frame then adds its own 44, 178 and 711 to them. Their cost is stated on the page so
they can be judged alone.

**The start, and a cut** (`gi_preroll.h`, `renderer.gi.preroll` 32, `renderer.gi.cut_m` 8). A load
is the one place the cache has nothing, and the first picture was the sky's harmonics with the
light arriving over the next second; fast travel is the same start somewhere else. A frame that
starts cold — the cache's first, or one whose eye is more than eight metres from the frame
before's — records the sample pass and the fold **thirty-two times more** before its resolve
reads, against the frame's own visibility buffer and structures. Each step is a frame of the
cache's clock (`gfx::GiStepPush`: the pixel offsets, the directions and the seeds turn), so
thirty-two are thirty-two frames' samples at one pose: the trickle has reached every pixel three
times, an own cell holds about 350 samples, the sphere has had two million directions, and a
bounce's hits have read cells that already held thirty-one rounds of the bounce before them
(sixteen left the box's first frame 2.3 floors from its long-held picture, the bounce's later
rounds still arriving). The first frame is then inside the same bound as any other (`gi cache:
the pre-roll runs on the first frame and on a cut, and neither shows a fill`). The fold counts
only on the frame's last step and the young claims are a step's, so a frame's counts are the
frame's; `Stats::gi_preroll_steps` says which frames pre-rolled. A turn is not a cut and never
pre-rolls.
**The bounce off the ground** takes the ground's own material: the cache's passes have a terrain
module (`gi_update_terrain.slang`, picked as the resolve picks its own) in which a hit on a
terrain root reads the masks' layers there through R129's `terrain_hit_material`, at a footprint
of a twentieth of the ray's length. Until then it read the root's base colour, the record's first
layer, and a tan bank bounced its meadow's green (`gi cache: a bounce off a bank of sand under the
masks is sand's, not the first layer's`, in `systems/water`'s tests beside R129's bank).

**On baking** (the owner's question; the page has the numbers). What a bake buys is light on the
first frame, and the pre-roll buys that at the load for the milliseconds in the table below, for
exactly the cells the view reads, at the sun the frame has. A bake kept per tile would have to
hold every level a tile can be seen at (the level follows the eye's distance) for every sun
position, or only the coarse levels — which are the ones a frame warms in one step. What it would
still add is nothing a viewer has been shown to see; it is not built.

**What it costs, and where it stands** ([the page](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-5-the-light-is-already-there)
has the pair and the curves). At 3840×2160 with traced primaries and shadows the stage costs
**1.4 ms a frame on the lake view and 2.4 on the forest view**: 0.6 to 1.6 of read, 0.5 to 0.6 of
the samples round the eye, 0.2 of their volume. In the box a turn, a cut and (from the
twenty-fourth frame) a load stand inside twice the cache's steady floor, where the plain read
stands eighteen floors off; on the forest the turn's variance is gone from the ground and the
near trees and its change between frames is a third less, the flight's dark start is gone, and
the far forest's bright first frames are new. **The owner's target is not met on the forest**,
and the stage is `in progress` on the roadmap: the count a level is read whole at, the read's
cost on crowns, and a measurement that holds the clouds still are what is next.

### Stage 6: what a difference between two levels shows

Roadmap R69 stage 6 (2026-11-11, batch 60; [the page](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-6-what-the-band-is-and-what-a-difference-between-two-levels-shows)
has the count, the curves and the costs). Stage 5 was held for the band it showed after a turn:
the far forest brighter than it will be, darkening over about twenty frames.

**What the band is.** Stage 5 read it as the coarse levels holding more light than the fine
ones. Counted (`renderer.gi.show_level`: the resolve's read takes one level of the ladder whole,
the cache filled as ever; the diagnostic stays), they do not: every sample is added to all four
levels, and over the pixels that read them the levels' means agree in linear light within a
tenth of a percent. What a coarse level holds is that light **flattened**. A crown's cell three
levels up is the mean of its leaves in the open and its leaves in the shade, so it shows the
shade 1.6 times as bright as it is and the lit leaves a little darker; and the display's curve
turns a flattening into a brightening, because a dark pixel lifted by some light rises by many
more steps than a bright one lowered by the same light falls. The band's sign is the same
everywhere for that reason, and it is in the still picture too wherever a crown's own cells
never fill. So nothing that corrects a coarse cell's *mean* touches it (a ratio of sums, cells
weighted by their samples, the young rays kept out of the coarse levels: each measured, each
nothing), and the count a level is read whole at only trades it for the noise of fewer samples.

**The reveal** (`gi_reveal` in `gi_cache.h` and `gi_cache.slang`, `gfx::k_gi_reveal`,
`renderer.gi.reveal`, on). The count's rule — a level takes its samples over 255 of the read —
is the rule of a surface with no detail between the levels: there the coarser mean is as good
and quieter, and waiting costs nothing. Where the levels differ the difference is the picture,
and waiting for 255 samples to show it is the band. So a level its count does not read whole is
compared with the next one up before its share is settled. With means m and m′ (in luminance)
over n and n′ samples, and a sample's variance taken as s² = `k_gi_sample_cv2` · max(m, m′)²,

    d² = max((m − m′)² − s² (1/n + 1/n′), 0)        the detail the noise does not explain
    shown = d² / (d² + s²/n)                         the share the difference gives the level

and the level takes the larger of its count's share and `shown`. That is the shrinkage weight of
a noisy mean towards a prior whose spread is known, with the spread estimated from the data by
its positive part (James and Stein, 1961; the page cites it): the read was already called a
shrinkage estimate in stage 5, and this is the term it left out, the prior's spread, which the
count's rule takes as zero. What follows from the form, and is held by
`gi cache key: a level is taken early by what its difference shows, and only by that`:

- where the levels agree within their noise `shown` is zero and the read is stage 5's to the
  bit (ground, walls, anything a coarse cell describes as well as a fine one);
- where it is not zero the noise the level adds to the read, `shown · s/√n`, is less than the
  difference it shows — a level is never taken early on the strength of its own noise;
- it is continuous in both means and both counts, and zero at one sample, so a cell's first
  sample is still no step;
- `shown` is cut by the trilinear weight of the cells that are there where they hold under an
  eighth of it (`GiLevelRead::weight`), so a far corner's mean is not shown as the point's;
- it reads no level the count's walk did not: a level waits only if the count's walk would have
  gone on to the next one anyway.

`k_gi_sample_cv2` is 2, from a model and not a fit: a cosine ray from a half-hidden leaf escapes
to the sky, or meets a leaf in the shade, or one in the sun, and that mixture's variance is one
to two times its mean's square. A bounce's hit walks the same ladder with the same rule.

**What it does, and what it does not.** On a stand of trees turned to from looking away (the
grove, past the volume round the eye) the first frame's band falls from +0.29 of an 8-bit step
over the crowns to +0.18, inside the still picture's floor (0.27), with the frames' change at
0.097 against 0.091 (the floor's 0.070), at 0.03 ms of resolve over stage 5 at 3840×2160 traced.
**It is a third of the band.** Two neighbouring levels of a crown differ by little (each octave
flattens a little), and in a crown's first frames its cells hold few samples — a cell is keyed by
which of six ways its surface faces, and a crown's leaves face all six at every depth, so its
samples are divided among a dozen cells where ground's are in one — so a small difference is
inside the noise and the count still decides. Main, which reads a cell whole at 32 samples and
looks one level up, stands nearer on those crowns (and shows the speckle stage 5 removed
elsewhere). What takes the rest is the key, not the read: foliage filled and read without the
face at the levels above its own, which would also halve the read's cost on crowns (the second
face is 0.55 of its 1.4 ms there); it is on the roadmap row and not built.

**On the forest** (v41, 3840×2160 traced, the owner's wind) the band is inside what the wind
does to the picture for main and stage 6 alike (+0.19 and +0.23 of a step against a floor of
11.5), no still of the turn shows a fill in either, and two things stand that the grove did not
show: stages 5 and 6 cost about **1.4 ms a frame over main** on the lake view (0.5 the samples
round the eye, 0.46 the read, 0.23 their volume: stage 6 took none of stage 5's cost back), and
their forest is **darker than main's by a tenth** over the trees, the same on every frame —
most likely stage 5's bounce off the ground taking the ground's own layers, not isolated and
not yet judged against the reference. Both are why the row is still `in progress`.

### Stage 7: a crown's shade as a prior

Roadmap R69 stage 7 (2026-11-12, batch 61; [the measurements](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-7-a-crowns-shade-as-a-prior),
[the grounding](../experiments/crown-shade-grounding.md)). Stage 6 left the cache asked for
something it is the wrong shape for: the fine structure of light inside a crown.

**The darker forest, judged first.** The reference tracer on the grove over a layered, textured
ground (the page has the scene and the table): over the trees main stands at **1.47** of the
reference in linear light, stages 5 and 6 at **1.05**; over the ground both stand at 1.07.
**Stage 5's darker picture is the right one.** Main's bounce off a layered ground does not read
any of its layers — the palette's order moves neither picture — and brings back more light than
any layer reflects; stage 5's `terrain_hit_material` brings back the ground's own.

**What is fine inside a crown is the crown's own shade, and it is known from the tree alone.** The
diffuse light at a point inside foliage is what the leaves between it and the open let through,
exp(−G u s) along a path of s metres through u m² of leaf a cubic metre (Monsi and Saeki 1953;
G = 0.5 for leaves of no preferred direction), averaged over the directions it comes from. So:

- **Each mesh with a crown carries a grid of its own shade** (`gfx::build_crown_prior`,
  `domain/gfx/crown_prior.h`; `renderer::build_crown_priors`, `crown_priors.h`). At load, the
  finest level's alpha-tested triangles of a mesh are its leaves; each one's area times **the share
  of it its own mask keeps** — the material's base colour alpha asked at the triangle's 16
  sub-triangle centroids on the CPU, as the coverage bake asks it (T146; it was a constant 0.7, a
  solver's blade, and cards over 0.05 m² were refused, which left every bought tree without a
  crown; a host that released the mesh's UVs before the prior is built — `engine-view` today,
  `release_uploaded_streams` — gets each image's mean instead, exact for a card that maps its
  whole image) — is gathered into a grid over the mesh's bounds, at most 16 cells an axis and
  a quarter metre a cell, and from each cell's centre the grid is marched along twelve directions
  of the upper hemisphere and their mirror images. A cell keeps two bytes: the mean transmitted
  fraction from above and from below. A mesh whose leaves stand under 1.5 m has none (a sward's
  shade is its own solver's), and the load logs it (`crown prior skipped: …`). One buffer holds a 32-byte `gfx::CrownPriorDesc` a mesh and the
  grids behind them (`ResolveParams::gi_crowns`, `gi_crown_count`; the block grew a row, 576 to
  592 bytes): 11.8 KB for the grove's three crowns. **No vertex carries a byte for it**, the field
  is the same for every LOD and every instance (optical depth does not change under a uniform
  scale), and a mesh that arrives after the load has no record and is read as before.
- **A surface's prior** (`gi_crown_prior`, gi_cache.slang; `gfx::crown_prior`) is the grid's two
  means at its point in mesh space — the instance's 3×4 inverted by its rows' cross products,
  trilinear between cell centres — weighted by the share of the surface's own hemisphere that is
  above the horizon, (1 + n.y) / 2, and never under a sixteenth. **Foliage** is a pixel or a hit
  whose material is alpha-tested (`k_material_masked`) on a mesh with a grid; a trunk, a twig's
  bark, the ground and everything else keep the faces and the ladder they had.
- **A crown's cells have no face** (`k_gi_face_crown`, the nine key tags past the six faces'). A
  crown's leaves face every way at every depth, so a face split their samples six ways (stage 6's
  count) and described nothing. A foliage sample goes to the three levels above its own (the own
  level's leaf-sized cells never filled) and **adds its light undivided and its own prior to the
  cell's count, in sixteenths** (`k_gi_crown_weight`): the cell's mean is then the sum of its
  samples' light over the sum of their priors — a ratio of sums, whose noise is the samples' own
  and which gives back, over the pixels that read it with their own priors, exactly the light the
  samples brought. (The first build stored each sample's own quotient: a deep sample's noise
  times up to sixteen.) A count that fills its sixteen bits now stands for the whole history
  (`gfx::gi_history_rate`), since a crown's coarse cell at 3840×2160 takes more than 4,095 a
  frame.
- **A foliage pixel reads one face and one level** (`scene_ambient`'s `crown`): two levels up
  from its own — sixteen times the own cell's samples and every facing's together, whole on the
  first frame — and the one above only while that is young; times its own prior. Eight lookups
  where stage 6 read two to four levels on one or two faces. Where no level has a sample it is the
  harmonics times the prior, the tree's own shade under an open sky. A bounce's hit on foliage
  reads the same way (`gi_bounce`), and so does a reflection's (`hit_shade.slang`).

**What it does** (the grove, RTX 5090; the page has the tables). At 3840×2160 with traced
primaries and shadows the frame over crowns is **0.22 ms under main's** (4.75 against 4.97 ms;
the resolve 1.90 against 2.11, stage 6's 2.28) and 0.1 under it over sand. On the turn to the
grove from looking away the first frame stands **0.39** of an 8-bit step from the long-held
picture (main 0.72, stage 6 0.99, the still picture's floor 0.29) and +0.07 in the mean (main
+0.03, stage 6 +0.17): the band is inside the floor. On the stand of nine crowns
(`gi cache: on a stand of trees a coarse level holds the fine one's light, flattened`) a coarse
level of the crown's cells times each pixel's prior moves the darkest third and the brightest
third of the crowns together (−1.5 and −1.7 steps against the fine level) where a coarse level
of faces moved them 8.8 apart (+7.3 and −1.5): the flattening is gone, and a level's offset of
3 % is left.

**What it does not do.** Against the reference the still picture is where stage 6 left it, a
little worse in the shade: the trees' darkest third stands at 1.9 to 2.1 of the reference (stage
6: 1.7 to 1.9; main 2.8 to 3.0), so a crown's shaded leaves are still too bright by a factor of
two with every read — the prior moves where the light is held, not how much of it the cache
finds. The still picture's change between frames over far crowns is 0.14 of a step against
main's 0.08: a whole crown now shares a few cells, and their sixteen frames of memory move every
pixel of it together. And one G and one card fill stand for every species (the grounding page).
**A prior that is wrong shows on a turn's first frame.** The stand's crowns are cubes, which
counted as leaf are 6.5 m² a cubic metre and sit on the prior's floor: turned to from looking
away, their first frame stands 3.7 steps *darker* than it will be for seven frames
(`gi cache: a turn to a stand of solid crowns stands nearer and settles sooner with the prior` holds
that it is nearer than stage 6's 6.8 apart and settles sooner, and says the band's bound is not
met there) — a bounce's hit on foliage with no cell yet takes the harmonics under its prior.

**On the forest** (v41, 3840×2160 traced, the owner's wind; two flights thirteen minutes apart,
not one lease) stage 7 costs **1.6 ms a frame over main** at `south-lake` held (20.33 against
18.75 ms: the sample pass 1.99 against 1.46, the resolve 9.10 against 8.48, the ray tracing chain
2.54 against 2.32, the primaries 3.01 against 2.73), where the target was half a millisecond.
The prior's read does not show there: of the forest's 14,749 meshes 93 have a crown of their own
and 196 distance forms read their source's, while the far forest's impostors, the sward and every
other alpha-tested mesh keep stage 6's walk, and the samples round the eye and their volume are
stage 5's as they were. Its forest is darker than main's by 9.0 8-bit steps over vegetation and
2.5 over the rest — the side the judge above says is right. The row stays `in progress`.

### Stage 8: what the forest paid for, and what a far crown remembers

Roadmap R69 stage 8 (2026-11-12, batch 62; [the measurements](../experiments/gi-cache-2026-11-07.md#stage-8-the-forests-cost-by-term-the-far-crowns-flicker)).
Stage 7 was held for two things: the forest's frame over main's, and a still picture that changed
between frames by 0.136 of a step over far crowns where main's changes by 0.076.

**The split came first, and it moved every cut** (the page has the table: stage 7's binary flown
on the forest with one thing switched at a time, main beside it). The gap was 0.75 to 1.0 ms in
one machine state, not 1.6 between two: the sample pass +0.48, the resolve +0.37, the chain
+0.19, the primaries +0.17. Three of the four were not what stage 7 took them for:

- **The directions round the eye cost by where they ran, not by what they traced.** A quarter of
  them cost three quarters as much, and halving the volume they trace through changed nothing.
  They were the sample pass's last workgroups; their rays are its longest (from the eye through
  whatever stands round it, then a bounce); and a workgroup of them was dispatched when the
  windows' work was done, so the pass waited on an idle device for its slowest few threads.
  **They are the pass's first threads now** (`gfx::k_gi_shell_first`, `gi_shell_base`,
  `renderer.gi.shell_first`): the same directions, the same rays, the same cells, run beside
  the windows' 620,000 samples. Nothing a picture can show changes.
- **The chain's share is the swaying trees between 24 and 48 m behind the eye**: 9,300 clusters
  whose structures are instantiated from the deformed pool every frame. Nearer than 24 m the
  volume's geometry is rigid or already in the frame for the sun. **The volume's reach is 24 m**
  (`renderer.gi.shell_m`, 48 until now). What a turn shows of a tree past it is the ladder's
  and the crown's prior's to hold, and they hold it: the grove's turn, 75 m out, stands 0.24 of
  a step from its long-held picture on its first frame.
- **The primaries' share is the nearest geometry** — the instances the eye stands in hold their
  clusters all round the eye with the volume, and every primary ray starts inside more boxes —
  and no reach worth having removes it (0.13 of the 0.17 at 12 m). It stays; an instance that
  holds only casters could be masked out of the primaries' traversal, which is the chain's row.

**The resolve's read is stage 7's, and the cut that was built for it was not kept.** Stage 7
gave a crown's cells and its one-level read to the 93 meshes of the forest that have a crown,
and left every other alpha-tested mesh — the sward, the shrubs, the far forest's impostors, the
forms' merged cards — the walk over face-keyed levels: "every alpha-tested surface on the
crown's cells with a prior of one" was its untried lever. It was built in the form that leaves
the resolve's modules byte for byte stage 7's: a record for such a mesh in the load's table, **a
grid of one cell that lets everything through**, which the shader's lookup reads as a prior of
one by the rule it already had (a build then compiles two new pipelines, the cache's own, in
80 ms each, where a change to the resolve's source compiles them all — a first forest load that
needs 53 GB of the machine). Flown on the forest twice, main beside it in the same lease: with
the cell for every mesh the resolve stood **0.77 ms** over main's and the water's reflections
0.14 (stage 7's walk: 0.37); with it for meshes of low leaves alone (cards that stand under a
crown's 1.5 m), 0.58. The cell is read through the grid's lookup — the instance's 3×3 inverted,
eight cells, their blend — and that, on every alpha-tested pixel, costs more than the walk it
ends: a far impostor's level is the ladder's last, so its walk was one level already. **A cut
is held by the pair that measures it, not by the count of lookups it removes**, and this one
is out of the tree. The form that pays no lookup is a one returned in the shader before the
grid is touched; it changes the resolve's source, a first forest load of such a build needs
66 GB of commit free, and the machine had 57 to 64 on this day, so it was not flown.

**A foliage cell remembers sixty-four frames** (`gfx::k_gi_crown_history_frames`,
`k_gi_stamp_crown`; the fold). What sets a cell's rate is `gi_history`: a cell keeps 256 samples
or sixteen frames of them, the longer, so a coarse cell that takes hundreds a frame moves a
sixteenth of the way to each frame's mean. For a face's cell that is grain: the pixels that read
it are its own patch, and its neighbours' means move independently. A crown's cell has no face
and is read two levels up, so every pixel of a far crown reads the same few cells, and their
sixteenth-steps moved the whole crown together — which the eye reads as flicker, and the measure
as 0.136. What such a cell holds is the light outside the crown's own shade over the sky's
harmonics: the sun's hour and the sky's colour reach the picture through the harmonics the
ratio multiplies, the same frame, and what is left in the ratio is the bounce off what stands
round the tree and the crown's own geometry, which change over minutes. **A face's cell follows
the camera's world (a door, a torch's reach, a rock rolled into a hollow); a crown's follows
the sun and the wind**, and neither is hidden by a second of memory. The fold has a cell's
words and not its key's tag, so a foliage sample sets the top bit of its cell's stamp. Until the
history is full the rate is the plain mean's whatever the memory, so a crown fills as fast as it
did (`gi cache key: a foliage cell remembers sixty-four frames, and fills as fast as ever`).

**Two levers, stated and off** (`renderer.gi.shell_refresh`, `renderer.gi.shell_clip`). A
direction whose surface's cells are already whole can stop at the eye's ray and take its bounce
one frame in n, and the eye's ray can stop at the volume's reach. Both were built against the
sample pass's cost before the split showed where it was; with the directions first they buy
0.01 ms and nothing on the grove. With both on, the box's turn stood 2.06 floors from its
long-held picture where its case allows two (the first frame no further off than stage 7's:
the still picture's floor fell under it), and the stand of trees at 16 m, past the volume,
stood 5.9 steps off on a turn's first frame where stage 7's stood 3.7 — until the eye's rays
are stopped at the reach they warm what the sun's sweep holds past it. They stay as knobs with
those numbers beside them.

**What it does** (the page has the tables). On the grove at 3840×2160 with traced primaries and
shadows the frame is **0.3 ms under main's** over crowns and 0.2 under it over sand (stage 7:
0.2 and 0.1). The still picture's change between frames over far crowns is **0.043** of a step
(main 0.076, stage 7 0.136) and its floor 0.14 (main 0.27, stage 7 0.29); the turn's first frame
stands 0.24 from the long-held picture (main 0.72, stage 7 0.39) and +0.05 in the mean. Against
the reference tracer the picture stands where stage 7's did: 1.07 over the trees from 50 m and
1.05 from close (the grove's crowns all have grids, so nothing of this stage reaches them but
the memory).

**What the turn to a stand still shows.** Stage 7's stand of nine crowns stood 3.7 steps dark
on its turn's first frame and its fixture was blamed: crowns of solid cubes, every prior on its
floor. Built of leaf cards at a tree's leaf area (1.5 m² a cubic metre, priors from a third to
one) the stand's first frame is as dark (−3.8 against a floor of 0.14; the solid crowns −3.1),
so it is not the prior. It is the hit's fallback: a bounce's ray that meets a leaf with no cell
takes the harmonics by the ray's openness, nothing under a metre, and inside a crown every leaf
is that close — the light a crown's leaves hand each other, a fifth of its indirect term,
arrives over the frames after. A foliage hit's openness is its prior, not its ray's length;
that mend is the row's next step and not in this stage, because it moves every picture the
stage measured (`gi cache: a turn to a stand of leaf cards stands short of light, not over`
holds the error's side and says what is unmet).

**On the forest** (v41, 3840×2160 traced, the owner's wind; main and the stage back to back in
one lease). The sample pass and the chain are main's again (+0.03 and +0.02 ms held at
`south-lake`, where stage 7 stood +0.48 and +0.19) and the primaries within 0.02 to 0.11 of
them (+0.17). What is left is the resolve's read, stage 7's walk, 0.2 to 0.4 over main's.
**The frame is 0.19 ms over main's held, 0.26 on the turn and 0.11 after it** (the build as
committed; the two builds that carried the cell stood 0.60 and 0.61 over). The turn, flown as
capture sequences with the wind off: the first frame after it
stands 0.46 of a step from the long-held picture (main 0.70) and +0.03 in the mean, a tenth of
the floor, and the still forest changes between frames by 0.10 (main 0.13). The volume at 24 m
asks the chain for 800 clusters a frame more than main at that view where 48 m asked for
9,300 — a little off a capacity the owner's 4K walk overran by 38,000 the same morning, not
the mend of it.

### R171: the grain on a plain wall

Roadmap R171 (2026-11-15, batch 66; first leg: the cause and the measurement, not the mend).
The owner, walking a furnished village under `bounce`: indoors the indirect light "ends up with a
large patchy static-like texture on everything", seen before in a cave.

**The cause: the read shows the own level's mean, and indoors a mean of 256 samples is not
quiet.** Once a cell holds `renderer.gi.confident` (255) samples the walk takes it whole and stops
(stage 5), so a surface shows its own cells' means, each an average of 256 samples or sixteen
frames of them (`gi_history`), at the cells' own size. Such a mean carries a sample's spread over
the square root of its effective count (about 2T − n for an exponential average of T samples
taking n a frame: 511 for an own cell at the trickle's density). On open ground a sample's spread
is about its mean (stage 6's `k_gi_sample_cv2` of 2); indoors it is not, because the light comes
through an opening a cosine ray seldom finds — a share p of the hemisphere brings nearly all of
it, and the spread squared over the mean squared is about 1/p. Under `sky`, where only the
opening brings light, the village's walls show 15 to 28 % grain; under `bounce`, which lights
every hit, 4 to 5 %, which is a spread squared of about five times the mean's square. Nothing
else is needed to explain it, and each candidate the brief named was isolated by one capture
(3840×2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt`, `bounce`, main's build b299cce2, held 180 to 320 frames;
the grain is the spread of the indirect term over the harmonics' picture of the same frame,
divided by its own falloff, at 1.5 to 32 pixels):

| capture (village, house 0) | near wall | far wall | what it rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| the read as it is | 3.97 % | 5.17 % | the defect |
| four times the rays | 2.28 | 3.56 | samples: the law of a mean says half |
| level +1 read whole (`show_level` 1) | 1.91 | 3.46 | four times the samples a cell |
| level +2 | 1.02 | 1.84 | sixteen times |
| level +3 | 0.86 | 1.21 | sixty-four times |
| `cell_scale` 0.002 or 0.008 | 3.97, 4.04 | 5.17, 3.30 | the footprint against the pixel |
| `sky` (no bounce) | 15.0 | 27.7 | heavy samples through the opening |

- **A cell's few heavy samples, and the level the read takes**: in. The grain falls with the
  samples behind the level shown, as a mean's noise does, and only with them.
- **The footprint against the pixel**: out, and why the forest's four times the cell scale bought
  nothing. A wall within about 6 m of the eye is at level 0 whatever the scale (25 mm is the floor:
  0.004 × 6 m = 24 mm), so a scale half or twice the default leaves the near wall's cells as they
  were (the same bytes); only the far wall, 5.5 m off, crossed to level 1 at twice the scale.
- **The hash or the jitter**: out. The pattern decorrelates as the cell's memory says: in the box
  below, 0.93 between consecutive frames and −0.07 sixty frames on (an exponential average of
  sixteen frames gives 0.94 and 0.02). Two runs draw the same pattern because the same binary
  traces the same rays from the same frame counts (`rng_seed` of the pixel and the cache's frame):
  a scale half the default, which changed no level near the wall, drew the default's numbers to
  the second decimal. "The same pattern in two runs" is determinism, not a fixed bias.
- **A bias in what a cell stores when most of its rays miss**: not seen as a fixed pattern. The
  village's far wall keeps more of its pattern over time than its memory explains (0.57 at 140
  frames), which is the bounce's feedback (each sample reads the hit's cells, whose errors last
  their own memory) and is in the light's mean, not its grain; the cave's mean is still falling
  at 320 frames (−27 % from 180), the room's light iterating through its walls.
- **The cave** (one passage under a 4 m shaft, `engine.caves.passage`, noon): the term over
  level +3's picture (the cave's limestone texture does not divide out of the harmonics' picture,
  which reads the same material with another normal) is 6.8 to 8.7 %, 4.4 to 6.0 with four times
  the rays and 2.6 to 3.4 at level +2: the same law, with a heavier tail (a shaft is a smaller
  share of the sky than a window).

**The measurement the tree keeps** (`gi cache: the grain on a plain wall is its cells' sampling
noise`, `systems/renderer/tests/gi_cache_tests.cpp`): the box with one opening, a plain wall seen
square from 2 m at 512 × 512 with its own cells 13 pixels wide and the trickle at one pixel in nine
— a 4K cell's footprint and density. It measures the grain as above and holds the law that names
the cause: four times the rays halve it (0.63 measured; the bound is the law with a third of
slack) and the level two up quarters it or better (0.17). It prints the grain (1.76 % here; the
box's wall sees its opening wider than a room's wall sees a window) and warns while it is over
the owner's target of 1 %.

**What the mend has to be, and what it may not be.** More rays are out (four times halve it and
cost the bounce's sample pass four times); a longer memory is out (it trails a moved light); a
blur is out (it loses the corners R167 asks for). The right shape is a read that takes the own
level by **its cells' measured spread**, not their count: a level is shown where its difference
from a coarser one is more than its noise explains, and the coarser one where it is not — stage
6's `gi_reveal` (James and Stein's positive-part shrinkage) applied to a converged level too, with
the sample's spread measured per cell rather than modelled, since indoors the model's 2 is
a fifth of the truth. That needs a cell to carry its spread: the fold can estimate it without a
per-sample accumulator, as n (m_frame − m)² averaged at the cell's own rate, and it fits in the
bucket-pressure word, which only a bucket's first cell uses (the pressure would take its high
half). Level +3 shows what the noise floor of such a read is indoors (0.9 to 1.2 % on the
village's walls). Simulated per pixel on the village's captures (the own read shrunk towards
level +3's with the spread squared at c times the mean's square over 511 samples), the model's
c = 2 leaves 2.1 and 2.6 % on the two walls and c = 5 — what the walls' grain says it is — 1.05
and 1.6 %, near the floor: the measured spread is half the mend. The shrinkage's own noise in the
read, a corner's contrast against it and the read's cost
(a second level's eight lookups on every faced pixel, 0.3 to 0.5 ms at 3840 × 2160 by stage 5's
figures) are the second leg's to measure.

**The mend: the read by its cells' measured spread** (second leg, 2026-11-16; `renderer.gi.spread`,
**off by default since the third leg**, below; `gfx::k_gi_spread`, `gi_spread_fold`, `gi_spread_detail`, `gi_spread_keep` in `gi_cache.h`,
the same arithmetic in `gi_cache.slang` and the fold in `gi_update.slang`). Two parts:

- **A cell measures its spread** in the fold, from the frames' means, with no sum of squares in
  the cell: a frame's mean of n samples differs from the history's mean m by a sample's variance
  over n plus the history's own, so n (m_frame − m)² · previous / (previous + n) estimates a
  sample's variance; the estimates are averaged at n / previous (their plain mean while the count
  grows, the cell's own rate at its cap), and at the cap each is scaled by T / (2T − n), so the
  spread over the cell's count is the variance of an exponential average's mean, arriving at the
  rate that variance relaxes at. It is a half in **the low 16 bits of the cell's first word**: the
  bucket's pressure, which only a bucket's first cell used, keeps the high 16 as fifteen bits of
  the frame with the top bit set (`gi_pressure_stamp`; a stamp matches its frame again 32,768
  frames on, and a bucket never stamped never matches). **The cell is still 32 bytes**: the cost
  is that the pressure's write in the sample pass keeps the low half (every writer stores the same
  word, so the race is benign) and the fold's free clears only the low half. `gi cache key: a
  cell's measured spread over its count is the variance of its mean` folds a heavy-tailed sample
  (5.7 times its mean's square), a tame one and level +3's 711 a frame for 26,000 to 40,000 frames
  and holds the spread's prediction to the measured variance of the mean within 0.8 to 1.25 (four
  standard deviations of a run that long, and the 3 % the correction at the cap leaves).
- **The read shrinks its answer towards the ladder's last level** (the own plus three, 64 times
  its samples) by James and Stein's rule with the variances measured: the walk's answer keeps
  (detail + var_u) / (detail + var_u + var_r), var_r its variance from the measured spreads of the
  levels it took, var_u the last level's, and **detail** the spread of the light about the last
  level at the own level's scale, **pooled over the own level's cells round the point** — each
  cell's squared difference from the last level's mean less its own noise and the last level's,
  averaged by the cells' shares (trilinear weight times confidence, as the mean is), positive
  part. Two other forms were built and flown. Stage 6's, the one difference at the point, kept
  0.6 of the grain on the village's walls (3.9 to 2.4 %): a single difference cannot tell a cell's
  detail from its noise, so a cell two of its noise off is kept three-quarters whole. Counting
  each cell round the point once pooled more (1.9 to 2.2 %) and **drew the cells' squares**: the
  set of cells round a point changes at every half cell, so the detail stepped there. By the
  shares the estimate is a population's between cells and one cell's at a cell's centre, and it is
  continuous in space and in every count. Nothing measured (a cell's first frame) keeps the answer
  whole; a level with no cell keeps it whole. It is applied to every face read and to a bounce's
  hit (whose walk has the four levels), not to a crown's cells (stage 7's prior is their detail)
  and not under `show_level`. The cost is the last level's eight lookups where the walk stopped
  before it (a converged neighbourhood), and each lookup reads the cell's first word beside its
  mean (one 32-byte block).

**What it does** (3840×2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt`, `bounce`, the first leg's held views and
metric at frames 180 to 320; the base build is this branch before the mend, which draws main's
pictures; the RTX 5090 shared with other agents' builds, 7 to 31 % of the CPU busy):

| grain, % of the indirect term | before | **the mend** | counted once (taken out) | counted once, 4× rays | before, 4× rays | level +3 read whole |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| village house 0, near wall | 3.94 – 4.14 | **2.45 – 2.57** | 1.92 – 2.19 | 1.44 – 1.50 | 2.39 – 2.49 | 0.92 – 0.94 |
| village house 0, far wall | 4.02 – 4.07 | **2.49 – 2.58** | 2.20 – 2.25 | 1.63 – 1.72 | 3.52 – 3.59 | 1.15 – 1.16 |
| the cave (over level +3's picture) | 9.85 – 9.95 | **5.43 – 5.58** | 4.43 – 4.59 | 3.33 – 3.49 | — | — |

Six-tenths of the grain, not under 1 %. **What is left**, by the same captures: the last level's
own floor (0.9 and 1.2 %, which it shows where it is taken) and the own level's noise the
shrinkage keeps: the cells whose difference from the last level is large by chance, which the
positive part keeps nearly whole (the crops show them as round blobs a cell or two wide on a flat
field, where before the whole wall was mottled). A sharper estimate of the detail is the lever: a
wider pool continuous in space (the sixteen cells round a point at the own level, eight lookups
more), or the detail kept in the cell by the fold. Four times the rays take the counted-once
read to 0.7 of itself where pure sampling noise would halve: the floor and the kept noise in
quadrature fit both. And **a fact the metric shows that the cells' memory does not explain**: the
grain's correlation with the next frame is 0.5 to 0.8 before and after the mend, where an own
cell's history (rate 1/16 to 1/23 a frame) gives 0.94 to 0.96, and level +3 read whole gives 0.92
to 0.95; so a large part of the fine levels' grain is drawn fresh each frame, which a cell's mean
cannot be. Not isolated: cells freed and remade (a full bucket's eviction; `renderer.gi.log`'s
counts would say), the young rays, or the bounce's hits reading a different cut each frame are
the candidates, and the next step is that census.
The box in the tree (`gi cache: the grain on a plain wall is its cells' sampling noise`, now with
a fourth run, the mend) goes from 1.76 to 1.29 %, 0.73 of it, and the case holds it under the read
before (what a James–Stein estimate pooled over several means guarantees); the box is small and
its light changes across a last-level cell (40 cm, 100 pixels), detail the read keeps. The three
runs that state the samples' law run with `renderer.gi.spread` off, since they describe the
samples, which the mend does not change.

**What it does not do**: blur a corner, trail a moved light or dull open ground.

- **Corners** (the indirect term over the mode-off picture, near a meeting over 40 to 400 pixels
  from it, frames 180, 240 and 320): the village's right wall under the ceiling 0.843 before and
  0.851 after (level +3 read whole: 0.856), the back wall at the floor 0.996 and 0.995, at the side
  wall 1.023 and 1.018; the box's corner in the tree 0.907 before, 0.913 after, where level +2 read
  whole lifts it to 0.928 (the case holds the mend under half that lift; four times the rays
  move it as far, 0.913, so what moves is the corner's noise). The village has no furniture in
  this view: a contact at a foot is not measured.
- **A moved light** (`gi cache: a moved light settles no slower with the measured spread`: the
  box's sun moved two hours along its arc, the wall's light −13 %, frames until it stays within a
  tenth of the change): 116 frames before, 110 after (the case holds it to two frames over). The
  last level remembers sixteen frames where an own cell remembers 23; most of the hundred frames
  is the bounce's feedback converging, which neither read changes.
- **A turn** (`gi cache: a turn shows no fill`) is nearer its long-held picture on every count
  than before — the furthest frame 1.01 of a luma step against 1.19, the change between frames in
  the first seven 0.536 against 0.534, after them 0.176 against 0.230 — but **the case fails**:
  its bounds are twice the still picture's own floor, and the mend lowered that floor more (0.47
  against 0.61; the change's floor 0.089 against 0.179) than the turn's transient, which is coarse
  cells' first frames. The bounds' derivation (a coarse cell read whole after one frame of samples
  against an own cell's 256-sample average) assumed the floor is the own level's noise; it is not
  re-derived here and the check is not widened: the coordinator's call.
- **Open ground** (the village's lane, held, same settings): the picture's mean is the same to
