So the refusal went, and a skinned character among the loaded instances draws through the pool beside a rigid tail, with the chain built over both (`dynamic instances: a skinned loaded instance beside the tail draws through the pool`, `dynamic_instances_tests.cpp`, through no shadows, the cascaded maps and traced shadows: 0 id, 0 depth and 0 colour differences against the same instances loaded whole, with the tail and without it). Writing that test found a bug of the chain over the tail: **the capacity policy's ceiling was frozen at the load's prefix**. `RtCapacity` takes its limit — the budget or the chain's union, whichever is less — when the renderer is created, and a dynamic scene's union is its prefix's pairs times the views until the tail grows the stride; the policy kept the old ceiling through every `relayout`, so a tail whose frames wanted more structures than the prefix could ever hold lost whole instances every frame, a frame drawn complete included (the test's: 70 wanted of 21 held, ten instances dropped, 2,619 pixels shadowed otherwise than the scene loaded whole). `SceneRenderer::set_dynamic_instances` now gives the policy the scene's new ceiling after a relayout. A world on tile ground never showed it, because its prefix — every tile slot — is the larger part of any frame. Such a loaded instance also **moves** since 2026-10-19 (through the flip, above), which is what lets the test game's actors walk among its props. **Still refused**: a move of a tail slot (the tail places its own), and a **deformed tail instance** — a skinned one, or one of a mesh with morph channels, which deforms whatever the flags say — refused alone, by name, by `GpuScene::set_dynamic_instances` before the layout is touched ("tail instance 6 (mesh 0, 2 joints) is skinned: …"), because the deform table is the load's and a tail slot has no entry to point at. What it needs is that table laid out like the instance tables: a capacity of entries in pages, an entry written with the instance's slot (`DeformDesc` and its pose-weight and joint runs, which the per-frame copies already rewrite), the static-shape caches budgeted over entries that come and go, and the joint span's `instance_joints` indexed by tail slot rather than by the load's instance — a stage of its own. `--deform` stays off for such a scene (`resolve_settings`, with a warning: it would deform the tail's instances too), and so do cluster templates (`--rt-templates`, built once from the load's clusters; with the chain they are refused by `GpuScene::create`). [E37](../experiments/e37-tile-instance-blocks.md) measures the blocks along E35's flythrough: a change costs 0.17–0.18 ms of CPU with the ashlar kit and 0.36 ms with the kit of boxes, against 15.6–15.9 and 3.3 ms before, and no frame waits for the device (the worst frame is 2.4 ms of wall time, against 23); a frame that brings a table set up to date spends 16–17 µs of GPU on it at the median, and 0.27–0.51 ms on a whole rewrite after a compaction or a growth; and the holes, at a median 14–18% of the dispatch under the 25% share, cost the ashlar kit's cull 18% (0.037 ms) — a hole costs what a culled pair does, which is the search — and the boxes' nothing measurable. At a 12% share they cost half that for four times the compactions. Until W81 a change still read the tail whole — the world handed every tile over on every change and the renderer compared each against what it held; since 2026-10-31 a tile brings its version and an unchanged one is not read (above, "A block may bring its own instances and a version").

**What holds it.** `dynamic_instances_tests.cpp` builds one scene with a prefix (a box and the ground) and, in its first case, gives it tails as one block between frames — a tile of six boxes; that tile and 768 small boxes, which grows the stride twice (to 4,096 and to 12,288 pairs); another tile alone, rewritten in place and compacted; both tiles in the other order; nothing — rendering a few frames from elsewhere after each change so the capture's occlusion history is a moving one, and captures each against a scene **loaded** with the prefix and the tail from the start: **0 id, 0 depth and 0 colour differences** at every step, through the mesh path with occlusion culling, with cascaded shadow maps, and through the vertex path's indexed draw, with the tail holding 832–7,550 of the pixels (RTX 5090, 2026-09-25). Its second case hands the tail over **tile by tile**: a tile, then a second behind it, the first leaving a hole, a third taking the hole (a block reused, split), a fourth going to the end, the first coming back differently and then moved (rewritten in place), a compaction asked for, the large tile leaving so that the holes bring one on, and nothing — every step against the loaded scene, with the ids compared through `tail_indices`, and `validate_tables` (every slot's `first_pair` at or above the last, every live slot its block's, every other slot null) after every change; and then the same ten changes on **consecutive frames none of which is waited for**, captured at the end — through the mesh path with two and with three frames in flight (two and three table sets), with cascaded maps and through the vertex path: **0 id, 0 depth and 0 colour differences** at every step of every run, with 2 compactions, the hole reused, and 10–320 hole pairs at the steps that have them (RTX 5090, 2026-09-25). **A loaded instance moved among tiles** (`dynamic instances: a loaded skinned instance moved every frame among tiles that come and go draws the loaded scene`, 2026-10-19, RTX 5090): R84's skinned bar walks 0.6 m a frame for ten frames while three tiles of boxes arrive, leave, come back and are kept in blocks of their own (0 to 13 tail instances, 1 to 3 blocks); each frame it is moved half a step, a frame is submitted and not waited for, and the rest of the step is moved with that frame in flight, so the set the captured frame flips to must have taken both moves and the tail's change. Through no shadows, the cascaded maps and traced shadows with casters: **0 id, 0 depth and 0 colour differences** on every frame against a scene loaded whole with the bar where it then stands and that frame's tail (the ids through `tail_indices`), the bar over 70–168 pixels and its centre moving from column 78 to 121, and a tail slot's move and a move to another mesh refused. The same file checks that a scene read whole refuses a tail, that the ray path and traced shadows resolve away for a dynamic scene, that `PairExpandParams` is the push-constant block `pair_expand.slang` reflects, and, with no device, the pair cap and the placement: a tail's prefix sum, a caller's own budget, the 2^24 limit before anything is allocated, a mesh the scene has not, a skinned tail instance, and the fit and the transform composed as the load composes them. `tile_layout_tests.cpp` holds the layout's arithmetic with no device: the classes and their quarter bound; first fill, keep, rewrite in place, free, reuse with a split, merge and trim, step by step; compaction by share and on request, tight packing at the cap and the refusals past it; and 400 random changes of forty tiles of four kinds, after each of which a simulated table written from the layout's own writes is sorted by `first_pair`, holds every tile where the layout says, and answers every sampled pair of the dispatch — found by the cull's own search — with its tile's instance or with nothing.

**On tile ground, traced** (`streamed_tail_tests.cpp`, 2026-10-12, RTX 5090): a small world of dune tiles (8 m tiles in three rings, `terrain_tiles_gpu_tests.cpp`'s) drawn through the pool, given a test layer of two boxes on every tile within two of the camera, a block per tile keyed by it. Loaded to take a tail and holding none, the ground is the picture of the same world loaded not to — 0 id, 0 depth and 0 colour differences — and with the layer, every pixel no box covers is still that picture, at both cameras; 33 boxes in the ids at each, none a slot the layout does not hold; the layer moved to another camera and back draws the first picture's depth and colour again, and the layer gone draws the ground alone word for word. With traced shadows and casters, the rasterizer and the ray path over the tail: no pixel where both hit the tail names another instance or cluster, and 1–2 coverage and 4–5 triangle differences in 3,468–3,534 tail pixels — silhouettes, as a ray and a rasterized edge always differ (the posed bar's case above; the ray path's depth is its hit's, so it is not compared); the boxes' traced shadows darken 1,720 pixels of the sand; the tail grew the stride, so the chain and the pool were laid out again at least once; and with every block gone the traced, shadowed picture is the ground alone's word for word: a block that leaves traces nothing.

### The cull culls instances first

(R16 and R173, 2026-11-17; behind `renderer.cull.instances`, on by default.) The cull ran one thread per pair of the whole pair space, and nearly every one of them did the whole of its work — found its instance (the search over `first_pair`, or W6's pair table), read the instance, its mesh and its cluster, moved the sphere, tested six planes and every caster volume — to learn that its instance was behind the camera. On a grid of 328,328 rocks at 16.74 M pairs, the forest proof of concept's scale, about 1 % of the pairs survive a camera run, and a run cost 0.75 ms searching and 0.35 ms reading the table at 3840 × 2160 traced; the table's 134 MB were never the cost (about 0.075 ms of the card's bandwidth), the threads were ([the measurement](../experiments/cull-by-instance.md)). So every cull run now begins with an **instance pass**, as NVIDIA's cluster LOD sample and Nanite do (the same page has what was read of them):

- **The sphere.** `mesh_bounds_main` (cluster_cull.slang, a workgroup a mesh) measures, in mesh space, a sphere round every cluster's own sphere of each mesh — the box of their spheres, its centre, the farthest sphere's reach from it — into a float4 a mesh (`CullParams::mesh_bounds`). The renderer measures them again on a frame that writes the mesh table (an admitted or retired mesh, a ring's chunk shown or hidden: `GpuScene::prepare_records`' mesh copies), when the table is another buffer (a relayout), and at the first frame, in front of that frame's first instance pass; nothing per frame otherwise.
- **The instance pass.** `cull_instances_main` runs a thread an instance over each run's block and moves its mesh's sphere as a pair's is moved (`instance_point`, the radius times `scale_max` plus the instance's padding and its terrain level's, and a slack of a few ulps of the distance from the eye for the rounding on either side), then applies the tests that reject a pair **with no side effect**: a null mesh (a hole's instance), the cascade's caster policy, the frustum — outside it, a caster volume when the run keeps casters, and inside it a cascade's own volumes (R49) — and the Hi-Z where the run culls by it, neither streams (a streamed pair asks for its pages before its occlusion test) nor counts (the occlusion term's debug counters count an occluded pair's LOD). Each test is the pair's own on a sphere that holds the pair's and is monotone in the sphere, so an instance it rejects has no pair the pass over pairs would have kept. A survivor appends one **item**, `{instance, first local cluster}`, a run of 32 of its clusters, behind a count word — one atomic a wave.
- **The pair pass.** A fold turns each run's count into a folded dispatch (`fold_args.slang`, T165), and the run's cull is that dispatch, indirect: `cull_items_main` runs one 32-lane workgroup an item, and each lane runs exactly what `cull_main` runs for its pair (`cull_instance_pair`), with its instance known — **no search and no table read**, so `renderer.cull.pair_table` has nothing to do while this is on. The camera's runs (pass 1, pass 2 or the single pass, a block a view) and each cascade's take it alike; the per-pair outputs — the flags, the fade, the entries, the casters — are written by the same code for the same pairs.

**Why the Hi-Z test is monotone, and how it was not** (review finding A1, fixed 2026-11-18). A sphere inside another must fail every test the outer one fails. The planes do. The occlusion test (`occluded`, cluster_cull.slang) has two halves: the screen rectangle of the sphere's cube, whose inner one lies inside the outer's and is read at a mip no finer, where each texel holds the farthest of its children, so the outer's farthest depth is no nearer than the inner's; and the sphere's depth, which must be its least. It was not: the test took the point nearest the eye in distance, `c - r c/|c|`, whose view depth is `(|c| - r) cos θ` while the sphere reaches `|c| cos θ - r`, deeper by `r (1 - cos θ)` — and a small sphere inside a large one off the view's axis reads nearer than the large one. A dumbbell's sphere of radius 19.4 centred 45 degrees off the axis at (60, 0, −60) read view depth 46.3 against its near cube's 41.0, and a wall at 42.95 covering the rest of its rectangle culled the instance and the cube in front of the wall with it, while the pair pass, on the cube's own small sphere, drew it. The pair test had the same flaw at a cluster's radius, on main since occlusion culling: with the cubes as one primitive, one cluster whose own sphere is the large one, the near cube vanished with occlusion on and the instance pass off. **The depth is now the sphere's least** (`sphere_nearest_depth`): a perspective `view_proj`'s clip w is the distance along the view's axis, `A·p + w0` with `A` its w row's xyz, and its clip z a function of w alone, so the depth — reversed Z, largest where w is least — is largest at `c - r A/|A|`, exactly, anywhere on the screen. Both passes test by it; a view with no perspective (`|A|` zero) culls nothing by the Hi-Z. The occlusion term's hidden share (`hidden_fraction`) still reads the old point: it scales the LOD thresholds and removes no surface, and changing it moves the cut, which is a row of its own.

**Every mesh's sphere is measured** (found by the same case, 2026-11-18). The renderer told `CullInstances::prepare` the table held `null_mesh() + 1` meshes, which is right for a dynamic scene, whose null mesh is the table's last entry, and wrong for a scene read whole, which has none and whose `null_mesh()` is 0: only mesh 0's sphere was measured, and every other mesh's instances were tested by whatever the buffer held — on the RTX 5090 a point at the instance's origin — so an instance whose origin was off the screen or behind a surface lost every cluster. The grid of rocks (one mesh) and the tiled world (dynamic) never showed it; the dumbbell, the second mesh of its scene, did. Now `prepare` takes the table's size in bytes and measures every `gfx::MeshDesc` in it: the scene's meshes, a ring's and the room's slots, and the null mesh where there is one.

**What it costs.** One more pass a run over the instances (a fiftieth of the pairs at the forest's ratio) and a fold, the buffers `CullInstances` keeps (`src/cull_instances.h`): a run's items, at most an item an instance plus one a 32 pairs (`gfx::cull_item_capacity`), 8 bytes each, for every view's two blocks and every cascade — about 6.8 MB a run at the cap, so 41 MB for one view with occlusion and four cascades, grown by half again as the scene grows — and 16 bytes a mesh. A survivor's last item runs fewer than 32 lanes: an instance of 35 pairs fills 35 of 64. The timers count the instance passes, the folds and the spheres in the cull's zones (`cull`, `shadow_cull`), so a frame record compares like with like.

**What it saved** (2026-11-18, the session locked, main searching, main reading the table and this build back to back a scene in one lease; 3840 × 2160 traced with the bounce; the grid of rocks; the cull's medians in ms, then the frame's total): 1.01 M pairs 0.052 / 0.035 / **0.019**; 8.04 M 0.325 / 0.181 / **0.112**; 16.74 M 0.747 / 0.354 / **0.236**, the frame 5.02 / 4.62 / **4.49** ms — every frame of the three culling the same set. A weaker card should expect more of the same: the pass over every pair is thread-bound, so a card with a sixth of the 5090's processors (the Titan Xp) spends several times as long on it, and the instance pass cuts the threads it runs by about the share of the pairs whose instances are out of view. The hw/csm pair and `streamed-forest`'s were not flown ([the measurement](../experiments/cull-by-instance.md)).

**What holds it.** `dynamic instances: the cull draws the same with instances culled first and not` flies the tiled world — tiles arriving and leaving between frames, holes, the camera's two occlusion passes and four cascades — with the instance pass on and off, the pair table read and searched, and every step draws the loaded scene's ids, depth and colour. `renderer: occlusion keeps a surface in front of the Hi-Z off the view's axis` is the dumbbell above, its cubes as two clusters and as one: occlusion on, the instance pass on and off, draws exactly what occlusion off draws, the near cube whole. Every other GPU test of the renderer runs with it on, the picture tests against their references among them; `domain/gfx`'s tests run the pass over pairs (`items` 0) as before.

### Nodes before instances

(R188 stage 1, 2026-11-19; behind `renderer.cull.nodes`, **off by default** until its pair is flown and holds the culled set to the frame; [the design](../experiments/instance-hierarchy.md).) The instance pass runs a thread an instance over every instance, once a cull run — once traced, six times with occlusion and four cascades — and the forest holds 300,000 to 375,000 of them, most of which survive nothing. A **node** is a level above it: up to 64 consecutive slots of one block of the layout — a tile's run, a hand-off cell's, or a run of the load's prefix — with a sphere round every live instance's tested sphere. A node never spans two blocks, because two blocks adjacent in slot order may be kilometres apart; the prefix is cut once, in slot order, a node ended at 64 slots, where the next slot's 64 m cell is more than one cell from the node's first on any axis, or where its terrain level differs.

- **The layout** (`NodeLayout`, `node_layout.h`) says only which slots each node holds. The renderer keeps it from the scene's public surface — the prefix's records and `TileLayout::blocks` — so neither the GPU scene nor the tile layout knows nodes exist: after a change the tail's nodes are compared with the blocks by first slot and count, a run that stays keeps its id, and every other id is freed or given out (a free list) and named in each table set's list of changed ids.
- **The sphere is measured on the GPU** (`cull_node_measure_main`, a workgroup a node, a lane a slot), never handed over by a world: each live instance's sphere exactly as the instance pass takes it, but from its anchor's cell (the node's first live slot) rather than the eye, its box, the box's centre `m` and the farthest reach, `R = max(|c'_i − m| + r0_i) × (1 + 1e-5) + 1e-4`; and its live count, the largest cascade policy of its instances (0 when one casts into every cascade) and their one terrain level (a node of two levels is never culled). The node pass tests `R + |c_m| × 2e-5` round the centre moved into the eye's frame as an instance's translation is, plus the level's padding, which moves with the frame and so is not measured. Why that sphere holds each instance's, to the float, is the derivation in `cluster_cull.slang` beside the passes: the instance pass's distance slack is bounded by the node's, and the second `1e-5` of `|c_m|` covers rounding the centre separately.
- **The passes of a run**, in front of the fold and the item pass, unchanged: the **node pass** (`cull_nodes_main`, a thread a node, the instance pass's own tests — the caster policy by the node's largest, the frustum and the caster volumes, the Hi-Z where the run neither streams nor counts — each monotone in the sphere), appending the survivors' ids one atomic a wave; a fold of their count; and the **instance pass from node items** (`cull_node_instances_main`, a 64-lane workgroup a surviving node, each lane `instance_may_survive` on its slot exactly as before, its items appended as before). A rejected node holds no instance the instance pass would have kept, so the culled set and every picture are the instance pass's own; only the visible list's order within a run, which nothing drawn may depend on, changes. Every pass declares what its shader reads and writes: the node table read by the node pass, the instance pass and the guard and written by the measure, the node items and their dispatch, the measure list.
- **What keeps a node's sphere true.** A node table a table set, because the instance tables are flipped in turn and each set's nodes must be its own instances'. The frame that flips to a set measures again, before its first node pass and after its copies, the nodes of every slot that set's pending runs write (`GpuScene::TableUpdate::copies`; for a scene read whole the record upload's instance regions, which carry `move_instances`) and every id whose slots the layout changed since the set was last current; every node of a set made again or carried over (T167); of every set on a frame that measures the meshes' spheres (a ring's chunk shown or hidden writes the mesh table, so a walk pays a full measure there — one pass over every instance, about one instance pass); and of every set when the nodes are switched on or the node table grows. A list the frame staged and recorded no measure for is measured whole next time. The pairs numbered again (T154) move no slot and measure nothing. The table is imported as last read everywhere, as the meshes' spheres are, so a measure into the set a frame in flight still reads waits for it.
- **The guard** (`cull_node_guard_main`, `renderer.cull.node_guard`, on in debug builds): once a frame, every live instance's sphere as the instance pass takes it and its node's as the node pass does, in the eye's frame, and a count of instances outside their node's sphere, under another terrain level or under a caster policy their node's would reject, beside the count checked; `SceneRenderer::cull_node_guard` reads them. A missed re-measure — the fault class nodes add — is a failing count on every frame that has one instead of an instance lost on one frame.

**What it costs.** 32 bytes a node a table set (`gfx::CullNodeDesc`, mirrored in `scene.slang`), a node id a slot on the CPU, a run's node items (4 bytes a node) and a 16-byte measure list entry a node measured; `gfx::CullParams` took its node count in a pad word and four addresses, 1,808 to 1,840 bytes. The measure, the node passes and their fold are timed in the run's cull zone (`cull`, `shadow_cull`), the guard in none. On the forest's 375,000 instances in about 5,000 tiles that is about 10,000 nodes, 320 KB a set.

**What holds it.** `world translation: nodes before instances change no byte, at home and moved by cells` draws one node whose 29 instances stand either side of a cell edge, on the three rasterizers, the vertex path's capacity draw, the ray path, traced shadows and the cascaded maps: with the nodes on the frame is the frame with them off to the byte, at home and moved by 156,250 cells, and the guard finds nothing. `dynamic instances: the cull draws the same with nodes before instances` flies the tiled world's ten changes — blocks placed, freed, reused, rewritten in place, compacted, numbered again — and then a change every frame with none waited for, with two and three table sets, through the camera's two occlusion passes and the cascades and through the vertex path, against the scene loaded whole: 0 id, 0 depth and 0 colour differences, the guard's count 0. `renderer: occlusion keeps a surface in front of the Hi-Z off the view's axis` draws the dumbbell with the nodes on too (the wall and the dumbbell one node). `node layout: …` holds the layout with no device: the prefix's cut, ids kept and freed, and 300 random changes of the tile layout itself after each of which every live slot is in exactly one node of its block.

**What it saved** (2026-11-19, the RTX 5090, this build's `msvc-release` with `renderer.cull.nodes` false and true, alternated twice in one lease, offscreen at 3840 × 2160, the session unlocked and the processors 54 to 100 % busy with other agents' builds, so upper bounds; medians / p95 / p99 in ms). R173's grid of 328,328 rocks at 16.74 M pairs, a scene read whole, so its nodes are the prefix's cut, which on a grid laid out row by row are strips of a row a few cells long (reasoned from the cut's rule, not counted): traced (`--raster rt --shadows rt`, the bounce off) the cull went from 0.240 / 0.43 / 0.66 and 0.240 / 0.35 / 0.64 to 0.229 / 0.43 / 0.56 and 0.228 / 0.35 / 0.45, the frame's GPU total 3.08 and 3.00 against 3.09 and 2.99; with the cascades (`--raster hw --shadows csm`) the camera's culls went from 0.292 / 0.30 / 0.56 and 0.292 / 0.30 / 0.52 to 0.253 / 0.29 / 0.58 and 0.254 / 0.29 / 0.50, the cascades' from 0.257 / 0.31 / 0.54 and 0.262 / 0.29 / 0.48 to 0.232 / 0.28 / 0.30 and 0.236 / 0.29 / 0.47, and the frame's GPU total from 1.600 and 1.595 to 1.524 and 1.562. Every frame of every pair culled the same set (the drawn pairs by draw, the casters, the shadow pairs, the built structures: 400 of 400). So stage 1 takes about 0.01 ms off a traced frame at the cap and 0.06 off one with the cascades — the design's estimate for the traced camera, a tenth of what it estimated for the cascades: the grid's nodes are strips a row long whose spheres pass the frustum far more often than their instances, and the instance pass then runs over every slot of a surviving strip. **The forest staging** (`<scratch>\v41`, the owner's drop replayed as the staging's flights replay it, 2,456 frames, traced with the bounce, nodes off at 18:50 and on at 19:16, the processors at 12 to 100 %): the cull 0.093 / 0.70 / 0.89 off against 0.080 / 0.71 / 0.89 on, the frame's GPU total 17.09 / 22.08 / 23.23 against 17.26 / 22.20 / 23.49, which is the two flights' own spread (the world streams at its own pace, so the two flights hold different tiles on most frames: 347,608 against 347,672 instances at the median). Frame by frame the two cannot be compared where their worlds differ; on the 66 frames whose instances, pairs, holes and meshes were the same in both, the culled set was the same on all 66, and the id captures at frames 1,799 and 2,399 and the last were the same to the word (frames 599 and 1,199 held different tiles). **A small scene costs a little**: `streamed-forest` (6,835 instances, traced, 600 frames, flown off, on, off, on at 19:50): the cull 0.0137 / 0.023 / 0.024 and 0.0134 / 0.023 / 0.025 off against 0.0156 / 0.036 / 0.038 and 0.0153 / 0.036 / 0.038 on, two thousandths at the median and a hundredth at the tail (the measures on the frames a tile arrives), the frame's total in its spread; all 600 frames of both pairs the same set. So on its own stage 1 buys a few hundredths of a millisecond where it buys anything, and the tunable stays off: the design expects the larger share from stage 2 (the second occlusion run over the first's survivors and Hi-Z rejections alone, which removes a whole instance pass from the camera's two) and from the hierarchy below the instance, where the traced remainder is (the survivors' whole DAGs). Nodes cut square rather than along slot order where a scene is read whole (a grid, an imported world) would make the prefix's nodes compact; that is a step to measure, not taken here. Stage 2 (the second occlusion pass over the first's survivors and Hi-Z rejections alone) and stage 3 (the near band at the instance and the node) are not built.

### A relayout is swapped in

Roadmap T152 (2026-11-15). **What it was.** A tail's change that grew the stride or the instance capacity of a scene with the pool or the chain, or whose new trees' records passed the deform table's or the pose table's room ([below](#streamed-trees-sway)), left `relayout_pending()`, and `SceneRenderer::set_dynamic_instances` answered it with `FrameContext::wait_idle` and `GpuScene::relayout`. That made the trees' tables, `deform_slots` and `deform_blocks` again — the mesh records that name the slots through `upload_buffer`, a device wait of its own — and, **on every relayout, whatever had grown**, destroyed and made the whole ray tracing chain again (`lay_out_ray_tracing`): its per-instance tables and top-level structure, and through `resize_ray_tracing` at the capacity it kept, the frame's CLAS set (330,881 clusters on the engine's streamed forest, about 2 GB on the RTX 5090) and the bottom-level set. The device had to be idle because every frame in flight reads those buffers by address and the old ones were destroyed in place. On `content/test-scenes/streamed-forest` at 3840 × 2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt`, the bounce on, that was three frames of 57–83 ms on the frame's thread (`world.relayout_ms`, frames 42, 154 and 324 of every flight on both T154's and main's builds) while the GPU's own frames took 5–7 ms: the wait was a frame or two, the rest freeing and making the chain. Two of the three (frames 42 and 324: no table set written whole) were the trees' tables alone, which nothing of the chain depends on. **The slot wait two frames later** (40–56 ms at frames 44, 156 and 326, `slot_wait`) is the frame recorded just after the relayout finishing late: its timers say 5 ms, and the begin of the frame two later, which waits for its fence, waited for the rest. It is time the GPU spent outside the frame's own work on the chain freed and made again in place — what R128 found for the chain's first build at a new capacity on a card others held memory of ([above](#the-ray-tracing-chains-memory)) — and it went with the chain: a T152 relayout frees and makes none of the CLAS set, and the frame after it waits 3–5 ms, as every other frame does.

**What it is.** `GpuScene::relayout(error, &retired)` makes every buffer beside the old one and hands the old one back (`GpuScene::RelayoutRetired`); nothing in it waits for the device or uploads. The deform table and its per-frame copies are made again together (`grow_flora_tail`), so no record is ever written into a copy a frame in flight reads, and the pose table when the parts passed it; `deform_slots` and `deform_blocks`, which every frame writes before it reads, start empty as they always did, and every mesh record is written again in place by the next frame's copies (`pending_mesh_writes_`, as a mesh that arrives is) rather than uploaded — the frames in flight read the old records, which name the old slots, and those are freed only after them. **The chain is laid out again only when the instance capacity or the stride outgrew it** (`rt_layout_outgrown`): its per-instance tables, its top-level structure and bindless slot go to `retired`, and the bottom-level set is made at the capacity the scene holds through the chain's own step, which keeps the frame's set (`keep_frame_set`, R130 and R152) — so a relayout never frees or makes the CLAS set. The top-level records are not uploaded: an outgrown layout made every table set again (`fit_tables`), and the frame that next flips to one copies every slot's record before its top-level build, which reads none past the instances. The renderer defers the buffers to the slot of the frame submitted last (`FrameContext::defer_destroy`), the chain's step's to its worker (R128), and frees each retired top-level structure with its bindless slot once that frame's timeline value has completed (`SceneRenderer::free_retired_tlas`, from `begin_frame`). **What still waits**: a relayout whose chain half the device cannot hold beside the old — asked of the memory budget as a swapped resize asks it (R116), at half as much again as the half it replaces — sets `must_wait`, and the renderer waits and lays out as before, counted (`TileStats::relayout_waits`). So does one that **fails part way** (since 2026-11-16, the review of T154): the budget's answer is an estimate, and a step out of memory inside the chain's lay-out used to return false with the retired half neither deferred nor freed, `relayout_pending()` already cleared and the chain half replaced — new per-instance tables and top-level structure beside the old bottom-level set — while `resize_ray_tracing`'s comment said the caller waits and tries again, which neither caller did (the hosts stop on that false). Now what the swapped call had replaced goes to the same release as on success, the relayout stays pending with the chain marked to be laid out whole (`rt_relayout_failed_`, since the swapped call had already moved the instance slots and the union and `rt_layout_outgrown` alone would not see it), and the renderer waits and calls it without `retired`, which destroys whatever stands and makes the whole layout, counted in `relayout_waits`; only that call's failure is returned. **The trees' tables' growth cannot fail part way** (T163, 2026-11-17): swapped, `grow_flora_tail` sets the old pose table, deform table and copies aside instead of retiring them, and only once every new one is made retires the old and keeps the new capacities; a make that fails destroys what it made and puts the old buffers and capacities back, so the scene is exactly as before the call and the growth stays pending with the rest, for the waited call. Until T163 its capacities had moved and the old buffers were retired by the time a make failed, so it returned the error and the hosts stopped. Waited, it still frees first — that call may be waiting for want of room — and its failure is returned, as the chain's is. **A seam the tests pull**: `GpuScene::fail_next(Fault::rt_step | Fault::flora_tables, n)` makes the next `n` makes of the chain's step (`resize_ray_tracing`, whoever calls it) or of the trees' tables' growth fail as a device out of memory would; no host sets it. The cases: "dynamic instances: a relayout whose chain fails part way is retried whole, the same" (one wait, then the scene loaded whole to the pixel) and "tail budget: a growth of the trees' tables that fails is put back and retried whole". **What it costs**: memory for the frames in flight, the old and the new together — the trees' tables (2 to 4 MB on the tests' palms), the pool's per-entry slots, and on a capacity growth the chain's per-instance half and bottom-level set, which on a smaller card are as much smaller as its scene is; a card too full to hold them waits, as above, rather than evicting. A scene with no tail never relays out and pays nothing.

**Measured** (streamed-forest, 3840 × 2160, rt/rt, the bounce on, 900 frames, three alternating pairs in one lease; 21.5% of the processors busy with others' work, the session locked, so every number an upper bound):

| | Before (T154's 8a5318e3) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `relayout_ms` at frames 42 / 154 / 324 | 63–65 / 58–69 / 57–76 | 0.75–1.22 / 0.38–0.40 / 1.36–1.39 |
| `slot_wait` at frames 44 / 156 / 326 | 48–56 / 40–47 / 43–48 | 2.6–3.7 / 3.3 / 5.0–5.1 |
| frames over 33 ms (each flight) | 6, 6, 6 | 0, 0, 0 |
| wall median / p99 / max | 4.63–4.65 / 9.09–9.31 / 65.7–78.3 | 4.62–4.65 / 8.68–8.86 / 9.5–9.6 |

**What holds it.** `dynamic instances: a relayout with frames in flight waits for nothing, draws the same` hands the skinned bar's scene its six boxes with two frames in flight, under the cascaded maps and, where the device traces, traced shadows: the stride and the capacity grow, the change makes no device wait on the frame's thread (`gfx::device_waits_on_thread`), none is counted in `relayout_waits`, and the frames after it draw the scene loaded whole to the id, the depth and the colour; on the RTX 5090 the relayout took 0.47 ms traced. `tail budget: the trees' tables grow beside the old ones and wait for nothing` grows the palms' tables past their first room and checks the same of the trees' half: no wait, the old tables handed back, the chain untouched. The forest staging's frame of the same mechanism (`relayout_ms` 150 of a 189 ms frame) and the player walk's 523 ms frame were not flown on this change: the machine had 16 to 20 GB of free commit against the forest's 40.

### The tail's CPU table grows into room made ahead

Roadmap W155 (2026-11-21). The GPU's tables grow beside the old ones (above); the CPU's own copy of the instance table did not. `GpuScene::instance_table_` (96 bytes a slot) and the keys beside it grow by the container's half again when a hand-over passes their capacity, and on the forest staging's grounded walk that is the hand-over near frame 1,578: 470,000 slots, a new 67 MB block, 45 MB copied and every page of it faulted in for the first time, on the frame thread — the slot write's 28 to 48 ms of CPU (the startup trace's `tiles write slots`, beside 297,268 slots written in 114 ms by the first fill) on the frame that also grows the GPU's tables, so the walk's worst frame of its own ([the page](../experiments/wide-frame-and-long-frames-2026-11-21.md#w155-the-walks-own-long-frames)). **Now the next block is made before it is needed** (`renderer::TableRoom`, `table_room.h`): between frames (`SceneRenderer::begin_frame`), once the table is three quarters full, the block its next growth takes is reserved — an address range, nothing touched — and faulted in `renderer.tiles.table_room_kib` (1,024) a frame; the hand-over that passes the capacity copies the table into resident pages and swaps (`TableRoom::take` in `GpuScene::write_slots`), allocating nothing, and the old block is freed by the next frame's `prepare`. **On the walk** (W155's pair, the same hour, four flights alternating): the growth frame's world update 30.8 and 35.7 ms on the base, 20.2 with the room; its slot write 24.5 and 29.7 against 15.2. What is left on that frame is the copy itself, 11.5 ms for 45 MB element by element, and the relayout's chain resize (T152). The table's contents and order are the container's own growth's to the byte, so nothing drawn can differ. A growth larger than the room (a jump past half again at once) grows on the frame as before. The cost is the room itself, a block of the next capacity held from three quarters full until the growth (67 MB at the walk's 470,000 slots, a third of a percent of the forest's commit), and about a millisecond a frame of page faults for the 70 or so frames it takes; 0 turns it off. The startup trace splits the slot write into the table's own resize (`tiles slots resize`) and the slots written (`tiles slots written`) so a flight says which. Held by `table_room_tests.cpp`, with no device and by count: a growth that takes the room makes no allocation on the thread where the plain growth makes one, the block is faulted in the stated bytes a frame, and every slot is where it was.

### The visible list's runs are sized by the frame

Roadmap W51-5 (2026-11-19). **What it was.** Every run of the visible list — three a view and one a shadow cascade — was as long as the pair stride, because no draw can append more than every pair, and so was everything kept per entry: the deformed-vertex pool's slots (`deform_slots`), the allocator's tile scratch (`deform_blocks`) and the vertex path's records. A scene read whole holds its pairs and no more, but a streamed world's stride is its tail's pairs and half as much again, and its frames draw a small part of it: standing in the forest staging at the low setting (1080p, the cascades) the stride was 15.8 million pairs, the list 842 MiB and the slots 421 MiB, for frames whose fullest run held a few hundred thousand entries — the frame's own device bytes 2.9 GB against 1.1 at the end of `gpu scene` ([start commit by owner](../experiments/start-commit-by-owner-2026-11-18.md#w51-5-the-withheld-meshes-and-the-runs-sized-by-the-frame)). That is `views × pairs` again, the shape this page's rule forbids for the chain.

**What it is.** A run holds `GpuScene::run_capacity()` entries, which is the stride until the frames have said what they draw and never more than it. The cull pass appends past it to nothing (`gfx::CullParams::run_capacity`, `run_takes` in `cluster_cull.slang`): the append that went over takes its slot back, so the run's count ends at the capacity whatever order the threads came in and every reader bounded by the count reads only what was written, and it is counted (`CullParams::run_drops`: two words behind the list's last entry, the camera runs' and the cascades', zeroed by the frame and read back with its statistics as `Stats::run_drops` and `cascade_run_drops`). The records pass reads its runs by `gfx::ClusterRecordParams::run_length`, a field of its own, because its `pair_count` also counts the pair slots `emit` covers, which are the scene's (208 bytes, a size table entry). **The capacity is the chain's arithmetic** (`RtCapacity`) over the fullest run each folded frame filled (`Stats::run_high`), with its own numbers (`SceneRenderer::step_runs`, scene_renderer_runs.cpp): a headroom of 50 % (`renderer.runs.headroom_pct`), twice the chain's 25 %, since a run that fills takes pairs out of the picture where a full chain takes shadows or traced primaries, and not more, because the arithmetic shrinks only when a window's peak with its headroom leaves more than half unused — at 100 % the low setting's runs stood at the stride (its fullest run, the farthest cascade's, is 28 % of it) — and a step of 65,536 entries; it grows the frame a demand eats into half the headroom, and at once, by `grow_to`, on a frame read back with drops; it shrinks after the chain's window; and the stride it starts at is a guess the first two seconds and frames answer. `GpuScene::fit_runs` makes the list, the records, the pool's slots and the allocator's scratch again beside the frames in flight (the old ones deferred to the slot submitted last) and points every mesh record at the new slots. **It is all or nothing** (W51-5b): every buffer is made before any old one goes, and a make the device refuses destroys what was made and leaves the scene exactly as it was — runs, buffers and mesh records — so the frame records at the runs it had; the refusal is counted (`Stats::run_refusals`) and said, and the policy asks again when the demand next does. Until W51-5b the old list was retired first, so a refused make leaked it (the caller returned before freeing it) and a fallback whose own make failed left the frame no list at all, and the slots were made again by a relayout whose waited form destroyed the slots every mesh record named before making their replacement. `GpuScene::Fault::runs` is the test's seam for it. **What stays by the pairs**, because a pair indexes it: the pair-to-entry tables, the occlusion flags, the cross-fade's tables and the pair table; the chain's union and its slots are the chain's ([above](#the-ray-tracing-chains-memory)). A scene read whole keeps its runs at its pairs (`step_runs` acts on a dynamic scene only), as does `renderer.runs.by_frame=false`.

**What it costs.** Nothing drawn, while the runs hold the frame: the cull's appends are the same appends, and the picture is the scene's. **A frame somebody waits for is drawn whole** (W51-5b), as the chain's is ([above](#the-ray-tracing-chains-memory)): `render_offscreen` — every capture, the reference renderer, a test — reads the frame's drops after it, and when a run filled it grows the runs to what the frame drew and turned away (the policy's growth, or exactly that with the policy off) and draws the frame again, and a second filling takes the stride, which no frame overfills (`Stats::run_redraws`; the first attempt's drops stay in `run_drops_total` and `run_drop_frames`). Until W51-5b only the chain's shortness was redrawn, and a capture taken after a long stand could come back with pairs missing. **A frame drawn in flight may still drop**: one whose demand jumps past twice what the runs were sized for within the read-back's frames drops pairs from the picture until the growth lands, counted in those same totals, and a pair a run turned away is neither counted drawn nor flagged drawn for the second occlusion pass, which asks for it again. A growth or a shrink is a list of a few tens of megabytes made beside the old one. `dynamic instances: runs sized by the frame draw the same, and a full run counts drops` holds it: the tiled world drawn by both rasterizers, both occlusion passes and the cascades with runs as long as the stride and then exactly as long as the fullest run draws the loaded scene's ids, depth and colour both ways with no drop; with half that and the policy off, the frame counts its drops, grows the runs, draws again, and the capture is the loaded scene's; the policy back on drops nothing. `dynamic instances: a refused lay-out of the runs leaves the scene as it was` holds the refusals with a skinned instance beside a tail, swapped and waited, and through the renderer with runs of one entry and every growth refused.

**A tail's arrival lays the runs out at a first bound, not the stride** (W156, 2026-11-22). The stride the runs start at is laid out when the world's first commit hands the tail over, before any frame has drawn, so the first frames of every launch held a list for every pair the tail could ever name, beside the chain's first capacity and the world's first commit: on the forest staging at 4K the list and the pool's slots stood at 16,777,216 entries a run (576 MiB) for four seconds, for frames whose fullest run held 1,100,232, and at 1080p with the cascades at 15,757,312 (1,262 MiB) for six, against a fit of 6,684,672 (535 MiB) — the largest transient of the engine's own after `gpu scene` on a warm launch at both settings ([W156](../experiments/start-commit-by-owner-2026-11-18.md#w156-what-a-launch-commits-after-it-is-ready)). Now `SceneRenderer::set_dynamic_instances` hands the scene a bound (`GpuScene::set_first_runs`, `renderer.runs.first_entries`, 4,194,304 entries, 32 MiB of list a run) and `create_working_set` lays the unsized runs out at the smaller of it and the stride; the bound is 0, the stride, where nothing would grow the runs (the cull off, or `renderer.runs.by_frame=false`). **Why that number**: the guess is given back to the frames' fit only when the fit is at most half of it (`RtCapacity`), so a bound the fit passes half of would stand instead of the fit — 8,388,608 would, at 1080p with the cascades, 137 MiB above it — and a bound under the fullest run has the first frame fill it: at 4K the camera's runs (1,100,232) fit and the guess goes to the fit; at 1080p the farthest cascade (4,419,461) fills it on the first frame, which is grown to the same fit and drawn again before anybody sees it (below). **When it applies**: only to a commit that grows the stride before any frame has sized the runs (`create_working_set` from `fit_tables`) — in practice the world's first commit after the load; a load whose own stride already covers the tail, and every arrival after the first fit, keep the runs they have. `dynamic instances: a tail's arrival lays the runs out at the first bound` holds it: the bound off lays the arrival's runs at the stride, a bound of one entry lays them at one, the list's bytes by the count, and the frames that fill it grow it, are drawn again and draw the loaded scene's ids, depth and colour.

**No frame drawn at the first bound reaches a window with an entry dropped** (W156-2, 2026-11-22). Every run shares the one capacity — the camera's two passes, the software rasterizer's, every cascade's — and a full run turns pairs away one by one in the atomic append's order, not by whole instances, so a frame drawn in flight at a bound no frame had measured could present clusters missing from the picture and from the ray-tracing structures, or casters missing from a cascade (the review of W156 found the farthest cascade dropping 225,157 casters for two or three frames of every windowed launch at the low setting). Now the arrival marks the runs to be measured, and `submit_frame` — every host's path, the window's included — draws the next frame without its present's semaphore, waits for it, and while a run filled grows the runs as `render_offscreen` does (the policy's growth, then the stride) and draws it again, the acquired image waited on by the first attempt only; then the runs count as the frames' (`GpuScene::fit_runs`) and an empty submission behind the frame raises the present's semaphore, so what is presented is the frame that was checked. Once a scene load: its cost is one waited frame and its redraws, and in a window that wait is one long frame a load, which engine-view's `--report` counts in its `long_frames` ([apps](apps.md#the-reports-long-frames)) (`Stats::run_measured`, `run_redraws`; the turned-away attempt's drops stay in `run_drops_total` and `run_drop_frames`). From there the runs are in the fitted regime above, whose frames drawn in flight may still drop on a jump in demand, counted the same way; engine-view's summary line carries every one of these counts in its `runs` block ([apps](apps.md)), so a walk's report says whether any frame it presented dropped. `dynamic instances: a frame drawn in flight at the first bound hands back no drop` holds it on the window's path: a bound of one entry, the arrival, six frames through `begin_frame` and `submit_frame` with each one's drops read after it — none — one measured frame, its first attempt's drops counted and redrawn, and the loaded scene's ids, depth and colour. Beside it, `dynamic instances: a frame measured at the first bound raises its signal once` holds the signal on both paths: a frame names a binary semaphore as `FrameDesc::signal` and the next names it as `FrameDesc::wait` and completes, at the default bound (the frame not measured, the frame itself signalling) and at a bound of one entry (measured and redrawn, the empty submission signalling), one semaphore serving both pairs.

### Meshes that come and go

**A streamed scene's meshes were all resident from its load** (R142, 2026-11-10): "a tail is instances and nothing else", so everything a placement generator would ever place had to be listed and loaded when the scene was read. Four solver rows paid for that in one day — a square kilometre of ledges solved at `open`, a wall cut into a kit of 39 modules because a merged mesh a tile had nowhere to come from, a channel bed with no cobbles — and the forest proof of concept loads 7,124 mesh records in 10.3 s at start. This section is the renderer's half of the answer; the contract is [scene_gen](scene_gen.md#a-tiles-meshes), the residency is [world](world.md#a-tiles-meshes-residency-by-reference), and the decision is [ADR-0061](../adr/0061-a-tiles-meshes-arrive-with-the-tile.md).

**The published practice it follows.** Virtualized geometry streams *pages of clusters* into a fixed pool on the device, keeps the hierarchy resident, and patches offsets when a page lands (Karis, Stubbe and Wihlidal, "Nanite: A Deep Dive", SIGGRAPH 2021 Advances in Real-Time Rendering; this engine's own page pool, "Geometry streaming", is that half). A visibility buffer there names an instance and a triangle of a cluster, never an address, which is what lets a page land in any slot. World partition loads cells of a grid by distance from streaming sources and unloads them outside a larger range, and level streaming keeps a minimum time between unload requests so a boundary does not thrash (Epic Games, Unreal Engine documentation, "World Partition" and `ULevelStreaming::MinTimeBetweenVolumeUnloadRequests`). Asset systems hold what cells share by reference count and release at zero (Unity, "Addressables: memory management"). The three ideas here are those three: a pool with patched offsets, ids that name content and not storage, and reference-counted residency with a delay on the way out. *These are cited from the published talks and manuals as known, not re-read on the night this was written; the one number taken from them, the two-second delay, is a default this page does not depend on.*

**Room, reserved in the scene's own buffers.** Every mesh of a scene lives in one set of buffers with scene-wide offsets baked into `geometry::ClusterDesc`, and every shader takes those buffers' addresses once. So a mesh that arrives goes where a terrain ring's chunk goes ("The rings in the scene"): into room made at `GpuScene::create`, by copies the next frame records. The room (`GpuScene::MeshRoom`) is a run of mesh records after the scene's own and the rings', a **cluster arena**, and the vertices and triangles the arena owns: cluster *c* of the arena owns `ClusterLodOptions::max_vertices` vertices and `max_triangles` triangles at fixed offsets, so a mesh's streams are where its cluster run puts them and there is one free list (first fit over runs of clusters) rather than three that fragment differently. A material arena follows the scene's materials. Two alternatives were weighed and left: **a second set of buffers per mesh** needs an address per stream in `gfx::MeshDesc` (full at 64 bytes, read per position) and in every build record of the ray tracing chain; **relocation** (grow the buffers, move the scene) is a wait for the device and a copy of everything resident on the frame that wanted a tile. What reserved room costs is its bytes, resident whether or not a mesh is in it:

| Per cluster of the arena | Bytes, rasterized | With the ray tracing chain |
|---|---|---|
| `ClusterDesc` + `ClusterLodDesc` + its material index | 48 + 48 + 4 | the same |
| 64 vertices: 16-bit positions, attributes | 64 × (6 + 8) | + 64 × 12 float positions |
| 124 triangles: packed indices | 124 × 4 | + 124 × 3 8-bit indices |
| **A cluster** | **1,492** | **2,632** |
| **256 MiB holds** | **179,916 clusters** | **101,989 clusters** |

The sum is taken with `sizeof` when the room is laid out (`MeshRoom::cluster_bytes`, logged as `mesh room`), from the load's own `ClusterLodOptions`; the two totals are that log's on an RTX 5090 (2026-11-11). The fixture rock of 1,152 triangles is 24 clusters with its DAG: 31,040 bytes staged, 35,808 reserved. `renderer.meshes.budget_mib` (default 256) is the arena, `renderer.meshes.slots` (4,096) the meshes at once, `renderer.meshes.max_clusters` (4,096) the most one mesh may have, which the chain's per-instance tables are sized by. **Only a scene one of whose generators says its tiles hand meshes reserves it** (`scene_gen::PlacementGeneratorDesc::tile_meshes`, carried as `SceneData::tile_meshes`): every other streamed scene is byte for byte what it was. A **paged** scene (`--stream`) reserves none: its payload is a page pool, and a mesh that arrives there has to arrive as pages (a row left open).

**Admission and retirement** (`SceneRenderer::admit_mesh`, `retire_mesh`; `GpuScene` in `gpu_scene_meshes.cpp`). An admission takes a run of clusters and of materials, writes the mesh's clusters with their offsets moved to the arena, its LOD records, 16-bit positions, attributes and triangles — and with the chain its float positions and 8-bit indices — its clusters' material indices and its materials into the terrain's staging ring, and queues the copies; the next frame's "terrain upload" pass records them, ordered after every frame in flight by the barrier in front of it, and its "record upload" pass writes the mesh's record, before the "pair expand" that reads a new instance's cluster count from it (the pass now declares that read). Nothing waits for the device. A tail handed over after the admission may name the mesh; before it, the tail is **refused by name** (`a mesh slot with no mesh admitted`). A retirement zeroes the record's cluster count and frees the runs at once: the frames in flight that drew it read streams nothing overwrites before a copy that waits for them, exactly as a ring's slot is reused.

**The order rule: nothing drawn depends on the order meshes arrived in.** A visibility id is `pair << 8 | triangle`, and a pair is (instance, cluster *of its mesh*): neither the slot a mesh took nor where its clusters landed in the arena is in it. The mesh's bytes are a function of its recipe (one cache entry, whoever built it), and its clusters are in the order a whole read's merge leaves them (`load_placement_mesh` runs the same leaves-first merge). So two walks that end in the same place hold the same instances of the same bytes, and draw the same depth and colour to the byte; their ids agree once each is read as (instance of the tail, cluster of its mesh, triangle), which `mesh_first_cluster` is for. What *does* depend on arrival is where a tile's block sits in the instance table — as it has since the tail had blocks — and so which of two instances wins an exact tie in depth; compaction lays the blocks out in the tail's order.

**Its textures arrive with it** (R147, 2026-11-11; [texture](texture.md#textures-that-arrive-after-the-load)). A scene with a mesh room keeps one table of built textures by `.tex` build key — the load's, pinned, and the admitted ones with a count of who holds each — and `SceneRenderer::acquire_texture` puts one in without a wait: an image made empty, its levels staged in the terrain's ring, copied by the same "terrain upload" pass that copies the mesh's streams (`gfx::record_image_levels_upload`), into a pair of bindless slots from a run reserved when the scene was made. `admit_mesh` makes the mesh's materials with the function the load makes its own with (`GpuScene::fill_material`: factors, the five slots, the built flags, a sampler per textured slot, the UV transform, the alpha mask), holds a reference on each texture, and `retire_mesh` gives them back; a texture nobody holds leaves the table at once and its image four recorded frames later. A mesh admitted without its textures in the table — refused by the room's pairs (`renderer.textures.slots`, 1,024) or bytes (`renderer.textures.budget_mib`, 1,024), or never built — draws its materials' constants, said once. **Alpha-tested materials** draw their coverage on every rasterizer and the ray path when a generator of the scene said its tiles may hand one (`scene_gen::PlacementGeneratorDesc::tile_meshes_masked`, carried as `SceneData::tile_meshes_masked`), since the masked pipelines are chosen when the scene is made; without it such a material is drawn opaque, by name.

**What does not arrive, yet.** An admitted mesh's **coverage errors** and its **motion contract** (it is rigid). An admitted alpha-tested mesh has no entry in the **opaque shadow proxy's coverage table** and no **opacity micromap**, both baked at load over the load's clusters: its shadow rays test the mask's texel at every candidate, which is the right shadow at the cost the proxy and the micromaps were made to cut ([texture](texture.md#textures-that-arrive-after-the-load), what would give it those). A material that asks for **stochastic sampling** gets it only where the load already has a stochastic material (the resolve's variant is chosen from the load's), else it draws plain, by name. **Cluster templates, static structures and the resident cluster cache**: the chain builds an admitted mesh's clusters per frame, as it builds any mesh that has none of the three; the per-instance tables are sized for it (`rt_max_per_instance_` takes `max_clusters`), and that is all this row asked of the chain.

**What an admission costs.** Staging is a copy of the mesh's bytes on the committing thread; the device's share is the same bytes as buffer copies in a pass that exists anyway. The world's allowance is two meshes and 4 MiB a budgeted commit ([world](world.md#a-tiles-meshes-residency-by-reference)). `mesh_room_tests.cpp` prints a rock's clusters, its staged bytes and what the room reserves for it; `GpuScene::mesh_use()` carries the totals (`staged_bytes`, `admitted`, `retired`) for a host's summary. **Not measured yet**: the p99 frame time along a walk over activating tiles, before and after — it needs a scene whose generator hands meshes drawn by engine-view in `msvc-release`, and the only such generator is the tests' fixture; the first converted solver is where that number is taken (R142's hand-back, "Rows this leaves").

**Tests** (`mesh_room_tests.cpp`): the room's bytes before an admission, with one mesh and after its retirement; a tail naming an empty slot refused; a scene whose rocks arrived one by one against the same scene read whole, and against the same rocks arriving in another order through other slots after one came and went — depth and colour equal to the byte and every id equal as (instance, cluster of its mesh, triangle); the room's refusal naming `renderer.meshes.budget_mib` and changing nothing, a mesh past `max_clusters` refused by name, a scene with no such generator reserving nothing; and an admitted rock on the ray path against the rasterizer, held as the streamed tail's is, casting a traced shadow. `mesh_texture_tests.cpp` holds the textures (R147): textured rocks that arrived one by one against the scene read whole and against another order of arrival, depth, colour and ids to the byte, rasterized and traced, and not the picture their constants draw; a shared texture uploaded once and gone four frames after its last mesh, in bytes, and back without an upload when wanted sooner; both refusals by name; an alpha-tested rock's holes drawn as the whole read draws them, only in a scene told to expect one; what an admission allocates; and a 2K texture's admission timed.

### Authored instances per tile

Roadmap W73 (2026-10-24). **A streamed world's own instances come and go with their tiles too.**
Until this date a scene file's `instances` (and its `scatters`) were the load's prefix whether the
scene streamed or not, so every cluster of every tree was a pair however far it stood, and only a
generator's placements streamed. The full v8 forest — 16,675 file instances of 74 meshes, trees of
1,000 to 12,000 clusters — was refused before its first frame: its 16,680 loaded instances held
28,333,343 pairs and the rings' slots 292,408, 28.6 million against the visibility id's 16,777,216,
and the sentence it got blamed the terrain rings.

**What moves.** When the world streams (`--world` or the file's `world` block) and the registry has
the placement generator `authored` ([authored](authored.md)), `load_scene` hands the file's own
instances to it as the last streamed entry (`engine.scene.AuthoredSet`), in the file's order, each
with its place in that order as a stable id. **What stays in the prefix**, counted in
`SceneData::authored` by why: a host's actor (`AuthoredStreaming::keep`, [below](#an-actor-is-never-streamed)), an instance with an animation block, a skinned or morphed mesh (a
deformed tail instance is refused, above), a mesh that reaches farther from its origin than a tile
edge (`AuthoredStreaming::max_reach_m`, 0 the tile: the landmarks — the v8 forest's two ancients
reach 56 m — so they stay where the scene put them, visible from anywhere, as a landmark must be),
the terrain, and everything in a paged scene (`--stream`), whose forms would need page tables of
their own. `--world-instances whole` keeps them all in the prefix as before.

**A far form per ring, so a far tree is a few pairs.** A tile in ring *r* (r ≥ 1) has its centre at
least ring *r* − 1's radius from the observer once the ring is updated, so every origin on it is
at least `(radius[r − 1] − √2/2 − 1/4) × tile` away — the quarter tile is the camera's way between
two updates, since a tile coming in keeps its outer form until the first update past the boundary
promotes it (8 m at 32 m tiles, 480 m/s at 60 updates a second). For every mesh the entry uses and every ring past the first,
the load cuts a **distance form** at that distance (`geometry::extract_lod_form`,
[geometry](geometry.md#distance-forms)): the clusters the mesh can select from any camera that far,
the frontier's own error zeroed, everything else its own bit for bit — the same spheres, errors,
cone, vertices, attributes, triangles and 16-bit grid — at the session's projection and thresholds
(`AuthoredStreaming`, which engine-view fills from its height, the default 55° field of view,
`--lod`, the foliage threshold and the fade: `authored_rules`). The distance divides by the mesh's
fitted scale and the largest scale among its instances, and counts every sphere's offset from the
origin, so a crown that reaches into a nearer tile is still cut for what its near side can select:
the one rule is "filed by the origin, cut by the origin's nearest". A form that keeps what the ring
inside it kept is that one (the cut only drops more as the distance grows). Each form is a mesh of
its own appended after every other (`SceneData::form_source` names its source), with its source's
fit and materials; the generator's form sets name, per ring, the resident mesh it draws, and a ring
past the last draws the last. Meshes with **no authored levels** benefit too: a decimated spruce's
far form is its coarse levels. **The handover is invisible at the cut's projection**: from at least
the ring's distance the form and the full mesh select the same clusters with the same fade splits,
so a tile moving from ring *r* − 1 to *r* changes no cluster that draws (the cull's choice is the
same formula, `lod_forms_tests.cpp`; the end-to-end handover is engine-view's, below). What the
guarantee does not cover, said plainly: a window taller than the one the forms were cut for, or a
lower `--lod`, draws a form's frontier where the full mesh would have drawn finer — a coarser tree,
never a hole; a tile waiting on the ring's per-update promotion budget draws its outer form until
promoted (engine-view's world on tile ground runs the ring with no budget); and the cross-fade's
dither seeds by the instance slot (R91), so a handover whose tile block is not rewritten in place
(growing back into a larger form) changes which of a fading transition's pixels each side keeps for
the frames that fade lasts. **Streamed trees sway** since W74, in the inner ring's full mesh and in
every form whose ring is within `renderer.flora.sway_m` — cut, then, for the sway's padded spheres
([Streamed trees sway](#streamed-trees-sway)); until then a tail instance had no deform entry and
only the prefix's landmarks moved.

**What it measured** (2026-10-24, RTX 5090, release, offscreen 1600 × 900, `--raster hw --shadows
csm`; the machine was shared with the frame-budget gate's flights and other agents' builds throughout
— `machine_state` 9–55 % of the CPU and up to 100 % of the GPU by others at the starts — so every
time is an upper bound). **The full v8 forest** (the proof of concept's scene as read-only data, its
caches copied to scratch, with a `world` block of 32 m tiles in rings of 1.5, 6 and 40 tiles — 48 m,
192 m, 1,280 m): it initializes. The load streams 16,556 instances and keeps 119 (52 animated, 67
reaching past a tile: the two ancients, the rock sites, the logs), cutting 90 forms of 12,031
clusters; the prefix is 904,053 pairs and the rings' slots 622,008, so the fixed parts are 1.53 M of
the 16.78 M (5.59 M with the ray tracing chain's index space over three runs). At the hardwoods view
the tail is 1,943,164 pairs — ring 0 6 tiles, 20 trees, 45,646 pairs; ring 1 104 tiles, 270 trees,
900,885; ring 2 2,425 tiles, 13,110 trees, 996,633 — and no tile is withheld. Along a 60 s crossing
of the region at 40 m over the ground (1,800 frames, about 75 m/s) the tail peaks at 2.26 M pairs
(14,459 trees, frame 272), no tile is ever withheld, the frame's GPU time is 2.46 ms at the median
and 8.2 ms at p99 (cull 0.15 / 1.96, shadows 1.24 / 3.79), the CPU's 1.1 ms, and the GPU memory
3.6 GiB; the wall time (17.7 ms median, a 5.4 s first frame) is the world's — every ring's tiles and
the drawn ground's built as the flight crosses them. **Ray tracing**: `--shadows rt` and
`--raster rt --shadows rt` are both accepted (7.4 and 7.2 ms of GPU at the median, the chain's
structures 0.9 GB under `--rt-budget-mib 1024`, nothing dropped), where v7's staged scene had
reserved 5,815,332 pairs and a geometry index of 17,445,995. **At the owner's 11520 × 2160**
(`--views surround3`) the forms are cut for a projection 2.4 times larger, so they keep more (85 forms
of 19,465 clusters) and ring 2 holds 1.46 M pairs where 1600 × 900 held 0.40 M at the same place; the
tail is 1.56 M and nothing is withheld. The pair count depends on the resolution only through the
forms; what the resolution costs is the GPU's (14.3 ms median there). **The streamed-forest test
scene** (`content/test-scenes/streamed-forest`, 3,000 trees and an ancient): 284,522 pairs streamed
against 2,910,325 read whole (`--world-instances whole`), 0.62 ms of GPU at the median against 2.81
(the whole read's trees also sway, 0.2 ms of the difference). **The handover** along its path: 1,532
handovers over 1.92 M of their tiles' pixels change **0 pixels** with the cross-fade off, and with
R91's 0.1 change 745 colours and 771 depths in 13 of them — every one a tile coming in from the
outer ring at about 410–440 m, whose larger form no longer fits its block, so its instances take
other slots and the dither's seed with them, exactly the case stated above.

**What is still the load's, and the order it should go in** (2026-10-24, from the startup trace's
measurements of the v7 forest: 15.7 s to ready with the OS cache warm, all on the main thread). The
pairs are per tile now; the **work** is not. (1) Every file instance is still stood on the ground
when the scene file is read (1.8 s warm, 39.6 s cold for v7's 12,330, the tile set's files read one
at a time): a streamed instance's height belongs to its tile's activation — the `authored` set
carrying the file's `ground` and `y` and the generator standing each placement on `Context::ground`
at `tile`, the same millimetre query the reader makes so the whole read and the streamed one stay
equal — and the prefix's kept instances at load. (2) Every mesh of the scene and every image its
materials name are loaded and uploaded whole (6–8.5 s of the load); the residency design (roadmap
W47, W10) is to load the observer's neighbourhood first — the meshes and textures the inner rings'
tiles name, then outward — with a tile withheld until its meshes are resident, as the pair budget
withholds one now. (3) `build_cache_textures` read and hashed every source image once per mesh that
used it, with a job pool made and joined per mesh, and `find_built_textures` did it again — **done**
(W75, [What the load reads](#what-the-load-reads)): one identity per distinct image, a pack's from
its index, a built texture trusted from its header, one pool per load, the meshes on it. (1) and (2)
are stages of their own.

#### An actor is never streamed

Roadmap W78 (2026-10-25). **The instances a host moves stay in the prefix**: a host names them, by
their index in the whole read, in `SceneDesc::authored.keep` before `load_scene`, and the load keeps
them whatever else they are (`AuthoredStats::kept_actors`; an actor is counted there and not as
deformed or far-reaching). engine-view fills it with the game's declared actors (`keep_actors`,
[apps](apps.md#actors-the-characters-a-game-moves)), which are read with the scene file before the
module loads and so before the scene does. **Why**: a game moves, plays and asks after an actor on
every tick, so its entity, its joint run and its row of the instance table must exist from the first
frame to the last, wherever the camera is. A streamed placement exists only while the ring holds its
tile — the ring would stream it out from under the game, and a tail instance has no joints anyway
(a deformed tail instance is refused, above). Today every declared actor has an animation block and
so was kept already by the deformed rule; the set makes the rule the actor's own, so an actor that
stops being "deformed" by that test (a rigid prop a game drives, a skin moved to the tail when R84
lands) still is not streamed by accident.

**What keeping them costs** (2026-10-25, RTX 5090, `msvc-debug` engine-view offscreen at 1600 × 900,
the first 120 frames of `streamed-forest`'s path, two flights each; shared machine, others at 36–49 %
of the CPU and 1–8 % of the GPU, so the GPU numbers are the trustworthy ones): the scene as committed
against the same scene with 52 of the Fox sample walking near the path's first look (the forest
PoC's count, each an instance with an animation block): **+52 loaded instances and +988 pairs** (19
a fox) on 324,319, GPU median 1.313–1.336 ms without them and 1.324–1.329 ms with them, the deform
pass 0.117–0.131 ms either way — within the flights' own spread. Actors are a handful of small
skinned meshes; what a prefix cannot afford is thousands of trees, which is what W73 moved out.

#### The whole read's index

**A streamed load's instance indices are not the file's.** The prefix keeps a subset of the whole
read's instances in their order, so a kept instance's loaded index is its whole-read index minus the
streamed instances before it; the forest PoC's 52 animals, all kept, sat at loaded indices below
their handles, and engine-view's bind looked the handles up among the loaded instances, found
rigid trees or nothing, and the game failed at its first `actor_state` (`forest: actor_state
failed`). **One map, owned by the load**: `SceneData::loaded_of_read`, per instance of the whole read
its loaded index or `k_not_loaded` for one in the tail, built once by `stream_authored` beside W74's
`motion_key` (the whole read's index each kept instance already carries), and empty for a scene read
whole, where the two are the same number. `loaded_instance(scene, read)`, `read_instance(scene,
loaded)` (through the `motion_key`, checked against the map) and `read_instance_count(scene)` are the
only way across. **Every whole-read index user in engine-view goes through it**
([apps](apps.md#actors-the-characters-a-game-moves)): an actor's handle stays the whole read's
index, and its entity, joint run, tier and instance-table row are found once at the bind through the
map; the animated world takes an instance's animation block, its phase (the whole read's index over
the whole read's count), its entity id and its summary row from its whole-read index, so a streamed
world's animation summary and every actor's state are the whole read's to the bit (the actor test in
`game_actors_view_tests.cpp`). A declared actor whose instance is in the tail anyway — a host that did
not name it in `keep` — is refused at the bind by a sentence naming the actor and its instance, never
a silent `NotFound`.

### Streamed trees sway

Roadmap W74 (2026-10-24). **A tree a tile brings sways as the whole read's does.** Until this date a
tail instance was placed with `k_invalid_deform`, so W73's streamed forest stood rigid while its
prefix's landmarks moved: the owner would have seen a forest where only the ancients sway. The rule
now is that a whole read and a streamed read of the same scene draw the same animated picture at the
same world time, and the tests hold it to the pixel.

**A record per resident tree, from its mesh's free list.** A dynamic scene whose meshes the tail may
name carry the motion contract (`GpuScene::flora_tail()`, under `renderer.flora.motion` and
`renderer.flora.tail`) lays out past the load's deform records room for the tail's
(`k_tail_deform_reserve`, 1,024) and past the load's parts room in the pose table
(`k_tail_part_reserve`, 8,192). When `write_slots` writes a slot with an instance of a swaying mesh,
the slot takes a **record** — a deform entry of the flora stage (the mesh's first vertex, a run of
the pose table, its part count) — from that mesh's free list, or makes one past every other; when a
slot is rewritten, nulled, or dropped off the layout's end, its record goes back to its mesh's list.
Why per mesh: a record's entry depends on its mesh alone, so a reused record's entry is already
right and is **never written again**, and a frame in flight that still draws the tree that left
reads what it always read. A new record is written into the deform table in place — the table is
host-visible and mapped for such a scene, and no frame in flight reads an entry that did not exist —
unless it passes the room, when `relayout` (which `SceneRenderer::set_dynamic_instances` runs
before the next frame, as for the stride's growth, and since T152 beside the frames in flight:
[a relayout is swapped in](#a-relayout-is-swapped-in)) makes the deform table, its per-frame copies
and the pose table again, half as much again as the records need. The per-frame copies of a skinned or
morphed prefix are `deform_capacity()` entries a region, and only the load's entries carry morph
weights (`load_deform_count()`). The motion vertex stream already covers every mesh the scene holds,
forms included, so nothing about it changes. **A record another mesh can take.** Per mesh alone, a
world's records were the sum of every mesh's most at once — 15,101 records and 211 MB along the v8
crossing, where 365 trees swayed at its end, because the species change as a flight crosses the
region and each mesh kept the room its own peak took. So a record's run of the pose table is a power
of two of parts (its **class**), a free record is also on its class's list by age, and when a mesh
has none of its own the oldest of its class is taken once `k_joint_slots + 1` frames have been posed
since it was given back — no frame in flight can then draw the tree that held it — and its entry is
rewritten (`FloraStats::tail_repurposed`). The same crossing then made 10,677 records with both rings
swaying and 4,852 with the inner ring alone: the class lists cut it by a third, and what is left is
the peaks of a dense understory, below. **Every record a change moves is given back before any is taken**
(R137): `write_slots` releases the trees of every slot it will write first, then places, so a tree
that leaves one tile and a tree of its mesh that arrives in another share a record whatever order
the layout wrote them in — and the tail's budget counts a commit's records once, exactly, against a
ceiling that follows the device ([below](#a-commit-past-the-tails-budget-withholds-its-farthest-tiles)).

**Every copy of the table holds every record, a skinned scene's too** (T213, 2026-11-22). A record
made or repurposed between frames is written into the table and into all `k_joint_slots` per-frame
copies (`GpuScene::put_deform_record`). Until T213 a skinned scene's copies were left out, because each
skinned frame rewrites its own copy whole from the table before its pool pass; but the accumulation's
motion pool writes each block a second time from **last frame's** copy
([what a layout change costs the accumulation](#what-a-layout-change-costs-the-accumulation),
`MotionPass::previous`), which on a frame that wrote only some slots is trusted. A record new since
then was, in that copy, whatever the buffer held when it was made, and a repurposed one was another
mesh's: the pool read a part run, a vertex base or a surface address of nobody's, through a device
address. On 2026-11-21 the owner's forest, skinned by its player and 416 animals, lost the device
(an SM exception, nvlddmkm 13) on the flight that brought in more trees than had been resident; the
staging flown offscreen is not skinned, kept every copy, and never faulted. `tail budget: a skinned
scene's every copy of the deform table holds the tail's trees` counts the records a copy misses (its
trees times three copies before, none after).

**The phase is the instance's, never its tile's arrival.** A sway's seed is `key * 0x9e3779b9 +
0x632be5ab`, the hash the load always used with the instance's index as the key. A streamed read
gives every instance the key the whole read gives it (`SceneInstance::motion_key`): `stream_authored`
