keeps a landmark's index among the file's instances, and gives the `authored` entry the loaded index
of its id 1 (`StreamedPlacements::motion_key_base`), from which the world's placements consumer sets
a placement's key from its stable id. A tail instance with no id — another generator's — hashes its
position in whole millimetres. A tree whose tile comes back starts at rest in the push and in its
own phase in the wind; so does a tree a compaction moves, which costs a walker's push its ease and
nothing else.

**The pose pass covers the tail.** A tail tree is one more `FloraInstance` after the load's,
removed by the last one taking its place (a pose is a function of the instance alone, so the order
reaches no byte), and `FloraPoser::recut` cuts the chunks again after a change, in place. The pool
pass's per-frame blocks follow the cull's visible list as before, and a swaying tail tree is padded
by its mesh's sway bound and never cone-tested, as a loaded one is. **The pool's budget** for such a
scene is the budget unclamped — 96 MiB under `renderer.flora.pool_mib` — because no load can bound
what the tiles will bring (as the vertex path's index budget already said); a scene with no tail
clamps to its whole meshes exactly as before.

**Which rings sway: the inner ring's full meshes, and a ring's forms when its tiles come within
`renderer.flora.sway_m` (default 0: none).** A ring past the first draws a distance form, cut at the
nearest an origin on its tiles can be. A form sways when that floor is under the range, and is then
**cut for the sway's padded spheres** — from the padding nearer (`stream_authored` measures
`flora_bounds_padding` of the source mesh, the bound the cull pads its instances by, and the form's
instances take the source's padding), so the clusters the cull can choose over it are the full mesh's
swaying ones and the handover stays invisible with the trees moving. Past the range the form is drawn
and cut rigid (`SceneData::form_rigid`). **Why the default keeps the second ring rigid**, although its
sway is visible (at 48 m a frond tip's 0.24 m is five pixels at 900 lines and 55°): in the v8 forest
that ring holds **5,122** swaying plants at the hardwoods view, its understory included, against the
first ring's 261, and took the frame from 8.2 to 9.3 ms of GPU, the posing from 1.1 to 1.8 ms, and the
tail's room from 28 to 153 MB (below). `renderer.flora.sway_m=100` sways it for whoever wants that;
past about 100 m (a pixel is 0.116 m there, about a spray's flutter in a mean wind) no ring should,
and the v8 forest's third ring, from 161 m, holds 13,110 trees.

**What holds it.** `authored_view_tests.cpp`: the scene's 140 trees read whole and streamed in one
ring and in two (the second ring's forms swaying under `renderer.flora.sway_m=100`), thirty frames into the sway, **0 pixels** different
in both, where the sway moves 76 of the whole read's pixels and the tail drawn rigid differs by those
76; and a flight out past the outer ring and back draws, at the same world time, the picture a camera
that never moved draws, to the pixel. `frame_loop_tests.cpp` flies the same trees across two rings
twice and the second flight allocates exactly what it allocates with the tail rigid.

**What it costs** (2026-10-24; RTX 5090, i9-10980XE, `msvc-release` engine-view, offscreen 1600 × 900,
`--raster hw --shadows csm`, `--wait-quiet 120`; GPU total ms median / p95 / p99; `before` is the
same binary with `renderer.flora.tail=false`; the v8 runs are W73's: the proof of concept's scene as
read-only data with its caches copied to scratch, `--deform-pool-mib 64`, wind 0.7. The base is the
gate's d70d34bc, whose G86/G87 trees are heavier than W73's, so the before rows are not W73's 0.62
and 2.46 ms. The machine was shared with other agents' builds; each row's `machine_state`, CPU by
others and GPU busy at the start → the end, says how much, and every time is an upper bound):

| v8 hardwoods, ring 0 (default) | 8.16 / 8.84 / 9.15 | 6.49 | 0.197 | 439 (261) | 1.06 | 28.4 MB | 12% / 5% → 13% / 4% |
| v8 hardwoods, rings 0–1 | 9.32 / 9.97 / 10.41 | 7.47 | 0.315 | 5,300 (5,122) | 1.79 | 153 MB | 24% / 3% → 23% / 84% |

| v8 crossing, ring 0 (default) | 5.66 / 14.03 / 16.87 | 4.05 | 0.111 | 209 (31) at its end | 0.73 | 117 MB | 17% / 4% → 100% / 19% |
| v8 crossing, rings 0–1 | 6.25 / 22.56 / 26.35 | 4.61 | 0.119 | 543 (365) at its end | 1.31 | 254 MB | 37% / 5% → 61% / 58% |

The streamed forest's ring-0 row ran beside a GPU 99% busy at its start, which is why it reads above
the rows that sway more. **Where the time goes**: the shadow cascades, not the pool pass. A swaying
plant is padded and never cone-tested, and every cascade deforms its own copy of its cut, so the
hardwoods' 261 tail plants add 2.0 ms of cascades and 0.13 ms of pool pass; the pose is the CPU's
and runs on the poser's pool (0.5 ms more). The pair count barely moves (the forms cut for the
padding hold 5,877,921 pairs at the hardwoods view against 5,877,845). The tail room is the records'
entries, three slots' part poses (80 bytes each) and the push state, and it keeps the high-water of
the flight: 4,852 records after the crossing for the 31 plants swaying at its end.

**What it does not fix.** (1) The tail's room never shrinks: the crossing ends holding 117 MB for 31
swaying plants with the default, because records are kept for the next tile of their class; a
trim of records free for many frames, or poses in a pool sized by the visible plants rather than the
resident ones, is the next stage. (2) A swaying plant's cascades are most of its cost; a sway LOD
(far or small plants drawn rigid, or their shadows cast from the rest pose) would buy most of it
back. (3) The old 308-allocation second flight, with or without sway, is addressed by W73's
2026-10-26 allocation hunt: tile output scratch and tile instance/tag storage are retained, and
both versions of the test now require zero ([measurement](../experiments/streamed-tree-allocations-2026-10-26.md)).

### The field kind

Roadmap R95 (2026-10-25), G90's engine half. **Grass is posed on the GPU, from the wind at the
blade's root, with no CPU state, no pose table and no tail record.** Until this date a sward patch
was posed as a tree: its 1,040 parentless parts went through the CPU poser every frame, each a run of
the pose table, and a streamed patch took a record of the 2,048-part class — 480 KiB of poses over
the three slots for a three-cluster card. The proof of concept's 126,309-instance sward failed its
commit with `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` and lost the device on it.

**The catalogue says which** (`geometry::FloraMotionKind`, [geometry](geometry.md#flora-species-catalogue-g86)):
`parts` for the trees, `field` for `sward`. A field mesh's `FloraMesh` is built as a tree's (its
padding is the same bound) and marked `field`, and then:

- **One record per mesh, made at load whether or not the load places it**, which every instance of
  the mesh points at — the load's and every tile's (`GpuScene::field_deform_`). Its stage is the
  flora stage with `gfx::k_deform_flora_field`; `joints` is the address of the mesh's run of the
  scene's static blade table (`gfx::FloraFieldPart`: the root, which is the part's pivot, and the
  length, 16 bytes a blade), `joint_count` its blade count and `first_channel` its compliance's bits
  (`channel_count` stays 0, so no morph code reads them). The record is a function of the mesh
  alone, so it is derived rather than allocated: a tile of a meadow costs the tail's room nothing,
  and `acquire_tail_tree` points a grass instance at it and returns.
- **One block a frame** (`gfx::FloraFieldFrame`, 240 bytes; 160 until R152 added the rule of
  [the far field at rest](#the-far-field-at-rest)): the frame's eye, the wind (where it
  blows to and its strength, as the trees read it: the frame's, the ground's record at the sky's
  hour, or the tunables'), the four gust waves' vectors, phases at the eye and shares, the flutter's
  phase, the walker's capsule from the eye, and the rest distance, its fade and the scene's field
  records. It is written at the head of each slot's region of the pose table, three poses' room
  before the address `DeformParams::flora` carries, so a tree's `first_part` did not move and a
  scene of grass alone has a table of 720 bytes.

**What a blade does** (`deform.slang`, `field_vertex`). It bends about its root, across the wind
(the axis `up × to`), by the trees' lean and flutter with the gust read off a field instead of a
clock per tree:

    a = compliance · s · ((0.6 + 0.8 g) + (0.25 + 0.35 g) · sin(φ_f + φ_b)) + push,
    g = clamp(0.5 + 0.5 Σ_j w_j sin(phase_j + k_j · root), 0, 1)

`root` is the blade's root in the frame's space (the instance's offset from the eye, then its 3×3:
ADR-0053), `k_j` four plane waves 20° either side of the wind at two scales, their phases at the eye
reduced in double on the CPU (`renderer::flora_field_frame`), so the GPU adds only the root's offset
from the eye and never holds a world position. The vertex's arc fraction (section 36) scales the
angle and the rotation is about the root, so a straight blade's tip travels as the square of its
fraction — the cantilever's shape — and the root stays put. The axis is taken into the instance's
mesh frame by its 3×3's cofactors. `φ_f` is the frame's flutter phase and `φ_b` the blade's own,
a hash of its root's bits and the instance's placement (its cell and offset): **not** of its part
index, because a distance form prunes and renumbers its parts (below) but copies the roots, so a
card sways in its patch's phases, and whole and streamed reads, which place an instance at the same
bits, give a blade the same phase. Calm and untouched, a blade writes its rest pose to the bit.

**The gust's numbers are the literature's** ([grass-sward.md](../experiments/grass-sward.md#engine-hand-back-field-sway-r95)):
the canopy mixing-layer analogy (Raupach, Finnigan & Brunet 1996; Finnigan 2000) spaces the
coherent eddies at about 8 shear lengths, L_s ≈ h/3 for a dense canopy, and convects them at about
1.8 U(h): a knee-high sward's honami is a 1.4 m wave at 1.8 m/s, the sweeps a 20 m forest edge
sheds over a clearing a 57 m one at 4.5 m/s, and the flutter is the honami's own 1.26 Hz, between
Py et al.'s alfalfa and wheat. The speeds are fixed rather than scaled by the strength: a speed that
followed a varying wind would jump the phase by the change times the clock. **When the wind turns**
the field's wave vectors turn with it about the world's origin, so far from it a change of
direction re-phases the gust (the mean lean does not jump); an advected offset integrated per frame
would fix that and is left.

**The hand-off and the load-in are a term of the same pass** (G136, 2026-11-08; [the hand-off by
distance](#the-hand-off-by-distance)): for an instance with a hand-off role, before the wind, a
part (a blade, or a card's bake group) is kept while an independent stream of the hash its phase
comes from is below the share its role, its root's distance from the eye and its load-in age say,
and every vertex of a part not kept goes to the part's root. It reads the record's band and stamp
and the clock in the field block's `push.w`, about 20 operations and no memory a vertex beyond the
blade the wind already reads, and nothing at all for an instance with no role. A calm, untouched
blade it keeps still writes its rest pose to the bit.

**The walker's push** is a term of the same pass with no history: a blade whose root is within the
capsule's radius, a margin and its own length of the capsule's axis, and within its height, is
turned away from the axis by up to `k_flora_push_max`, most at the capsule's skin. It springs back
the frame the walker leaves: the CPU path's 12-tick ease and a walked track's history
(grass-sward.md, "Engine hand-back for walked tracks") need state this kind deliberately has not.

**What it costs per vertex**: the motion record (4 bytes), the blade (16), the instance's offset
from the eye (once per thread), a 3×3 product for the root, four sines for the gust, one for the
flutter, two integer hashes, the cofactor axis (three cross products), and the rotation's sine and
cosine — about 120 ALU operations and 20 bytes read, against the tree's 4 + 80.

**What it bought** (2026-10-25; RTX 5090, i9-10980XE, `msvc-release` engine-view, offscreen,
`--shadows csm --time-of-day 12`, `--repeat 2 --warmup 60 --wait-quiet 120` (never quiet: other
agents' builds), GPU ms median / p95 / p99; `before` is dcd77811, `after` 7668a437; the meadow is
G90's cooked dense meadow (`dense-meadow`, 1,310 patches in its ring 1 at the path's end, three
edge birches) copied to scratch; `machine_state` is CPU by others / GPU busy at start → end, and
every time is an upper bound):

| Run | GPU total | shadow | pool | resolve | CPU pose ms | parts posed | tail room | shadow pairs | machine_state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| meadow 1920×1080, before | 35.65 / 41.20 / 41.62 | 12.97 | 22.26 | 0.307 | 15.35 | 8,819,377 | 2,616,732,832 B | 370,918 | 18% / 1% → 22% / 16% |
| meadow 1920×1080, after | 1.42 / 1.65 / 1.73 | 0.106 | 0.093 | 0.303 | 0.135 | 177 | 2,146,304 B | 3,526 | 40% / 2% → 53% / 99% |
| meadow 11520×2160, before | 60.06 / 63.46 / 63.85 | 4.45 | 48.09 | 2.652 | 21.24 | 8,819,377 | 2,616,732,832 B | 596,875 | 100% / 1% → 100% / 1% |
| meadow 11520×2160, after | 6.94 / 7.58 / 7.72 | 0.191 | 0.157 | 2.657 | 1.150 | 177 | 2,146,304 B | 10,707 | 100% / 0% → 100% / 1% |
| POC v12 bounded sward 1920×1080, after | 7.58 / 8.17 / 8.38 | 4.60 | 0.438 | 0.37 | 1.20 | 160,883 | 24,226,048 B | 555,373 | 50% / 1% → 32% / 72% |
| POC v12 bounded sward 11520×2160, after | 23.89 / 24.79 / 25.27 | 11.44 | 1.019 | 3.44 | 1.27 | 160,883 | 25,184,512 B | 1,684,604 | 61% / 3% → 26% / 99% |

The tail's room "after" is the birches' reserve: grass takes none (4,514 records before, 0 after),
and the pose table is the three field blocks and the trees' 177 parts, 2,009,040 bytes. A full
dense patch's card took a 2,048-part class, 491,520 bytes of poses over three slots, before; it
takes none now, and its cooked card container keeps 16 of its 1,040 blades (below). The POC's
bounded dense sward (its `world/v12/comparisons/bounded-sward.json` read as data, its terrain cache
copied to scratch, `--raster hw --deform-pool-mib 64`, wind 0.7, the grass-clearing view, 4,067
sward instances) reported 173.2 ms of GPU with 147.8 ms of shadows and 25.5 ms of deformation on
51ef062a in a window; offscreen here it is 7.6 ms, 4.6 and 0.44. Both frame loops allocate the same
(26 frames, 1,180 allocations over the flight, the world's streaming of the placements: W73's,
unchanged by this).

**What holds it.** `authored_view_tests.cpp`: 160 sward patches read whole and streamed in one ring
and in two, thirty frames into the sway, **0 pixels** different, where the field moves 337 of the
whole read's pixels against the rigid picture; a second run of the same frames 0 pixels; the
streamed summary's 160 field instances, 0 tail records, 0 tail bytes and a 720-byte pose table (480
until R152 gave the field block a third pose's room). The
tree tests (`flora_scene_tests`, `flora_motion_tests`, the authored sway, return and handover
cases) draw what they drew.

### The hand-off by distance

Roadmap G136 (2026-11-08; the owner's v36 walk: "grass's LOD shifts are incredibly drastic", "the
grass load in is abrupt too"). Until this date a sward patch was its near form in the world's inner
ring and its card in the next, so the change from blades to cards was a straight line along a 64 m
tile's edge, a few metres to a few tens of metres out, that jumped as the walker crossed a tile,
with no blend, and a tile that came into the inner ring put its blades in the picture in one
frame. **Now the two forms hand over across a band of distance from the eye, and a tile's blades
fade in.**

- **Both forms near the camera.** The sward placement puts a patch's near form *and* its card in
  the inner ring, the near form named `scene_gen::k_handoff_near` and the card `k_handoff_far`
  (`Placement::handoff`, carried by `SceneInstance::handoff`); the next ring places the card alone,
  with no role, and the rings past it nothing, as before ([flora](flora.md#grass-sward-g90)).
- **A band per instance.** An instance with a role carries it in `InstanceDesc::flags` bits 8-9
  and the band `[from, to)` in the record's last spare word (`InstanceDesc::band`, centimetres in
  two halves; `gfx::pack_handoff_band`), set when the instance is placed from
  `renderer.flora.sward_near_m` (25 m) and `renderer.flora.sward_fade_m` (8 m): `[21, 29)` m by
  default. The record is still 96 bytes.
- **The cull pass draws each form only on its side** (`cluster_cull.slang`, `handoff_outside` in
  `scene.slang`): a near form's pair whose sphere lies wholly at or past `to`, and a far form's
  wholly short of `from`, are dropped — one compare a pair, against the sphere every other test
  uses, measured from the view's eye (the camera's in a cascade's run, where the LOD is measured
  from). A pair it drops is one whose every part the pool pass would collapse, so it is a cut and
  not a picture change; every rasterizer and the ray path read the same cull output, so they draw
  the same hand-off.
- **Inside the band the near form thins by blade and the card thickens by bake group**
  (`deform.slang`, `field_vertex`; `handoff_keep`): a part is kept while an independent stream of
  its existing phase hash (its root's bits and its instance's placement) is below the share —
  `(to − d) / (to − from)` for the near form, `(d − from) / (to − from)` for the card, `d` the
  part's root's distance from the eye — and a part not kept has every vertex moved to its root:
  zero area, met by no rasterizer and no ray. Between them the two forms keep the whole patch at
  every distance; the coverage is continuous because the card is fit to the near form's coverage
  (flora.md; the elevations are measured in [grass-sward.md](../experiments/grass-sward.md#coverage-against-elevation-g136)).
  A card is thinned by its part, a bake group's three cards (16 a square metre), so the card's
  mask and its cutoff are untouched: the alpha test every path shares (`alpha_mask.slang`) and the
  opacity micromaps baked from it read the material alone.
- **The load-in** (`flags` bits 10-31, the stamp): a tail block's instances carry the frame count
  (`GpuScene::handoff_tick`, the flora frames, modulo 2^22) of the change that wrote them, kept by
  the block's key while the caller's version stands, so a compaction or a move keeps a block's age;
  the first fill stamps 0 and is never faded. For `k_handoff_ramp_frames` (30) frames after its
  stamp a near form's share is scaled up from zero and a far form keeps every part at any distance
  (the cull pass ignores its `from` while it is young; `CullParams::handoff_tick`), so a tile that
  moves into the inner ring fades its blades in over the cards it already drew. A card alone (the
  next ring) has no role and no stamp: it arrives at the ring's outer edge, 150 m or more out, as before. The pool pass reads the clock from the field block's
  `push.w`.
- **A part of a tile is as old as the tile** (G205, 2026-11-15; `DynamicBlock::age_of`,
  `GpuScene::block_stamp`). The world's placements consumer hands a tile's near forms apart from
  the tile, by cells, and only the cells the band can reach
  ([world](world.md#a-hand-off-placement-is-held-by-its-band)), so a near form past the band holds
  no pair. A cell's block names its tile's, and a block that names another takes the stamp that
  one holds: a cell that comes into reach as the walker moves is not faded in (its tile's load-in
  is long over, and its blades are past the band's end, where their share is nothing), and one
  that comes with its tile fades in with it, since the tile's block is handed, and stamped, first.

**What it does not do.** The pool pass is what thins: an entry the deformed-vertex pool's budget
had no block for, or a frame with the flora motion off, draws both forms whole across the band (8 m
of doubled cover). **The shadow is one of those**: the nearest cascade casts the sward at its rest
pose, with no pool block for its entries (the caster policy), so inside the band it casts both
forms whole — the cull pass's band still bounds each form's casters to its side, so the doubled
shadow is the band's 8 m and no wider. A tile that leaves
the inner ring loses its near form in one frame; where the inner ring reaches past `to` that is
nothing the picture showed. **The inner ring must reach past the band's end**: a tile is in a ring
by its centre's distance, so a ring of radius `r` tiles reaches `64 r − 45.3` m at the least, and
where it does not the near form ends at the ring's edge as it did before (the v36 scene's inner
ring is 0.75 tiles: 2.7 m at a tile's corner). G136's report asks the scene for 1.2 tiles.

**What it costs** (2026-11-09, RTX 5090, msvc-release, the v36 scene with the common flags,
`--raster hw --shadows rt`, 1920×1080; a 60 m walk through the meadow by the lake, 10 s at 1.65 m
over 600 frames, `--benchmark` after 30 frames of warm-up, the same checkout at eeb8077c and at
e1979250 against one derived-data cache). The "before" run was quiet (other processes 9% of the
CPU, the GPU lock held); the "after" run was not (`quiet: false`, 17 to 21% of the CPU others'),
so its times are an upper bound:

| | before (by tile) | after (by distance) |
|---|---|---|
| frame GPU ms, median / p95 | 11.03 / 12.37 | 10.22 / 11.59 |
| cull pass ms, median / p95 | 0.548 / 0.551 | 0.540 / 0.546 |
| pool pass (`deform`) ms | 1.344 / 1.546 | 1.175 / 1.296 |
| hardware rasterizer ms | 2.346 / 2.595 | 2.091 / 2.307 |
| inner ring's instances / pairs | 7,547 / 1,921,631 | 15,063 / 1,944,179 |
| field instances (`flora.field_instances`) | 15,924 | 23,440 |
| tiles withheld (`tail_withheld_tiles`; the world's `ring_withheld`) | 0 (0, 0, 0, 884) | 0 (0, 0, 0, 884) |

The band test costs the cull pass nothing measurable, and the frame is cheaper: inside the band the
pool pass writes fewer moving vertices (a collapsed blade returns before its sway) and the
rasterizer meets zero-area triangles where it drew blades. The cards in the inner ring add 7,516
instances and 22,548 pairs (three a card) to a tail of 15.4 million, and withheld no tile at
1080p. Along the walk the sward's pixels are the same within 0.4% in every frame, and its share of
every twelfth of the picture's rows the same except the one at the horizon, which is 0.1 to 1.7
points lower (the card's 91% of the near form's coverage at a grazing view, where the card now
draws what the near form drew): no new density edge. The sward's frame-to-frame steps are the
same before and after (median 1.0%, the largest 9.7%, all at the walk's end where it leaves the
meadow: the camera's own motion). What changed is the hand-over: before it, the cards' pixels fell
by 8.5% and 5.6% of the sward's in one quarter-second step each (frames 29 and 494, the near
form's tile edge passing under the camera, the near form taking the same pixels at once); after it,
no step of the cards' pixels is larger than 2.0% of the sward's.

**The band seen.** v36's inner ring (0.75 tiles) stops short of the band, so the walk above shows
the near form ending at the ring's edge where it did before, only without the jump. The same walk
with the scene's `world.rings[0].radius` set to 1.25 tiles (one copy of the scene, nothing else
changed; the capture run, not the benchmark) shows the hand-off itself: the meadow reads as one
sward to the treeline with no line of density at 21 to 29 m, the cards' largest frame-to-frame step
is 0.37% of the sward's pixels (none over 2%), and the sward's own steps are the camera's (the
same 1.0% median and 9.8% largest, at the walk's end). The wider ring costs pairs, not frame
time: 7 inner tiles instead of 2, 28,363 instances and 3,897,508 pairs in the inner ring instead
of 15,063 and 1,944,179, with the next ring shrinking to match (24 tiles instead of 29), so the
tail as a whole is 15,373,825 pairs against 15,382,329; no tile was withheld at 1080p (926
placements of the outermost ring against 884). The defaults (25 m, 8 m) were kept: the walk's
frames read as blades well past the band and show no line where the band lies.

### The far field at rest

Roadmap R152 (2026-11-13). **Past `renderer.flora.field_rest_m` (120 m) a field does not sway, takes
no pool block, and in the ray tracing chain references its mesh's resident structures.** On the
owner's walk of the forest at 3840 × 2160 with traced primaries one view wanted 618,793 cluster
structures of a budget of 338,072 and dropped whole instances' structures for three seconds; the
census of that place ([the experiment](../experiments/rt-chain-walk-2026-11-12.md)) found nine
tenths of what a frame builds there to be the sward, two thirds of it 80 to 192 m away. It is built
every frame for one reason: it sways, so its positions are the pool's and its structures the
frame's own. This is a change to the picture, said plainly: **far grass stands still**. It is not
a cull, and nothing is dropped.

**How an instance comes to deform, and what the chain does with each kind.** `InstanceDesc::deform`
is set when an instance is placed: a skinned, morphed or `--deform` instance and every terrain level
get a record of their own at load; a swaying tree gets one per instance (the load's, or a tail
record from its mesh's free list, in the rings `renderer.flora.sway_m` reaches: the inner ring by
default); a **field** instance (the sward: `geometry::FloraMotionKind::field`) points at its mesh's
one shared record in **every** ring, the load's and every tile's (`acquire_tail_tree`), because the
record costs nothing. The chain then does one of five things with an instance's visible entries
(`GpuScene::rt_instance_kind`): a deformed one is built this frame from its pool blocks; an
untraced one (the sward's caster policy) is built this frame too, drawn entries only, where the
picture is traced; a rigid one of a mesh the cache keeps **references the cache** (its clusters'
structures are built once, the first frame any instance draws them, and addressed after); a rigid
distance form's structure is **built once** at load for its fixed cut; and a rigid instance the
cache does not serve is built this frame. "References the cache" needs an instance whose every
copy traces the same clusters at the same positions: rigid, of a mesh of the scene's own, not a
static form. "Built once" needs a fixed cut, which only a distance form has. A far sward card is
neither while it sways, and at rest it is the first.

**The rule.** A blade's share of the wind is 1 short of the band, falls linearly over
`renderer.flora.field_rest_fade_m` (40 m), and is 0 from `gfx::k_field_rest_margin_m` (0.25 m)
short of the distance on (`field_fade`, `deform.slang`'s `field_vertex`): the wind's angle is
multiplied by it, measured at the blade's root from the frame's eye, so a blade past the distance
has no angle and the pool pass returns its rest position off the grid, **to the bit** (the path
a calm frame takes). **No state changes at the boundary**: the last frame the pool poses a blade
in, the pose is the rest pose. An instance **rests** when it is a field's (its deform entry lies in
the scene's run of field records, made together at load) and its every root is at least the
distance from the eye — its origin's distance less the scene's largest root offset times its scale
(`gfx::field_rests`, `field_rest.slang`, the CPU mirror in `gfx/flora_motion.h`). Never a hand-off's
near form (past its band it draws nothing, which is not its rest pose), a hand-off's far form only
past its band's end (inside it the pass thins it by part), and never an instance the walker's
capsule can reach, whose blades it bends wherever the eye is. The rule's numbers ride in the
frame's field block (`gfx::FloraFieldFrame`, 240 bytes since: the distance, one over the band, the
roots' reach, the walker's reach and the field records' run), which already held the eye and the
walker; three passes read it:

- **the pool's allocator** (`deform_alloc.slang`, `DeformAllocParams::field`), on the camera's and
  the cascades' dispatches alike: an entry of an instance at rest asks for no block, so
  `deform_base` answers `k_no_pool_slot` for it and **every position reader draws it from the
  grid** — the three rasterizers, the resolve's reconstruction, the ray path — by the rule they
  already follow for a rigid instance, a frame with no pool and an entry the budget refused. The
  pool pass walks the blocks, so it does not run for the instance at all;
- **the pool pass** (`deform.slang`), for the fade;
- **the chain's records** (`clas_records.slang`, `ClusterRecordParams::field`): `instance_cached`
  answers true for an instance at rest, untraced or not, so its drawn entries (and its casters,
  where its species casts) take the cache's path — a reference each, a structure a distinct
  cluster built once from the rest-pose floats, the same floats an own record of an entry with no
  block names — and the frame builds none of them. Asked with the frame's eye, so an instance
  stops being cached the frame it comes inside the distance and is cached again the frame it
  leaves; the cache's slots are stamped by the frames that reference them, as for any instance.

**Why its own radius and not a ring's edge.** A ring is a set of tiles by their centres' distance:
the second ring begins 35 m from the eye at a tile's corner and ends 237 m away at another's, so a
rule by ring either stills grass 35 m away, where its sway is two to four pixels, or leaves the
second ring's 89,000 structures a frame as they are. A radius from the eye is the measure the sway's size
has, costs the instance table nothing (no slot is rewritten as the eye moves), and lets the fade be
by the blade.

**What sets the distance.** The sway's size in pixels at 3840 × 2160 and 55° (a pixel is 0.48 mm
a metre of distance: 3.9 cm at 80 m, 5.8 cm at 120 m, 9.3 cm at 192 m). At the forest's wind (0.7)
a blade's tip leans 0.084 to 0.196 rad with the gust and flutters ±0.035 to ±0.084 rad at 1.26 Hz
(the sward's compliance 0.20; `field_vertex`), so a 0.4 m blade's tip travels 2.8 to 6.7 cm peak
to peak in the flutter — 0.7 to 1.7 pixels at 80 m, 0.5 to 1.2 at 120 m — and its middle a quarter
of that. The band begins where the typical tip still moves a pixel and ends where it would move
half of one; [the measurement](../experiments/rt-chain-walk-2026-11-12.md#the-far-field-at-rest)
has what the picture lost on the forest.

**What the readers were checked for.** The cull pass is untouched: an instance at rest is still
padded by its sway bound and never cone-tested (its `deform` word still names its record), so the
cut — and with it the visible list, the ids and the raster's work — is the cut with the rule off;
a sward card is two-sided and its cones would cull nothing a rigid test could use. The cascades
already drew the sward at rest (the caster policy's `rest_pose`). The cache's structure and the
frame's own structure of a resting entry are built from the same floats, so a hit's position does
not move when an instance changes path; against a *posed* entry of the frame before, the pool's
positions are the 16-bit grid's and the cache's the floats', which differ by under a grid step (tens
of micrometres on a patch), as they do for every rigid instance beside a deformed one.

**What turns the cache's passes on.** `rt_cache_instances()` counts the instances the cache serves
when the instances change; which field instances rest is the frame's eye's to say, so a frame of a
scene with field instances and the rule on records the cache's passes too (`record_frame`), idle
when nothing rests. A scene read whole whose only servable instances are a field's now gets a
cache (`create_rt_cache`).

**What it does not do.** The first capacities are still estimated with every field pair in the
frame's own set (`rt_frame_estimate`), so a scene starts with more capacity than the rule needs,
and the references' capacity grows by its policy as the first frames reference more than the
estimate. A field instance's blades inside the band still take a block and an own structure: at
the forest's worst place that is the sward to 120 m. The far *trees* were already rigid forms.
`renderer.flora.field_rest_m=0` is the sward's picture and its builds as they were (an untraced
rigid instance still references the cache under a traced picture: [the caster
policy](#the-caster-policy)).

**What it costs and gives** ([the pair at the worst place](../experiments/rt-chain-walk-2026-11-12.md#the-pair-at-the-worst-place);
the forest's staging copy at 3840 × 2160, traced, with the bounce, main against this back to back):
the frame's own structures 130,264 → 77,152 at the most and 88,348 → 39,967 at the median, the
references 61,190 → 99,455, the chain 2.79 → 1.88 ms, the cluster builds 1.85 → 0.95 ms, the frame
17.06 → 15.66 ms, with the visible list and the casters the same to the entry in every frame. On a
held view of that place 1.51% of the picture's pixels, the sward past 120 m, stop moving
([what the picture lost](../experiments/rt-chain-walk-2026-11-12.md#what-the-picture-lost)).

**What holds it.** `field_rest_tests.cpp`: the fade and the predicate on the CPU (whole short of
the band, nothing from the margin, never rising, a centimetre at a time; the roots' reach, the
records' run, the hand-off's two roles, the walker); and on a row of nine sward patches from 6.4
to 20.6 m with the rule at 15 m over 3 m, on the hardware rasterizer and the ray path: a patch
wholly short of the band is the rule-off picture to the id and the depth's bits, one wholly past
the distance the calm picture's (to the bit on the rasterizer; on the ray path to the id, with the
depth within 3.6e-6, the floats against the grid), fewer entries take a block (72 → 48), and on the ray path the structures the
frame builds and the references add up to the rule-off frame's builds, nothing wanted is unbuilt,
and the picture is byte for byte the one drawn with `renderer.rt.cache=false`, the per-frame build
of the same poses.

### A swaying mesh's form by ring

Roadmap G204 (2026-11-14). **A mesh that sways takes its forms by ring as a rigid one does: a cut
of its DAG that still sways where its motion is seen, and a cut that stands still where it is
not.** [The ring-form rule](#a-placements-form-by-ring) left every swaying mesh as itself in every
ring, since a form that is not posed is not the mesh; after it the forest's tail was held by plants
that sway, the understory's ferns at 64 and 33 pairs an instance out to the last ring among them.
But a mesh's motion has a size, and past a distance that size is under a pixel.

**The measure** (`sway_forms.h`, `measure_sway`): the farthest any vertex of the mesh leaves its
rest position, in metres at placement scale 1, under the wind the session draws it in. It is the
bound the cull already pads a swaying instance's spheres by (`flora_bounds_padding`: every part's
most turn times each vertex's distance from the pivots of its chain), taken at the rule's wind
instead of the strongest (since W154 the bound follows the storm's law and the bend's cap, so it is
measured again at that wind, not scaled from the strongest). The wind is the session's
(`renderer.flora.wind_strength`), or `renderer.forms.still_wind` when a host says another: a
session whose frames name stronger winds than its tunable (a ground with a wind record, a game's
storm) sets it to the strongest it draws, or to 8.4 (42 m/s, `k_flora_max_wind`) for every wind. The measure reads the motion
contract as the flora stage reads it (`flora_mesh`), never a recipe.

**The rule** (`still_scale`, asked per ring by `make_placement_forms`). Seen from a ring's floor or
farther, a placement of the mesh stands still when

- its reach there is under `renderer.forms.still_px` (1) pixels at the session's projection
  (`AuthoredStreaming::proj_scale`, the projection the cuts and `min_px` use: at the owner's
  3840 × 2160 and 55° a pixel is 0.48 mm a metre of distance); or
- it is a field (the sward's kind) and the ring's floor lies past
  [the far field's rest distance](#the-far-field-at-rest) by its roots' reach: there the mesh is
  drawn at rest already, to the bit, so a form with no pose is the same picture.

**Why one pixel of reach.** The reach is the whole offset between a pose and the rest pose, so it
bounds what a hand-over to a still form can show; the sway about its mean lean is half of it (a
part turns between 0.6 and 1.4 of its lean with the gust, and flutters by at most 0.6 of it), so
under one pixel of reach nothing travels more than half a pixel about where it stands.

**Why this is not the far field's number.** [The far field's rest](#the-far-field-at-rest) is the
engine's other rule for where a plant stops swaying, and in this rule's measure it stops grass at a
reach of two pixels (a 0.4 m blade at 120 m and the forest's wind: 11 cm against 5.8 cm a pixel).
The two are kept apart because they promise different things. The far field's is **a loss its page
names and measured**: the sway ends where a typical tip still travels half a pixel to a pixel in
its flutter, and the motion of 1.5% of the worst view's pixels went with it. It can stop there
because nothing happens at its boundary: the sway fades by the blade over the 40 m before, so the
last frame a blade is posed in, its pose is the rest pose, and the lean the gust holds a blade at
is never dropped, only faded. A ring's hand-over drops the pose whole, a tile at a time: what can
show is the whole reach, the lean included, and a still tile beside a swaying one. This rule's
promise is **no visible change**, so it holds that whole offset under a pixel. On the engine
scene's walk two pixels stills the creeping fern a ring nearer, and a hand-over between the second
and third rings, which changed no value at one pixel, changes 29 of its tile's 641; what the
second pixel buys is in the measurements below, and `renderer.forms.still_px=2` is the far field's
trade for an operator who wants it here. **The answer is a scale**:
`still_scale` gives the largest placement scale that stands still from the floor. A ring has one
form, so its form stands still when that scale covers every placement a ring's cut serves
(`renderer.forms.cut_scale`, 1.5): no placement drawn still moves more than the rule's pixel, and
a ring where only the smaller placements would stand still keeps its swaying cut for all of them.

**The forms** (`make_placement_forms`, with a rigid mesh's). A swaying subject's cut for a ring is
cut for the sway's padded spheres, as an authored tree's swaying form is
([streamed trees sway](#streamed-trees-sway)): from the ring's floor less the padding, so what the
cull can choose over it from the ring is what it chooses over the mesh.

- **A swaying cut**, in a ring where the motion is seen: it keeps its motion records, its part
  table pruned to the parts it uses with their source ids (so it sways in its source's phase), and
  is drawn as a tail's tree or a field's instance is. It costs the pairs of the cut, and a pose
  record of the pruned table's class.
- **A still cut**, from the first ring that stands still outward: the same cut with no motion
  contract, so the frame builds nothing for it — no pose record, no pool block, and in the ray
  tracing chain its clusters reference the resident cache's structures like any rigid mesh's
  ([the kinds](#the-far-field-at-rest)). Its instances keep the source's padding
  (`SceneData::still_padding`, added by `make_instance`), so the cull's choice over a still
  instance is exactly its choice over the swaying one.
- **Never a static form** (`form_rigid` stays 0), whatever its caster policy: a static form draws
  its frontier at every distance, which is not what its swaying neighbour ring draws, and the
  hand-over between the two is the one place this rule can be seen. The cache gives a rigid tail
  instance its structures built once without the fixed cut.
- A form the mesh **offers** (G198's) is rigid, so it is weighed only in the rings that stand
  still. Under `renderer.forms.min_px` a swaying placement is drawn as nothing, as a rigid one is.

**The hand-over.** Between the mesh and a swaying cut, and between two swaying cuts: no pixel, by
the cut's rule and the shared phase. Into a still cut of a field past its rest distance: no pixel
either, both sides drawing the rest pose over the same choice of clusters. Into a still cut by
size: the pose is dropped, an offset under `still_px` at the ring's floor for the largest placement
it serves, and nothing else changes; the tile's hand-over cross-fades it like any other. Under the
cascades a still form casts its rest pose, where its swaying neighbour cast its pose unless its
policy already said rest.

**What decides where a plant stops swaying.** For a field, the rest distance does, by the blade
and with its fade, and this rule only follows it: a ring wholly past the distance takes a form
that says what is already drawn. For a mesh posed by parts there is no rest distance, and this
rule decides, by ring and by the placement's size. `renderer.forms.sway=false` leaves every
swaying mesh as itself in every ring, as before; `renderer.forms.still_px=0` keeps the swaying
cuts and stills nothing by size.

**What an imported plant gets, and what a scene with none costs.** A plant whose container carries
the motion contract and that the flora stage sways is measured and formed by this rule, whoever
made it. One the stage draws rigid — no contract, a contract that does not cover its vertices, or
a kind the stage does not know: the compliance a part bends by still comes from
`geometry::k_flora_species`, a closed list keyed by the container's generator kind, so an imported
plant's contract sways only under one of its names — is a rigid mesh to the rule and is formed as
one. A mesh that deforms any other way (a skin, morphs) keeps itself in every ring. A scene with
no swaying subject makes no form and pays one `flora_mesh` a mesh that carries the contract, at
the load.

**What the rule does not reach.** Ring 0, whose floor is the eye: the sward's near forms there are
drawn only inside the hand-off's band (29 m) but are placed, and counted as pairs, over the whole
of the ring's tiles; a still form cannot help what is under the walker's feet, and the count is a
row of its own (G205: [the world's placements hand a tile's near forms by the cells the band
reaches](world.md#a-hand-off-placement-is-held-by-its-band)). A placement that carries a hand-off
role must keep the mesh itself: its thinning is the pool pass's, which a still form does not run;
since G205 the consumer passes such a placement by when it picks a ring's form.

**Measured** (2026-11-14, `msvc-release`, main ae9efac5 against this, one tree; the machine shared
with a dozen agents' builds and GPU work at 85 to 100% of the CPU, so the times are upper bounds
and the counts are counts). A 2 km ridge streamed on the forest staging's tiles and inner rings
(64 m; radii 1.25, 3, 10 and 14 tiles: floors 18.75, 130.7 and 578.7 m) under a sward at whole
density (two tall-sod patches of 277 and 279 clusters, their cards 3) and a scatter of the engine's
arching fern (0.9 m fronds, 112 clusters) and creeping fern (60) at the staging's density, 50 a
tile, at the forest's wind (0.7). At 3840 × 2160 with traced primaries and shadows and the bounce,
from one place on the flank:

| ring | pairs, before | pairs, after | what changed |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 4,240,812 | 4,240,812 | nothing: the sward's near forms, 4,176,362 of it |
| 1 | 419,531 | 419,531 | nothing: a cut from 12 m keeps every cluster of both ferns |
| 2 | 1,323,760 | 661,880 | swaying cuts: the arching fern 112 → 56, the creeping 60 → 30 |
| 3 | 1,274,740 | 637,370 | the arching fern its swaying cut (56), the creeping its still cut (30) |
| tail | 7,258,843 | 5,959,593 | the ferns 2,744,588 → 1,445,338; the sward 4,514,255 in both |

The ferns halve and no more because their DAGs end there: the cut from 386 m keeps the clusters
the cut from 87 m keeps, 56 and 30 of them for a plant three pixels tall — the fern's own coarsest
level, which a cut cannot go under and a far form of its own would (a row; G198's offered forms
are weighed in the still rings already). By the rule at one pixel the creeping fern stands still in
the fourth ring and the arching one does not (the load's answers bound their reaches there: under
0.67 px and between 0.67 and 1.33 px at their own size; a 0.9 m frond at the leaf's compliance
works out at about one): swaying instances 29,416 → 24,541 and their pose table 161.6 → 134.8
MiB. **At two pixels** (`renderer.forms.still_px=2`, the far field's own measure) both stand still
there: 15,771 swaying instances, 86.6 MiB. The two captures differ in 177 of 8,294,400 pixels, by
at most 4 of 255, all in the band of the picture where the fourth ring lies.

**The frame**, like for like on the ferns alone (the same scene without its sward, whose blades
inside the rest distance otherwise fill the chain's budget of 338,072 cluster structures in both
binaries and hide everything else), a 140 m walk at 4.5 m/s, 1920 × 1080, traced shadows: the
GPU's frame 10.16 → 6.23 ms median, the chain's cluster builds 6.05 → 3.49, `rt` 6.99 → 4.17, the
pool's pass 2.09 → 0.80, the cull 0.080 → 0.051 (pairs 3,142,460 → 1,631,736), the frame's CPU
3.75 → 2.43 ms. On the whole scene's 10 s flight at 3840 × 2160 the frame is the sward's: 20.12 →
19.84 ms at one pixel, the chain still at its budget. **At two pixels** the arching ferns of the
fourth ring leave the chain and it comes under its budget: the frame 17.08 ms, the cluster builds
6.32 → 4.71, `rt` 8.09 → 5.97, the pool's pass 2.00 → 1.13, the frame's CPU 3.60 → 1.94 ms, the
posing 1.3 ms a frame. So what one pixel of strictness costs on this scene is 2.8 ms of a 4K frame,
for a sway of a plant three pixels tall; the default stays at one pixel, the rule as it was asked
for, and the lever is the operator's.

**The hand-overs** on that walk (the handover pass, the cross-fade off, traced shadows and again
with the cascades: the same counts): 81 ring changes of occupied tiles. The 31 between the mesh
and a swaying cut, in the wind, changed no pixel. Of the 50 between the swaying cut and the still
one, the 8 outward lay behind the walker and the 42 inward changed 103 values over their tiles
(10 of coverage, 58 of depth, 35 of colour; 21 in the worst), two or three a tile 600 m away: the
creeping ferns' poses coming back. `sway_forms_view_tests.cpp` holds the two exact cases: at rest,
and between swaying cuts in the wind, no pixel.

### The caster policy

Also R95. **Per species: in the ray tracing chain at all, how many of the sun's nearest cascades,
and whether a cascade draws its rest pose** (`geometry::FloraCasterPolicy`). The renderer turns the
policy into `InstanceDesc::flags` bits 2–6 per mesh at load (`GpuScene::mesh_policy_`, the species
the generator section names, a distance form's its source's) and ORs them into every instance of
the mesh, the load's and every tile's (`write_slots`): bits 2–4 hold `n + 1` for "the `n` nearest
cascades", bit 5 `k_instance_shadow_rest`, bit 6 `k_instance_untraced`; a species with the trees'
defaults sets none, so every existing scene's instances are the bytes they were.

- **The cascades.** Each cascade's cull block names its cascade (`CullParams::cascade`, c + 1;
  0 on a camera run), and the cull drops a pair of an instance whose species casts into fewer
  cascades before it reads the cluster. With `rest_pose`, the cascades' pool allocation
  (`deform_alloc.slang`, `DeformAllocParams::rest_beyond_m` ≥ 0 on that dispatch) gives the
  instance's entries no block, so the cascade draws it from the grid (`k_no_pool_slot`) and the pool
  pass bends it once, for the picture. The sward is `{false, 1, true}`: one cascade, at rest.
- **The chain: two contracts** (R110, 2026-10-28). `traced = false` means **no light's ray meets
  the instance** — its cost in the chain, its self-shadowing noise — and nothing about whether it
  is drawn. Until R110 it was implemented as "not in the chain", which under `--raster rt`, where
  the structures *are* the picture, meant not drawn at all: the proof of concept's v20 grass was
  absent from the ray path in an isolated grass-only scene with no drop and no overflow
  (`reports/quality-v20/ENGINE-AND-ASSET-ROADMAP.md`). Now the instance takes part as a caster
  never and as drawn geometry wherever camera rays trace the chain:
  - **A rasterized picture with traced shadows** (`--raster hw|sw|vertex --shadows rt`): exactly
    as before. The cull writes no caster entry for it, and `clas_records.slang`'s `records_main`
    leaves its drawn entries out before they are counted — no record, no slot, no count, no
    structure — so the grass costs the chain nothing and the records are the bytes they were.
  - **A traced picture** (`--raster rt`, and the reference renderer's frame, `FrameDesc::
    rt_complete`, whose path tracer's first ray is a camera ray): the records pass is told so
    (`gfx::k_cluster_records_untraced_drawn` in `ClusterRecordParams::mode`) and builds the
    instance's **drawn** entries as any instance's, from their pool blocks when it is deformed (the
    sward is a field kind posed on the GPU), never its casters. Until R152 the cluster cache never
    served it, so even a rigid one's entries were built per frame — the forest's litter, rigid and
    untraced, was most of what the owner's worst view built; **since R152 a rigid untraced
    instance references the cache in such a frame like any rigid instance** (`instance_cached` in
    the shader, `rt_instance_cached` on the CPU by the scene's path), and so does a field instance
    [at rest](#the-far-field-at-rest): the cache's structure is every instance's of its mesh, and
    what keeps a light off an untraced one is its own record's mask, below. The primary rays draw
    it exactly where the rasterizers draw it,
    and the resolve decodes its pixels through `hit_visible_entry` and `pair_entries` unchanged.
  - **No light's ray meets it, in either**: its top-level record's mask has no caster bit
    (`gfx::instance_ray_mask`, written every frame by `tlas_references.slang`), and the resolve's
    shadow rays and the reference path tracer's shadow rays and bounces trace with the caster bit
    alone ([gfx](gfx.md#the-ray-mask)). The path tracer treats it as the resolve does — lit, and
    never shadowing, occluding or reflecting onto anything — so the two still agree under the flag.
  A static form of an untraced species is built once and referenced as every static form is; the
  mask keeps light off it too, which the old filter did not (a static structure never passed
  through `records_main`).
- **The trees' sway LOD** falls out of the same switch: `renderer.flora.rest_pose_cascades_m`
  (default 0, off) is a distance past which every deformed instance but a terrain level casts its
  rest pose into the cascades — its entries in the cascades' runs take no pool block (until R103
  the terrain's rings too, which drew their rest heights there). Since R103 the cascades also put
  an instance at rest per cascade by its reach against the cascade's texel ([Cascaded shadow
  maps](#cascaded-shadow-maps), "Far casters at rest, per cascade"). Measured at the POC v12
  bounded scene's hardwoods view (1600 × 900, the same build and flags as the table above, 1,090
  swaying plants): GPU total 3.83 / 3.30 ms at 0 (off) / 100 m and the pool pass 0.097 / 0.093 ms,
  with the 50 m run (6.00 ms) taken beside a busy GPU (3% → 98%). Ring 0's trees are near enough
  that the option moves little there; it stays off until a view with swaying trees far off asks.
- **The far forest carries no policy** ([The far forest](#the-far-forest), ADR-0059): a moved instance's flags are its placement's alone (`GpuScene::place_instances`), so a policy on an instance the hand-off moves would not survive its first move; it casts as a rigid tree does.
- **A water body's surface takes the policy too** (S107, 2026-11-14; [water](water.md#where-the-water-is)): `mesh_caster_policy` gives a body's mesh — a `SceneWater` that is not a channel — `k_instance_untraced` and no cascade (bits 2–4 hold 1, "the 0 nearest"), whatever the flora switch below says. The water branch lights what is under the surface itself, so as a caster the surface only ever shadowed ground beyond its outline under its level, which the body's definition says is dry.
- `renderer.flora.caster_policy=false` casts every species as a tree does, for a before-and-after.
  `FloraStats::casters_nearest`, `casters_rest` and `untraced` count the instances by policy, when
  the instances change.

**What holds it**: the sward scene above under `--shadows csm` draws 140 cascade pairs a frame with
the policy against 1,400 without it, and under `--shadows rt` the chain builds 46 structures a frame
(the ground's) against 350. **The two contracts** (R110; `untraced_tests.cpp`, the shadow fixture's
floating cube with its mesh named the sward's species, against `renderer.flora.caster_policy=false`):
with a rasterized picture the cube is drawn, casts no traced shadow and the chain wants none of it;
on the ray path it is drawn word for word as the policy-off run draws it, rigid and deformed, and
casts no shadow there either, the chain wanting its facing clusters and none of its back faces; the
reference path tracer (direct light) sees it with its camera ray and lights the ground under it.
`domain/gfx`'s records test holds the filter at the bytes (a rasterized frame takes nothing of an
untraced deformed instance, a traced one its drawn entries from their blocks and no caster), and its
TLAS case the mask. **What it costs** ([the experiment](../experiments/untraced-primary-2026-10-28.md)):
the ray path's grass is word for word what it draws with the policy off (0 of 1,440,000 id words
differ on the proof of concept's grass-only scene at 1600×900), and the chain builds it — 2,308 →
67,934 structures and `rt` 0.54 → 2.00 ms on that scene, 99,811 → 100,957 on the v20 forest at
1600×900, and 247,302 at 11520×2160, all built at the device's default budget and not at the
proof of concept's pinned 1,024 MiB. A rasterized frame's grass is the bytes it was.

### A form carries only the parts it uses

Also R95. A ring's distance form copied its source's whole motion table and restricted only the
vertex records, so a sward card carried its patch's 1,040 blades and a tree's card form its whole
crown's parts. `stream_authored`'s copy now keeps the parts its motion records name and their
ancestors (a part's frame is its parent chain's), in their order so parents still come first, and
remaps the records, the parents and the structural table's ids (`prune_form_parts`); each kept
part's id in its source stays beside the table (`SourceMesh::motion_part_ids`), and the trees'
phase is taken from it (`FloraMesh::phase_id`), so a pruned form sways as its source and the
streamed-sway tests still differ by 0 pixels. `AuthoredStats::form_parts_before/after` count it; the
authored test's oak and spruce forms keep 144 of their 151 parts (the oak's cards name every part of
its crown; the spruce's forms keep 26 and 21 of 27). **A cooked grass container is pruned the same
way at load** (`adopt_container`, grass alone, since a tree's table also feeds the collision): the
meadow's card containers keep 14 to 16 blades of 270 to 1,040 — `d100-v0/distance.clusters`
1,040 → 16.

### A placement's form by ring

Roadmap G197 (2026-11-13). **A generator's placement of a resident mesh takes a form by its tile's
ring, as an authored instance does.** Until this row a placement entry's meshes were placed as
themselves in every ring: the forest's litter, four patches of 55 to 245 clusters, held 63% of one
staging scene's pairs and 53% of the next at 148 pairs an instance whatever the distance, and the
owner's walk sat at the pair cap ([the count](../experiments/rt-chain-walk-2026-11-12.md#what-a-far-placement-draws)).

**The table** (`ring_forms.h`, `SceneData::ring_forms`). After the authored forms, `load_scene`
(`make_placement_forms`) takes every scene mesh a streamed entry holds resident — except an entry
that picks its own forms (`StreamedPlacements::own_forms`, the `authored` entry's) — and for each
ring past the first cuts a distance form of it for that ring's floor (`geometry::extract_lod_form`,
the authored forms' cut, the same floor `(radius[r − 1] − √2/2 − 1/4) × tile`, the same projection
and thresholds), appended as a mesh of its own with `form_source` set, its fit, materials,
textures and caster policy its source's. It is a **static form** under the ray tracing chain
([above](#static-structures-for-rigid-forms); `form_rigid` 1) only when its caster policy traces
it: a static form draws its frontier at every distance, so where nothing traces it (the litter) it
would buy no structure and cost a change at the ring's edge (below). A ring whose cut keeps every cluster the
ring inside it kept reuses that one. Then **the rule** (`choose_ring_forms`) picks per ring the
cheapest, in pairs, of: the ring's cut; a form the mesh **offers** (`OfferedForm`: a far form its
container carries, the seam G198 fills), where the mesh's projected diameter at the ring's floor is
no more than what the form says it serves. A cut is cut for a placement scaled up to
`renderer.forms.cut_scale` (1.5) and an offered form serves the scales its size covers; and a
placement whose projected diameter at the ring's floor is under `renderer.forms.min_px` (1 px at the
session's projection, `AuthoredStreaming::proj_scale`) is drawn as nothing there.

**The read** (`pick_ring_form`, the world's placements consumer, per placement as it builds a tile;
[world](world.md#a-placements-form-by-ring)): the ring's entry when the placement's scale is
within what it serves, else the ring before's, down to the mesh itself; nothing when it is smaller
than the ring's `min_px` bound. A pure read of the load's table — no allocation, no state — so it
answers the same from any thread. A placement drawn as nothing still hands its footprint to the
entries after it, so the next entry places the same in every ring.

**The hand-over.** A cut drawn from at least its floor selects exactly the clusters its source
selects from there, with the same fade splits ([geometry](geometry.md#distance-forms)), so the
move from the mesh to its cut at a ring's edge changes no pixel: the same rule the authored forms
and R91's measure for trees rest on. **A static form is the exception**: under traced shadows or
primaries a rigid form draws its frontier at every distance (R94), which is finer than the mesh
draws past the floor, so a tile moved inward, from the form to the mesh, changes. Measured on the
streamed litter scene under `--shadows rt` with the forms static (the hook's first commit): 106
handovers, the outward ones behind the walker, the inward ones 3,341 changed colours over 4,100
of their tiles' pixels — at 80 m a patch's form drew 552 pixels where the mesh's own cut drew 156,
the mesh's coarse levels having lost the leaves its frontier kept. So a form is static only when
its caster policy traces it, and the litter's are not; a traced mesh's forms (a rock's) keep the
structure built once and this price, which its maker answers at the hand-over.

**Measured** (2026-11-13, `msvc-release`, a pair of binaries from one tree, 1920 × 1080, `--shadows
rt`; the machine shared with other agents' builds and GPU work, so the times are upper bounds and
the pairs are counts). A streamed scene of the staging's rings (64 m tiles, radii 1.25, 3, 10 and 20
tiles) over a 3 km terrain, two `litter` entries of the engine's own recipes at 2 m cells, 640
patches a tile (156,000 a km², the staging's 153,000), and a 158 m walk at 4.5 m/s; at its end:

| ring | tiles drawn (withheld), before | pairs an instance, before | tiles drawn, after | pairs an instance, after | pairs, before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 5 | 132 | 5 | 132 | 422,845 → 422,845 |
| 1 | 27 | 135 | 27 | 48.5 | 2,323,114 → 837,397 |
| 2 | 154 (167) | 134 | 321 | 4.35 | 13,232,354 → 897,272 |
| 3 | 0 (1,006) | — | 1,006 | 4.11 | 0 → 2,646,383 |
| tail | | | | | 15,978,313 → 4,803,897 |

Before, the cap withheld half the third ring and all the fourth; after, every tile is drawn with
71% of the cap unspent. The GPU's frame went from 1.32 to 2.23 ms median for the 1,173 tiles
more it draws (visible pairs 118,000 → 785,000). The handover pass over the same walk (106 ring
changes of occupied tiles) changed no pixel. **What a ring change costs**: on the walk 99 tiles
came in and 94 changed ring; before, a change rebuilt nothing (the litter draws every ring alike),
after, each of the 94 is built again for its forms, 378 generator calls where there were 190 (2 ms
each). A stretch paced back and forth across the inner ring's edge seven times rebuilt no tile:
the ring's own band held it. What can show is a form drawn nearer than its floor — a tile
moved inward and not yet built again — which the quarter tile in the floor covers, as for an
authored form; and the step to nothing, which happens only under `min_px`. An offered form draws
what its maker says it draws, and its hand-over is its maker's to show.

**Where the 0.9 ms went.** Per pass, the median over the walk's frames (the same pair of runs):
the hardware rasterizer 0.105 → 0.613 ms, the top-level records 0.081 → 0.393, the
deformed-vertex pool's pass 0.060 → 0.375, the ray chain's ranges 0.014 → 0.083 and `rt` 0.594 →
0.779; the cull fell 0.394 → 0.222 and the chain's records 0.252 → 0.106. Each rise follows a
count the newly drawn tiles brought, not the forms: instances 121,653 → 902,977 (the top-level
records are written a thread an instance every frame) and visible entries 117,780 → 785,188 (the
rasterizer and the pool's pass walk the cull's visible list, the pool's pass even where nothing
deforms); the cull, which runs a thread a pair, fell with the pairs, 16.3 M → 5.6 M. **Like for
like** — the same scene with its rings at 1.25, 3 and 6 tiles, so both binaries draw the same 5,
27 and 99 tiles and withhold none, over the same walk (2026-11-14, the GPU lease held, other agents'
work at 20 to 43% of the CPU): the frame 1.083 → 0.563 ms median, the cull 0.271 → 0.058 (pairs
11.8 M → 1.9 M), `rt` 0.536 → 0.218 (its records 0.236 → 0.034, its emit 0.142 → 0.025), and the
rasterizer, the pool's pass, the top-level records and the resolve unchanged (0.069, 0.039, 0.068,
0.17), with the same 74,194 visible entries: a cut draws what its source draws from there. So the
forms halve the frame's cost on the tiles both draw, and the after's 2.2 ms on the full rings is
the 1,173 tiles the cap withheld before, drawn.

**On the forest staging** (2026-11-14, the owner's settings: 3840 × 2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt
--no-lights --time-of-day 15 --lod 1 --terrain-tiles --terrain-far 6`, bounce GI, micromaps,
flora motion; six frames at (180, 200, 1509) looking north; `bin-base` 486AC137…, `bin-final`
52C394FD…; the scene file 184,799,237 bytes, written 2026-11-12 21:01; the machine shared with
other rows' builds, GPU suites and forest loads). Both draw every tile (5, 22, 285 and 815 by
ring) and withhold none from this camera:

| ring | pairs, before | pairs, after | the litter's, before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 5,181,536 | 5,181,536 | — (none placed near this camera) |
| 1 | 469,245 | 469,245 | — |
| 2 | 2,509,504 | 963,486 | 1,556,292 → 10,274 (10,274 instances) |
| 3 | 6,113,954 | 1,822,418 | 4,322,776 → 31,240 (28,984 instances) |
| tail | 14,274,239 | 8,436,685 | 5,879,068 → 41,514, of the cap's 16,777,216 |

The litter went from 41% of the tail to under 1%: every far patch is one or two clusters, and
none was under `min_px` there. What holds the tail now is what this rule does not touch: the
sward's cards (5,352,736, 64% of the after's tail, nearly all in the first ring) and the
understory ferns (`fern-arch` 1,630,928 and `fern-creep` 472,857, 25%, 64 and 33 pairs an
instance in the fourth ring as in the third). Both are flora recipes, which carry a motion
contract, and a mesh that sways keeps itself in every ring (below); that the ferns are kept for
that reason, and not because their entry picks its own forms, is read from the scene file and not
traced through the load. They are the next row's: a swaying mesh's far form that stands still.

**The forest walked** (the same settings, a 135 m walk north from (180, 200, 1509) at 4.5 m/s, 900
frames, one flight each; free commit 56 and 57 GB at the start, 8.5 and 14.3 GB at its lowest
with other rows' forest loads beside): the frame's GPU median 12.40 → 12.09 ms (p99 16.54 →
15.87), the cull 0.541 → 0.326, `rt` 1.741 → 1.659, the trace 1.042 → 0.939, the resolve 7.36
and 7.40 (the frame is the resolve's at this resolution); the tail at the walk's end 15,259,104 →
9,667,470 pairs, three fourth-ring tiles withheld before and none after; 25 pair-budget
withholding lines → 0, and 150 mesh-room lines → 54 (the room is T131's). Ring changes: 85 tiles
came in and 77 changed ring in both, and both built the same 193 tiles: **on the forest a form
change adds no rebuild**, because every tile there holds an entry that draws its rings differently
already (`representation`), so the base rebuilt them too. The builds are on the frame's thread
(`change_ring` → `take` → `build`), 2,042 and 1,992 ms of tile work, 21 frames over 50 ms of it in
each (at most 85 ms), about 10 ms a tile. Frames over 50 ms in all: 23 → 24, and the 20 over
100 ms (600 to 850 ms) fall on the same frames in both binaries with no tile work and a 2 ms
frame of their own: not this row's, handed to T131.

**What a ring change costs, and the swap it could be.** Where the base did not rebuild — the
engine's litter scene, whose only entries draw every ring alike — the forms do: on the like-for-like
walk 34 → 73 tiles built, 151 → 278 ms on the frame's thread (each about 3.8 ms, its generators
called again). **Since T131's merge** (`bin-merged` B3B09B11…, b64-G197 at 7f18339d) the same 73
tiles are built by the build job on the efficiency pool, 483 ms there, and the frame's thread keeps
the hand-over: 5 ms over the walk, 0.10 ms at its 99th percentile and 0.21 at most, where it was
3.71 and 7.60; the GPU's frame the same (0.577 ms). A tile whose ring changed keeps drawing its old
forms until its job's result is installed, about 7 frames of the walk later at the median and 22
at most (a FIFO match of ring events to collected tiles, so approximate): 1 to 3 m of walking, well
inside the quarter tile the floor is cut with, and no hole. In a window over the full rings (the
first walk, 106 ring changes, 205 tiles built by each; the session locked, so frames ran
unpaced; others at 85 to 88% of the CPU) the tile work on the frame's thread went from 1,004 ms
to 15 (p99 7.01 → 0.18 ms, at most 13.1 → 0.3), and the frames over 50 ms from 1 to 3, all
three with no tile work: two in the first second, behind the first fill's table rebuild (50 ms
of `tables`), and one at the end.

**The swap, since G202** ([world](world.md#a-ring-change-rewrites-the-forms-in-place)): a ring
change between two rings an entry draws as one representation rewrites each kept placement's mesh
through `pick_ring_form` on the committing thread, with no generator call, and hands the renderer
what it changed. `DynamicBlock::from_version`, `changed` and `changed_count` say it: **a block the
renderer holds at `from_version` with the same count is that block with exactly the instances
`changed` names different**, so it is not compared (`TileChange::told_instances`, `TileStats::told`)
and is rewritten in place from its first changed instance — `TileLayout::Request::keep` and
`keep_pairs`, a `SlotWrite` whose `skip` leaves the slots before it, and their pairs, as they were
(an instance's `first_pair` is a prefix sum within its block, so every slot after the first
changed one moves anyway). A block held at another version, or with another count, is read as
before; the renderer trusts the claim only against the version it holds. Until G202 such a tile was
built again and, coming back with its count and a new version, compared instance by instance: 440
instances in `engine_view`'s "a streamed world's hand-over reads only the tiles it changed", which
wants none, and passes again with the swap.

**Measured** (2026-11-14, the litter scene's 1,698-frame walk offscreen at 1920 × 1080, `msvc-release`,
`bin-base` 46B41458… at main ae9efac5 against `bin-final` FD45A149… at b65-G197 cb1e5ce2; a shared
machine, the harness's `machine_state` at 100% of the CPU taken by others and the GPU lock another
row's, so every millisecond is an upper bound): **the same 198 tiles built by the generators in
both** (592.6 and 600.4 ms on the job), where G197 before the swap built 73 against 34 on last
night's like-for-like walk; the 106 ring changes rewritten in place, 20,266 instances, 7.16 ms on the
committing thread in all (about 0.07 ms a tile); 0 instances compared, 20,266 told. The tail
15,980,404 → 4,803,897 pairs at the walk's end with 1,173 tiles withheld → none (by ring 422,845 /
2,323,114 / 13,234,445 / 0 → 422,845 / 837,397 / 897,272 / 2,646,383), the GPU's median 1.34 →
2.24 ms for 122 k → 902 k instances drawn (the 0.9 ms of newly drawn tiles G197 measured). **The
paced stretch** across ring 1's edge (frames 1,050 on, 12 m back and forth at 4.5 m/s): 12 ring
changes in both, 8 tiles built in both, the final's 12 rewritten in place (2,134 instances, 0.61 ms),
none compared; the world's tile work on the frame's thread 0.8 ms over the stretch in both, at most
0.28 and 0.22 ms a frame. Over the whole walk the frame's tile work is 17.3 → 34.8 ms, at most 1.6
→ 9.3 ms in one frame (not traced; the rewrites are not in it), and the renderer's hand-over at most
29 → 79 ms, its compactions over seven times the instances (T137's row).

**What it looks like.** The litter scene with the generated sets (`engine-content matgen`; the
ground `ground/soil`, stochastic at 2 m; `load.materials` the worktree's `content/materials`), at
1920 × 1080, from 1.7 m across the inner ring's edge, from 12 m, and to the horizon: before and
after differ in 147, 381 and 309 pixels of 2,073,600, every one in the band of the picture where
the third and fourth rings lie — the far litter the cap withheld, now drawn — at most 37 of 255 a
channel. That is the visible gain, and it is next to none: a far patch is a pixel or two. Beside a
photographed pine floor (the reels' r52) what a person objects to is not the rings: the litter is
scattered orange specks on a near-black soil where the photograph is a continuous rust carpet
that hides the ground; each patch is a disc with a hard edge, with nothing gathered at a stem or a
log; and the far floor goes one flat grey, since what carries a litter's colour to the horizon is
the ground's own layer under it, not placements a pixel wide.

**What an imported mesh gets, and what a scene with none of it costs.** Every input is what any mesh
has or can be measured for — its DAG, its size, a form its container offers — never which
generator placed it, so an imported boulder scattered by a scene file is cut, chosen and dropped by
the same rule; a mesh that offers no far form is drawn by its cuts. A mesh that sways (the motion
contract: the sward's cards, ferns, swaying trees) takes its forms by
[what its motion measures](#a-swaying-meshs-form-by-ring) (G204); one that deforms any other way
(a skin, morphs) keeps itself in every ring, and so
does every mesh of a paged scene, whose page tables a form has none of. A scene that streams no
entry makes no table; one whose meshes are small enough that no cut drops a cluster makes the table
and no mesh. A tile's own meshes (those that arrive with the tile, [above](#meshes-that-come-and-go))
are not in the table: they are built after the load, and draw themselves.

### A commit past the tail's budget withholds its farthest tiles

Also R95, and R137 (2026-11-07). **The tail's room never grows past `renderer.flora.tail_budget_mib`**
— the deform records and their per-frame copies, the pose table's tail regions and the push state, as
`FloraStats::tail_bytes` costs them. The default (the tunable's 0) **follows the device**: a sixteenth
of the device-local heaps, the share the ray tracing chain's budget takes, never under 1,024 MiB (the
fixed default from R95 until R137) and never over 4,096 (`resolve_flora_tail_budget`, settings.h):
2,025 MiB on the 32 GB RTX 5090, 1,536 on 24 GB, 1,024 on 16 GB and below. Why a sixteenth: the
owner's v34 walk at 3840×2160 was refused at a bound of 1.09–1.16 GB, and with the chain's sixteenth
and the structure cache's sixty-fourth the three take at most nine sixty-fourths of the card. It is a
ceiling, not an allocation — the room grows only as far as the records need, half as much again at a
time — and a tunable that is not zero overrides it (`FloraStats::tail_budget_source`).

**The bound counts a record once.** `set_dynamic_instances` computes, before anything changes, the
records the changed blocks' swaying trees make, the way `acquire_tail_tree` hands them out: a tree
takes its own mesh's free record first — newest first, the ones this commit's own departures give
back among them — then its run-size class's free record given back longest ago, once no frame in
flight can read it, and only then a new one. Per class that is what the meshes' demands pass their
own free records by, less the old free records their own meshes never reach (`tail_new_records`; a
record another mesh takes that its own mesh needed sends that mesh to the class in turn, which changes
nothing in the sum). It is exact because `write_slots` now gives back every record the change moves
**before** any slot takes one (until R137 each slot gave back and took in turn, so a tree that left
and one of its mesh that arrived later in the write order did not share a record); the room it
reports (`FloraStats::tail_bound_bytes`) is the room `relayout` grows the tables to, to the byte, and
a debug build asserts the commit made no record the bound did not count. **The slack was** every
swaying tree of every changed block counted as a new record — a tile whose trees moved to another
tile in one commit counted twice over, which is what refused the owner's v34 walk for fifty seconds:
841 commits of 61–66 thousand instances, every tree drawn as its far stand-in. **It is** none, where
the free lists say what the commit can reuse; conservative only in that a kept block a compaction
moves is left out of both sides (it gives back and takes the same meshes).

**Nearest first, the rest withheld.** The changed blocks are admitted in order — the block the eye
stands in (its instances' footprint holds the eye, `GpuScene::set_tail_eye`, which `flora_frame` sets
every frame from the frame's origin), then by ring, then by the footprint's distance from the eye,
then the caller's order — until the next would pass the budget; it and every farther block with
trees is **withheld**: not placed, its held block (if the key had one) freed like any tile the tail
no longer names, and named again by the caller's next commit, which tries it again — as the pair
budget's withholds are ([world](world.md)). A block that takes no record (rocks, grass, a tile of
rigid forms) costs nothing and is always admitted, and a block a request keeps as it is was admitted
before. `TileChange::withheld_tiles`/`withheld_instances` and `FloraStats::tail_withheld_tiles`,
`tail_withheld_instances` (the last commit's) and `tail_withholding_commits` count them, the log
says so once each time the count changes (INFO, never an error), and `GpuScene::admitted_blocks`
is what `SceneRenderer::set_dynamic_instances` hands the fires and **the far forest's hand-off**, so
a withheld tile keeps drawing its far stand-in. **The one refusal left** is a commit whose nearest
changed block alone would pass the budget: refused before anything changes, with a sentence naming
the trees, the records and the bytes (`FloraStats::tail_refused`), and the frame draws what the scene
has; nothing reaches the device as an out-of-memory loss either way. `tail_budget_tests.cpp` holds
the four rules on a GPU with a generated palm (the moved tile's bound equal to the room, the nearest
two of four tiles admitted and the farther two admitted once the near ones leave, the eye's tile in
the farthest ring admitted first, a single tile past the first room refused and the next commit
taken), and `authored_view_tests.cpp` still streams the 140 trees with the ceiling at 1 MiB, below
the first room, so the nearest tile alone is refused and the run ends well with its capture written.

**Measured on the owner's v34 stretch** (2026-11-07; the walk's frame records from pose time 283 s to its end, 22:01:44–22:02:45, as a camera path of 1,666 keys drawn at 30 frames a second, 1,836 frames, the owner's flags, offscreen at 3840×2160, the RTX 5090; the machine shared — other processes held 37–64% of the CPU and the GPU was busy beside the runs, so no timing is quoted). Main at 8be9c6d4: **2 commits refused** (115,196 and 114,672 instances, 15.1 M pairs, a bound of 1,372,501,952 bytes against 1 GiB), both at the jumps to the path's markers, where every ring's tiles arrive in one commit; the flight itself refused none, so it does not reproduce the walk's 841 retries, and its per-frame visible pairs are the same in both runs. The room it ended with: 26,306 records, 693,401,024 bytes. With R137: **0 refused, 0 withheld**, the device's budget 2,123,366,400 bytes (2,025 MiB), 23,633 records and 625,583,168 bytes at the end (fewer: a tree that leaves now hands its record to the next of its mesh whatever the write order), and the bound's room equal to the room to the byte. The two marker captures the main build refused show every tree of the nearest rings as its far-forest stand-in (`b54/R137/before/markers/00922-t922.png` in the coordinator's scratch); R137's show the trees. The slack the old bound carried at that commit: 1.37 GB counted for a room that holds the same tiles in 0.63 GB.

### The pair accounting

**Pair diagnostics (2026-10-26, R100/W73).** Hosts copy `GpuScene::resolved()` after upload;
`SceneRenderer::create` compares its caller's preliminary settings with that result once and,
when any differ, logs casters, ray path, chain, static forms and caster-index fallback as typed
requested/resolved boolean fields on one INFO line, with the pair account named for its fallback. The admission fallback count survives a warmup statistics reset, like the chain's capacity and other resolved state.
The 1 MiB GPU reporting case lowers only its own device object's advertised index limit and captures the actual admission fallback; the stdio load case crosses the real limit with a surround prefix while keeping upload lazy. The cold `GpuScene::pair_summary` reads the account, terrain slot tables, tile layout and instance
forms only when a host asks for a report; it adds no accounting or work to the frame loop.

**The sward's cards in the inner ring are tail pairs like any other** (G136, 2026-11-09; [the
hand-off by distance](#the-hand-off-by-distance)). The inner ring places a patch's card beside its
near form, about three pairs a card: on the v36 scene's 60 m walk that is 7,516 more instances and
22,548 more pairs in the inner ring (1,921,631 to 1,944,179) against a tail of 15.4 million, and
