no tile was withheld at 1080p (the outermost ring's 884 withheld placements are the same before and
after). The card is not placed in the next-but-one ring, which holds about ten times the next
ring's tiles, because the owner's 4K run already withholds there (engine-needs item 26, R107).
An inner ring wide enough to show the band (1.25 tiles; [the hand-off](#the-hand-off-by-distance))
doubles the inner ring's pairs (3.9 million) but takes about as many from the rings past it, so the
tail's total is unchanged to 0.1%.

**One reservation rule, before allocation and before admission** (2026-10-26, R100).
`account_pairs` constructs the `PairAccount` consumed by final `resolve_settings` and
`GpuScene::create`. Let `P` be the file prefix, `S = sum(slots[level] * clusters_per_slot[level])`
all terrain levels' reserved slots (including replacement slots), and `B(t)` a tile's pairs
rounded by `block_capacity(t, 16)`, exactly the layout's size class, at most an eighth slack.
The fixed reservation is `F = P + S`; a proposed tail costs `F + sum(B(tile_pairs))` against
`L = 2^24`. The load's diagnostic tail bound is `B(tail_floor_pairs)`.

The consumer receives `GpuScene::static_pair_count()` as `PlacementTilesConfig::fixed_pairs`
and `GpuScene::pair_limit()` as `max_pairs`, and uses the same `reserved_tile_pairs` operation
for each candidate tile. It admits nearest rings first, then nearest tiles, stopping at the
first that cannot fit. The layout can compact old holes when required; it never refuses tiles
whose fresh reservations fit this account. Live pairs remain separate statistics from reservations.

For the geometry-index bound subtract static-form and untraced pairs (counting an instance
excluded by both only once), then multiply by views. The first frame's capacity likewise excludes
those pairs. **On the ray path the untraced pairs count** (R110): there an untraced instance's
drawn entries are built ([The caster policy](#the-caster-policy)), so `PairAccount::frame_pairs`
takes the path (`frame_pairs(ray_path)`) and subtracts only the static forms' pairs, an untraced
static form's included (`untraced_static_pairs`: built once on either path), and
`GpuScene::rt_frame_estimate` keeps `untraced_pairs_live_` in on that path alone.
`FloraStats::untraced` stays the policy's count of instances, whatever the path. **Since R152 a
rigid untraced instance's pairs leave the frame's estimate on the ray path too**, where the scene
has a cache: its entries reference the cache there ([The caster policy](#the-caster-policy)), so
`rt_reference_estimate` holds them and `rt_frame_estimate` does not (`rt_capacity_tests.cpp`'s
untraced tile, whose pin moved with it). In v13 the fixed reservation is `6,578,247 + 347,040 = 6,925,287`; the file's
144,135-pair tile floor reserves 147,456, so the initial reservation is 7,072,743. No caster-run
factor belongs in that number. The live tail in the captured clearing is 3,760,093 pairs;
1,208,168 pairs reference static forms and the 115,629 grass instances are untraced.
The [R100 measurement](../experiments/rt-pair-accounting-2026-10-26.md) separates the bounds,
actual wanted records and memory budget.

Fallback is casters, then withheld tiles, then refusal only if `F > L`. A tail floor that does
not fit is a withheld tile, never grounds to refuse the prefix. The refusal keeps its existing
sentence naming loaded instances, prefix, slots, tile floor, limit and what to lower.
`TileWorldSummary` reports `prefix_pairs` (the fixed reservation), `slot_pairs`, `pair_limit`,
`tail_pairs`, and per-ring live instances, pairs, drawn and withheld tiles. Every refusal and
withheld tile is counted. R94's v8 tail loss came from a consumer that charged neither these
terrain slots nor the layout's slack; the traced-index ceiling is no longer a visibility ceiling.
## One request, two hosts

**What a host is asked is translated once, here** (2026-10-03; `request.h`). engine-view's flags and engine-host's `render.*` fields describe the same things, and each host used to turn its own spelling into `RenderSettings` and `FrameDesc` by hand. That is how the sky's hour and exposure ([ADR-0048](../adr/0048-the-sky-is-a-providers-model-drawn-by-the-renderer.md)), the ground's time, and the ground on rings or tiles ([ADR-0050](../adr/0050-the-ground-is-drawn-from-the-worlds-tiles.md)) reached engine-view and not the protocol, and how a mesh authored half-morphed drew its defaults in one host and nothing in the other. A `RenderRequest` is the one description — the settings, the clock (`ClockRequest`: a sky's hour and the sun's day), the ground's time, a page budget's percentage and the morph entries — and everything after it is this module's, called by both hosts:

| Function | What it turns the request into | Was |
|---|---|---|
| `read_protocol_settings`, `read_protocol_clock` | the wire's `engine.protocol.RenderSettings` and `RenderClock` into the request, with the 1004 sentence for a bad value | engine-host's `read_settings` |
| `read_protocol_camera` | the wire's `RenderCamera` or `RenderOrbit` into the frame's camera; the orbit is `orbit_camera_at` from the scene's centre and radius, which at the default pitch is engine-view's `--orbit` to the bit | engine-host's `camera_of` (2026-10-04, below) |
| `scene_file_options` | the ground's time into `SceneFileOptions::ground_time_s`, which the scene reader puts in place of the file's `Terrain.time` before anything stands on the ground | new (`--ground-time`, `ground_time_s`) |
| `settings_for` | the settings against the loaded scene: the page budget's share of its page bytes, the morph weights by name or index over the channels' authored defaults | engine-view's `resolve_morph_weights` and its `--page-budget-pct` arithmetic |
| `view_set_desc` | the renderer's view layout from the resolved settings | four lines each host wrote by hand |
| `frame_clock`, `frame_at`, `flight_clock` | the frame's clocks — `sky_time_s`, a sky's `time_of_day` offset from the epoch plus `sun_rate · f / 60` (or `86,400 / day_length_s`), and `world_time_s`, `world_rate · f / 60` — for a frame and for a flight | engine-view's `sky_offset_s` and its `sun_at` lambda; engine-host drew every frame at 0 |
| `MovingGround` | the time-lapse's pool, the rings or the world's tiles laid out round the first camera before the GPU scene, the motion started (waiting offscreen) and stepped a sixtieth of a second before each frame | engine-view's two copies (offscreen, window) of the job pool, `TerrainRingSet`, `ViewTiles` and `TerrainMotion` set-up; engine-host built the levels and never moved them |
| `sun_summary`, `time_lapse_summary`, `frame_terrain` | the summary's `sun` and `time_lapse` blocks and a flight record's `terrain` | engine-view's alone; `render.benchmark`'s flythrough carried both as null |

What stays a host's: where the world's tiles come from (engine-view's world ring hands them over, `ViewWorld`; a host without one calls `MovingGround::follow_tiles`, the ring's first-fill rule), the window's clock and keys (`SunDay`, `,` `.` `[` `]` `-` `=`), and the flags' own parsing.

**The gap, flag by flag** (engine-view's usage against `render.load`, `render.capture`, `render.benchmark`, `render.compare` and `render.evaluate` on 2026-10-03). Closed: `--time-of-day`, `--sun-rate` (`clock`), `--exposure`, `--exposure-ev100`, `--terrain-rings`, `--terrain-tiles`, `--terrain-far` (version 11, with the far levels themselves: [Ground to the horizon](#ground-to-the-horizon)), `--deform-pool-mib`, `--static-shape-kib`, `--morph`, `--page-budget-pct` (`settings`), `--ground-time` (`render.load`, and new in engine-view), `--time-rate` (in `settings` since version 8 and now run), the per-call `settings` on `render.capture`, and the sky, the ground and their GPU milliseconds in the results. Already there: everything else that is a `RenderSettings` field. **A host's own, and why**: `--width`/`--height`/`--frames`/`--capture`/`--capture-channels`/`--orbit` are a call's own parameters already; `--capture-every`, `--marker-captures`, `--census`, `--census-pixels` and `--verify-occlusion` are analyses over a run that a client composes from captures (or a follow-up method); `--fly`, `--start`, `--interactive`, `--walk`, `--record-input`, `--replay-input`, `--inject-input` and `--input-map` are a camera somebody drives; `--no-vsync`, `--present`, `--present-max-hz`, `--pace`, `--swapchain-images`, `--frames-in-flight`, `--borderless`, `--windowed` and `--no-present-timing` are a window's; `--animate`, `--anim-*` and `--morph-animate` are the animation capability's, which a host drives through `FrameDesc::joints` and `morph_weights` (engine-host has no animated world behind `render.*`; it draws the bind pose); `--world`, `--world-log` and `--world-handover` are the world capability's ring of instances; `--uv-seams`, `--normal-seams`, `--uv-weight` and `--normal-weight` are the content build's (`content.build` takes them, and `render.load` reads the container); `--page-source` is protocol.md's "Not yet"; `--tunable`/`--tunables` are process state, which engine-host takes at start; `--log`, `--shaders`, `--validation`, `--adapter`, `--require-quiet` and `--wait-quiet` are the process's or the measurement's. `RenderSettings`' `shadow_frustum`, `shadow_lod_scale` and `shadow_normal_offset` have no flag either, and `time_rate_live` is a window's.

**A call is a function of its request.** The clock is a call's parameter, not host state. A scene whose ground is drawn as terrain levels is rebuilt for every call that draws it (`RenderHost::ensure_renderer`), its rings or tiles laid out round the call's first camera, so no call's sand depends on the calls before; a capture at frame f of a time-lapse draws frames 0..f through the motion first and then one more step, which is `engine-view --frames f+1 --capture`.

**The camera is part of the request, to the bit** (2026-10-04). The merge of this work left one residue: the two hosts' pictures of the erg agreed to within a step of 255 at a pixel or two and no closer — on the RTX 5090 three years on, on the Titan Xp at the scene's own time too — and the sky's metered sum (`stats.sky.sky_lux`) was the one reported number that differed, in its seventh digit. The sum was suspected; it is a fixed-order reduction in one workgroup and gives the same bits for the same frame in any process ([Exposure](#exposure)). **The cause was the camera.** engine-view's `--orbit` rose `0.45 · d` above the orbit circle and the protocol's `orbit` rose `tan(radians(24.2277)) · d` — 0.44999903 against 0.45, 32 float steps, 0.8 mm on the shrunk erg's 812 m orbit — and the sky's tables are built from the eye's altitude to its last bit. Measured on the RTX 5090 (`msvc-debug`): engine-view metered 0.025508077815…, the host 0.025508083403…; the host given engine-view's eye as an explicit camera metered engine-view's number exactly and drew engine-view's bytes, and given its own orbit's eye as an explicit camera metered its own. Both now go through `orbit_camera_at`'s arithmetic from one pitch (`k_orbit_pitch`, the protocol's default) with a rise worked out from the four operations rather than `std::tan` (view_set.h says why), and the host reads the wire's camera through `read_protocol_camera`. engine-view's orbit moved down by those 32 steps (0.8 mm in 812 m); no test of the renderer, engine-view, engine-cli, the world or scene collision noticed (`msvc-debug`, 2026-10-04).

**What holds it.** `request_tests.cpp`, with no device: every field of `RenderSettings` (42) and `FrameDesc` (14) is named with the wire field that reaches it or the reason none does, and structured bindings of exactly those counts stop the build when either grows; every field of the wire's `RenderSettings` (by the schema's reflection) has a non-default value that changes the renderer field it names when read; the wire's defaults are `RenderSettings{}` exactly; the refusals; the clock's offset and rate with and without a sky; `settings_for`'s share and weights; **an orbit on the wire is `orbit_camera`'s camera to the bit** at four distances (rest, 22, 40, 3.5) and with no orbit named, the protocol's default pitch is `k_orbit_pitch_deg`, an explicit camera is taken as it is, and `orbit_rise` is tan within a float step of the C library's from −85° to 85° (it failed at every distance before the fix: engine-view's y 401.498 against the protocol's 401.497 at 22). engine-cli's `render_tests.cpp`, on a GPU (RTX 5090, `msvc-debug`, 2026-10-04): the erg (shrunk to 256 m) captured at 12:00 and 18:30 — every uncovered pixel differs, the reported hour is the asked one to 10⁻⁶ and the sun's elevation the sky capability's ephemeris at the reported time to 0.01°; the erg at its own time captured with no new field, with every new field spelled at its default, and by `engine-view` with the same flags — **the same bytes, all three**; three years on (`ground_time_s`, `--ground-time`) it differs from its own time, and the two hosts' pictures are **the same bytes** — on the Titan Xp too (`linux-server`, 2026-10-04), where with the old orbit the erg's own time and the endless desert below each differed at one channel byte; and twelve frames of the first two seconds of `desert-endless`'s path benchmarked with the ground on the world's tiles at 16:00 report the tile columns (`stats.ground`: layout `tiles`, the two far levels the call asked for, levels, chunks, slots' bytes; the flythrough's `time_lapse.rings`) and the sky columns (`stats.sky.hour`, `gpu_ms.sky`, the flythrough's `sun.sky` and `gpu_ms.sky` percentiles). The same scene loaded with tiles and no far levels named reports the tunable's count (six) where `engine-view --terrain-tiles` does, and the two hosts' captures from the orbit's 2 km up, where the ground runs out to the far levels' reach, are the same bytes.

**Canonical vertex ids, read-only.** `mesh_vertex_ids(scene, mesh)` is a span over the loaded mesh's cluster vertices' canonical ids ([geometry](geometry.md#canonical-vertex-identity)): entry *i* names `lod.mesh.vertices[parts[mesh].first_vertex + i]`, and `parts[mesh].vertex_id_source` says which id space it is in — each mesh of a scene has its own. It is what a future binding step will look a vertex up by, since a file written beside a mesh names ids and never cluster indices, which every rebuild renumbers. **Nothing uploads it**: no pass reads an id yet, so it is not in a page's bytes, not in the GPU scene, and not released with the paged host streams when a streamed scene's pages come off disk (`attach_page_source`) — the lookup answers the same however the scene was loaded. A single-mesh scene fills its one part's source itself, as it does its morph channel run, because it never goes through `merge_cluster_meshes`. The span is empty for a mesh with no ids (the procedural scenes, a container from before cluster cache version 12) and for an index past the scene's meshes.

## What engine-view still owns

The flags and their validation — what they mean is the renderer's ([One request, two hosts](#one-request-two-hosts)) — the window and its events, the surface and the swapchain (including the resize and the present), the screenshot of the *presented* image, the shader-reload timer, and the JSON summary line. It keeps the swapchain path because presenting is not the renderer's business and because reading the picture back out of the presented image is what makes an engine-view capture the same bytes it has always been. See [apps](apps.md).

## Depends on

`base`, `containers`, `hash`, `math`, `time`, `log`, `platform`, `io`, `image`, `geometry`, `anim`, `assets`, `gfx`, `json`, `tunables` (the `renderer.rt.*` budget and policy, read once when a scene or a renderer is created), `schema` with the generated `schemas` (the scene file, the camera path and the overlay are read through `engine.scene` types, and a flythrough's records are written as them), and `scene_gen` (the ground providers a terrain names, the waves among them, registered by this module, and the placement generators a scene's entries name; [scene_gen](scene_gen.md)) — **no capability**: the terrain's dunes and the ruins reach the scene reader through the registry, and the renderer's conditional link to the ruins, [ADR-0037](../adr/0037-scene-reader-links-ruins-where-configured.md)'s interim exception to [ADR-0027](../adr/0027-additive-capabilities.md) decision 1, is gone ([ADR-0046](../adr/0046-scene-generators-register-themselves.md)). **Not** `window`, by design and by a compile-time check, and **not** `systems/animation`, `domain/ecs` or flecs, by the same design: `anim` is here for the 48-byte `JointMatrix` and nothing else ([Skinned instances](#skinned-instances)).

## Testing

`tools/dev.ps1 test -Preset msvc-debug -Filter renderer` runs the module's tests, all headless — as **four CTest tests**, `renderer.1` to `renderer.4`, over the one executable, the test files dealt by `cmake/test-costs.txt`'s seconds and the rest round the four in name order — the table holds no renderer rows yet, so name order ([what to run](../ci/what-to-run.md#parts-dealt-by-cost)) — (`engine_module_tests(... PARTS 4 CONFIG_INVARIANT)`, doctest's `--source-file=` filter; `config_invariant` lets an off-configuration run them with no GPU, [the off-configurations' GPU cases](../ci/what-to-run.md#the-off-configurations-gpu-cases)), because the whole suite outgrew one test's GPU work budget on the Titan Xp on 2026-11-09 — 6,389 s there on gate b56, past the 9,000 s ceiling on b57's first run, 6,689 s as the four parts on its second, 1,164 s on the RTX 5090 in `msvc-debug` ([remote Linux builds](../ci/remote-linux.md)); `-Filter renderer` and `-Affected` take all four, and the executable run by hand takes `-tc=` and `-sf=` as before. They write a unit-cube GLB at test time (one primitive, one material — the fixture `apps/engine_view/tests` writes, minus the textures) into a `test::TempDir` of their own, with the derived-data root inside it, so nothing in the tree, nothing in the repository's cache, and nothing another copy of the suite is using is touched (AGENTS.md, test hygiene). They skip with a message on a machine with no Vulkan device or no 64-bit buffer atomics, exactly as engine-view exits 3. `vertex_id_tests.cpp` needs no device: a two-quad `.gltf` whose shared edge carries two authored ids loads with all eight vertices, `authored` on its part, and every id at the position the file gave it — from the glTF on a cache miss and again from the container on the hit; a scene of it beside the same file without the attribute keeps one id space per mesh (`authored`, then `position_weld` ranks under 6) with the two spans adding up to the merged vertices; and the procedural terrain exposes no ids. The others check: a cube rendered offscreen into all four channels at once, with the center pixel's id naming instance 0, a cluster of that scene, and a triangle under 128, and an uncovered corner naming nothing; every `Stats` field present and consistent; the four channels landing on disk in the documented shapes, with the id file exactly `width * height * 3 * 4` bytes; two instances of the cube producing exactly the ids 0 and 1 and no others; `resolve_settings` making the same five decisions on a synthetic baseline device, an RT device, and a path that cannot shadow; and the direct path refusing an id capture with a message while still capturing color.

**The glTF sampler's wraps and the texture transform** are a fourth case of `texture_tests.cpp`: a quad with UVs from 0 to 3 and a 2×2 texture of four colours through a nearest sampler shows nine whole tiles under repeat, every other tile reflected under mirror, and one tile then the edge texel under clamp — all 36 cells, matched to the nearest of the four colours at their centres — and UVs from 0 to 1 with a `KHR_texture_transform` scale of 3 show the same nine tiles; each from the decoded image and from the built texture, with one material sampler in the scene. The reference's agreement case gained a **dark plane lit by its own emissive texture**, held to the same kind of FLIP bound as the other three: 0.014 on the RTX 5090, under a bound of 0.05 ([Materials](#materials)). The emissive and occlusion slots, the ORM packing and the transform's rotation are held to the CPU reference at the gfx level, 1 of 255 at worst on the RTX 5090 ([gfx](gfx.md)).

**Built textures have three cases** (`texture_tests.cpp`, [Built textures](#built-textures)), each over a textured quad written at test time and loaded through a derived-data root in the test's scratch directory, drawn through the albedo view (`ResolveMode::Albedo`, the textured base colour unlit, so the lights are not in the comparison), once decoded and once after the test builds the `.tex` the container names. **Up close**, where level 0 is what both paths sample, the built picture is within BC7's bound of the decoded one (PSNR above 38 dB, no channel more than 16 codes off). **Far away**, a one-texel checkerboard resolves to its mean through the mips — display value 186, half the light, since the chain was filtered in linear light — with a spread under 3 codes, where the decoded path aliases to black and white. **The level the hardware picks** is read back from a probe texture written by hand whose level L is red 28 L: at four distances the red, taken back to linear, gives the level of detail the resolve's analytic derivatives selected, and it is log₂ of the texels per pixel that the projection's finite difference across a pixel gives, within 0.2 of a level. The distances put the level just past a whole one on purpose: NVIDIA's driver shortens the blend between two levels (a fraction f of the way reads as min(1, 2f)), which is the driver's filtering and not the derivatives' choice ([texture](texture.md#what-it-measured)).

**The sand's detail has two files** ([The sand close up](#the-sand-close-up)). `ground_detail_tests.cpp`, on the waves and so in every configuration: a block asking for nothing draws what no block draws, byte for byte; the detail on changes the terrain's colour and none of its ids; two runs are the same bytes; occlusion culling and the cone test change no pixel; the ray path shades every pixel it agrees on with the rasterizer to the same byte; a pull-back from 1.65 m to 350 m at 192×108, detail on and off, each frame beside a 4×4 supersampled one, adds at most 0.12 of a level of luma to the frame-to-frame change and 0.18 to the error against the supersampled picture, and moves its mean by at most 0.09 (RTX 5090, 2026-09-29; bounds 1.5, 1.0 and 1.5); and the reference at a walker's feet agrees with the resolve with the detail as well as without it (0.0498 FLIP against 0.0539; the bound is without's plus 0.02). `ground_detail_rings_tests.cpp`, where the terrain capability is: the dunes' ripple wind is the ripple term's rule, a unit vector, and turns at most 0.16° a game minute across four days (the bound a half turn over two hours allows is 1.5°); the seams across the rings' and the chunks' borders, and occlusion, cones and determinism over the rings, as that section reports.

**The world's tiles have two files** ([The ground from the world's tiles](#the-ground-from-the-worlds-tiles), which reports what they hold): `terrain_tiles_tests.cpp`, with no device and in every configuration, and `terrain_tiles_gpu_tests.cpp`, where the terrain capability is. `-tc="world tiles*"` runs both. **The rings' chunks at their corners** have `terrain_rings_tests.cpp`, no device, where the terrain capability is ([The ground's tiles are placed at their corners](#the-grounds-tiles-are-placed-at-their-corners)); `-tc="terrain rings*"` runs it with the rings' GPU cases.

**One upload per distinct image has a case of its own** (`kit members that sample one image upload it once and draw the same picture`, [One upload per distinct image](#one-upload-per-distinct-image)): four kit members written at test time, each a glTF quad in a directory of its own — two naming their own copy of one PNG beside them, one embedding the same bytes as a data URI, one naming an `image.png` that is another picture — three instances each, from the decoded images and from the built textures a cold cache fills. Each member's own upload (`share_textures` off) is four textures; shared, it is two — the three members whose bytes match, whatever they called the image, and the one that only shares its name — with half the bytes, the other half counted as saved, and **0 differing pixels** in ids, depth and colour at 256×256 (14,840 covered, RTX 5090). The same scene loaded with one instance and given the other eleven as a tail between frames keeps the same two textures and bytes and draws the same picture again.

**On a device without mesh shaders or ray queries — the baseline tier — the suite runs, it does not skip.** `RenderSettings{}` asks for `hw`, which `resolve_settings` turns into the vertex path there, so every case about the *picture* (the cube and its channels, two instances, the surround's centre view, occlusion culling, Panini, the skinned bar and its bend and sweep, the morph cases, the pool's budget, the cones, the shredded atlas, and all seven streaming cases) draws through `cluster_vertex.slang`. Only a case about a *path* skips, naming what is missing in the device's own words: the direct path (`no mesh shaders`), the mesh-path half of "the mesh, vertex and ray paths agree" and of the cone case (`no VK_EXT_mesh_shader`), and every ray half — the ray path, the turned surround's TLAS half, the four reference cases, the 8-bit-index streaming case, which only exists when the frame builds the ray chain — with `unavailable_reason`'s sentence. "The mesh, vertex and ray paths agree" holds the other two to the **vertex** path now, because it is the one every device that renders has; asking a device without mesh shaders for `hw` would compare the vertex path with itself. The harnesses of the atlas and streaming files skip **only** on no device or `check_availability`; a scene, GPU scene, page source or renderer that fails to build is a `REQUIRE` failure. Until 2026-09-23 they reported any build failure as a skip, which is how nine cases — all eight streaming cases and the shredded atlas — "passed" on the first run on the TITAN Xp without drawing a frame, while the renderer could not be created there at all; eight of them draw there now, and the ninth, the 8-bit-index case, skips because the card builds no ray chain ([self-hosted runners](../ci/self-hosted-runners.md#the-first-run-on-the-titan-xp)).

**A TITAN-Xp-like device is a case of its own** (`a TITAN-Xp-like device draws the default request through the vertex path`), so the baseline tier is tested on every GPU and not only on the server: `DeviceOptions::overrides` removes `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`, `VK_KHR_ray_query`, `VK_NV_cluster_acceleration_structure` and the two extensions the card lacks besides, which creates a device that really lacks them. The default request builds and draws there through the vertex path's indexed draw (the card has `geometryShader` and `fullDrawIndexUint32`, so the profile keeps them, and the case checks `vertex_indexed`, a nonzero `triangles_hw` and no fallback) with occlusion culling and no shadows, and the picture — a two-row wall of cubes at 200×120 — is compared with the same scene drawn by the device as it is with shadows off: on the RTX 5090 that is the mesh path, and **7,931 covered pixels, 0 id words, 0 colour bytes and 0 depths differ**. `--shadows rt`, `--raster rt` and the reference are refused on the profile with the verdict's own sentence, which has to name `VK_KHR_ray_query` and appear verbatim in `verdict.degraded`. The two devices are built one after the other and never live at once (see [gfx](gfx.md), "One live device per process"): the first draft held both, and the full device's next mesh draw called a null `vkCmdDrawMeshTasksIndirectEXT`.

**The baseline tier's two draws are one picture** (`without geometryShader the vertex path capacity-draws the same picture`). The same wall with the default request, drawn on a device without mesh shaders twice — with `geometryShader`, which is the indexed draw, and with it removed as well, which is the capacity draw — must agree to the byte: the ids, the colour and the depth, **7,931 covered pixels and 0 differences** on the RTX 5090 and on the TITAN Xp itself, with 72 triangles drawn indexed on one side and `triangles_hw` 0 on the other, over the same visible pairs. Both hardware runs draw in it, since occlusion is on. That equality is what lets `resolve_settings` choose between the draws by a device feature alone; the case skips where the adapter has no indexed draw to take away (no `geometryShader` or no `fullDrawIndexUint32`); removing `geometryShader` alone is enough to force the capacity draw.

**Running a case as a weaker card.** A case that draws with `RasterMode::Hardware` and asserts what the request resolved to must say what it skips on a card with no mesh shaders, where `resolve_settings` rightly turns that leg into the vertex tier: the walking actor in `motion_tests.cpp` and "the vertex tier accumulates the mesh path's bytes" in `accumulation_tests.cpp` each asserted `vertex_path == (raster == Vertex)` for both legs and failed on the TITAN Xp's server leg of batch 65 (141 of 142, roadmap T153). Each now asserts it unchanged on a card with mesh shaders; without them the actor's mesh leg reports `mesh skipped: no mesh shaders on this device` and its vertex leg proves the rest, and the accumulation case runs the vertex tier's twelve frames with the pass on and says the comparison skipped. Those two files open their device through `test_device.h`, which honours **`ENGINE_GFX_TEST_DEVICE`** with `gfx`'s profiles (`baseline`, `titanxp`, or a list of requirement rows; [gfx](gfx.md)), so a Windows run sees what the server would: `ENGINE_GFX_TEST_DEVICE=baseline` with `-tc="motion: a walking*,accumulation: the vertex tier*"`. A forced profile that yields no device fails the case: `device_options()` tries the profile once, the first time a case asks, and after a failed try fails every case that asks, whatever its caller then does, since most callers turn a device that will not open into a skip, as they must on a machine with no GPU, and a misspelt profile (a row `apply_overrides` refuses) or one the driver rejects turned the gate's `titanxp` leg green with nothing run until 2026-11-17 (review B6 of batch 67). `dynamic_instances_tests.cpp` opens its device the same way since batch 66's server leg, where T160's "a tail past a row of the folded cull" built a traced rig before asking whether the card traces and failed on the TITAN Xp; it now skips that leg first, as the file's older cases do, and the file's twelve cases pass under `titanxp` and `baseline`. **Since T162 every file of the suite that makes a device opens it through `test_device.h`** (`renderer_test::device_options()`; a case that removes something of its own — the vertex path's capacity draw, the micromap case's missing extension, the TITAN-Xp-like case above — adds its absences to the profile's), so `ENGINE_GFX_TEST_DEVICE=titanxp tools/dev.ps1 test -Filter '^renderer\.'` runs the whole suite as the server's card would, and the Windows gate runs it so once ([what to run](../ci/what-to-run.md#the-renderer-as-a-weaker-card)). **A new GPU test opens its device through the header too**, and skips before it builds whatever a weaker card lacks. `apps/engine_view`'s tests make no device in-process: they start `engine-view`, which reads no profile.

**A scene's ruins** (`ruins_scene_tests.cpp`, compiled with the ruins capability, no device): the kit of boxes written into the test's scratch directory and a scene with a terrain, a mesh of its own and four buildings read — the file's mesh, then the kit's, then the terrain, the instances exactly the assembler's for those fields in that order with the file's first and the terrain's last, every debris block on the terrain under it and every wall at or under the ground where it stands, a second read identical to the bit, and the scene loaded into a derived-data root in scratch — and a scene naming a kit that is not there refused with the entry named. engine-view's `ruins_view_tests.cpp` draws the same kind of scene offscreen ([ruins](ruins.md#testing)).

**A scene's generators, with no capability** (`scene_gen_scene_tests.cpp`, compiled in every configuration, no device): a ground provider and a placement generator registered from the test's own source ([scene_gen](scene_gen.md#testing)). A scene naming them reads as the file's mesh, each entry's, then the terrain, the entries' instances standing on the ground's floor and the file's on its surface, and `terrain_hash` names the provider; the ground is made before the first entry is opened and the entries are expanded in the file's order, swapped when the file swaps them; a streamed read opens each entry, appends its resident meshes and expands nothing; and an unknown placement generator, an unknown ground and a generator's own refusal come back with the registry's sentence after where the name is. It is the proof, in `msvc-minimal` and `linux-clang-minimal`, that the reader expands placements and draws a ground through the registry alone.

**The streaming cases wait for the reads, not only the queue.** `streaming_tests.cpp`'s `converge()` counts a frame as quiet — four in a row end the loop — only when nothing is pending, nothing is staged **and `StreamStats::loads_in_flight` is zero**. Until 2026-09-25 it left the last out, and on the TITAN Xp under load "pages read from the container draw what pages read from memory draw" declared convergence with five reads still in flight and captured a picture missing the pages they carried (463 s instead of 200 s, and a failure that passed on a rerun). A file-backed source's read has no bound in frames; the only honest end of a convergence is a streamer with nothing outstanding anywhere, which is the same three-way condition `GeometryStreamer` itself uses for `frames_to_converge`.

**The flythrough's cases** (`flythrough_tests.cpp`) are in two halves. With no device: the camera path — keys hit exactly under both interpolations, the cubic leaving the straight line between them, the frame count and the resampling, and each refusal with its sentence (no keys, times that do not increase, a height above a terrain the scene has not, a marker past the end, an unknown field); the terrain — deterministic, its ridge and basin where the fields put them, dunes with real relief, materials by feature, a hash that moves with every field, and a counter-clockwise grid; the scene file — the oldest spelling read as it always was, a typo refused with its path, grounded and yawed placements, a scatter inside its annulus and identical on a second read, a fit to 4 m on its point and to 2 m about its centre, a hash the bytes do not have refused naming both, and the overlay substituting by hash and then insisting on it; the summary's percentiles and per-frame medians over synthetic records; a terrain's cache entry giving back byte-identical positions and materials; and **every one of the fixture terrain's 182 clusters drawing with its own material after the scene's merge** — the vote of the merged cluster's own vertices against the map the GPU upload reads, on a cache miss and on a hit, with rock and sand both present so the check can fail (it found 18 wrong before the fix); and the scene file's `camera_path` resolved against the file's own directory like a mesh path, and absent from the oldest spelling. On a GPU, over a 64 m terrain with an 8 m ridge and three fitted cubes behind it: **two rigs built from scratch fly the path to the same visible pairs at all 25 frames**, `Stats::last` returns every frame once and in order with its own frame index, and the same rig flown again agrees from the fourth frame on; and **occlusion culling changes no pixel anywhere on the path** — all 25 frames drawn with and without it in lockstep, 0 surface and 0 colour differences — while the census shows it culled the hidden cubes (0 pairs against 12 at frames 3–6) and they are drawn once in view.
**Occlusion culling changes no pixel**, which is the case that guards both of the fixed-cost changes above: the same wall of cubes at two depths is rendered with `occlusion` on and off at 302×154 — a multiple of neither the 32-pixel coverage tile nor a surround's thirds — and every colour channel and the (instance, cluster) under every pixel must agree, at both `single` and `surround3`. Shadows are set off for it, because they turn occlusion off with them and this GPU would otherwise have taken them, which is also why the module's other cases never exercise the Hi-Z at all.

The multi-view cases add four. **The layouts**, on the CPU with no device: a single view over the whole target; a flat surround whose three off-axis rectangles meet and whose union is the single view's, with the centre one centred; a turned surround whose side cameras carry the yaw and whose side views alone carry the peripheral LOD multiplier; and a Panini view whose oversampling factor is the arithmetic's, is 1 at d = 0, and is refused past `k_max_oversample`. **The off-axis projection** against `perspective_reversed_z` through a centred rectangle, and a shifted rectangle putting its own centre line at normalized x of zero. **The Panini inverse map** against the projection it inverts, azimuth by azimuth, and its centre against the source's centre. **The frame itself**, on a GPU: a flat surround's centre monitor against a single view of one monitor from the same camera — equal visible-pair counts and *the same ids and the same colors, all 16,384 pixels of them* — and a 35-degree surround with one cube in front of each view's own centre, where each view's centre pixel names its own instance through the rasterizers **and** through the ray path, which proves the union structure serves every view. The d = 0 Panini case renders the same scene both ways and reports how many pixels differ. `Stats::gpu_memory` is checked with the rest of the statistics: a device-local total above zero always, and a budget within that total on a device with `VK_EXT_memory_budget`.

The pictures are pinned end to end by engine-view's own suite and by the comparison in that page: the FlightHelmet at a fixed orbit through `--raster hw`, `--raster vertex`, `--raster rt --shadows rt`, `--deform wave`, and `--grid-instances 3` is **byte-identical** before and after the move out of `main.cpp` (PSNR null, SSIM 1, FLIP 0 on all five).

**Skinning adds four cases**, over a two-bone bar built in the test rather than imported — a skinned glTF written at test time would be testing the importer too, and what these are about is the renderer's half of the contract. The bar is a square column sliced into 32 rings, bound root-to-tip by height, so every vertex of the top half moves when the tip joint turns. At the **bind pose** the skinned instance draws exactly what a rigid instance of the same mesh draws: 4,776 covered pixels, 0 id words differing, worst depth difference 4.7e-10 against the documented 2e-7 (they cannot be bit-identical — the rigid path dequantizes inside the rasterizer while the skinned one reads the float the pool stored). A **60° bend** moves the picture where `anim::skin_positions` says: the drawn rectangle's bend axis is [63, 109] against a projected [62.6, 110.0], 1,099 of 1,330 pixels change coverage, and the bent bar is visibly wider than the straight one. **Culling stays conservative** over the whole 0–90° sweep: twelve phases, each rendered with the exact displacement bound and again with eight times it, 0 id words differing at any of them, with the bar filling the frame where a frustum test can actually bite. And the three paths **agree on a posed frame**: the vertex path writes the same words as the mesh shader (0 of 1,278 covered pixels differ when this was written; 0 of 1,450 on 2026-09-23) and the ray path differs on 0 coverage and 1 triangle (0 and 0 on 2026-09-23), which is what a silhouette costs on a rigid mesh. The vertex path is the reference both are compared against, so on a device without one of the other two the case still runs and says which it skipped.

**The pool's suballocation adds a fifth case**, and it is the two halves of the budget. With the default budget over eight skinned bars, nothing overflows, `deform_entries` equals the visible pair count — plus `shadow_pairs` where the default request draws cascaded shadow maps, since a cascade's entries of a deformed instance get blocks of their own — and the pool's occupancy is the cut's 272 vertices rather than the instances' meshes. With `deform_pool_kib` set to **1** — 85 vertices, a third of what that cut needs — the pairs that did not fit draw their rest pose: the picture is still covered, every pixel still names an instance of the scene, `deform_overflow_entries` is nonzero, and placed plus refused equals the visible pairs (and the maps' pairs) exactly. That the budget is in kibibytes is what makes the second half writable at all; a mebibyte is more than a bar's whole mesh.

**A sixth case covers normal cones on a posed instance** (`a turned joint's clusters are not culled by their rest-pose cones`). The bar cannot carry it, because its clusters wrap all four sides and have no cone. The fixture is a closed sphere of 2,208 triangles bound wholly to a head joint and turned 150° about the vertical, with a rigid copy beside it. The frame's cut is set to the leaves (`FrameDesc::lod_px = 0`). A CPU witness, which runs with or without a GPU so the container's v3 builds check it as well, first establishes that the case is real: 8 of the skinned ball's 24 leaf clusters are culled by their rest-pose cones from this camera, and 6 of those face it once turned. The frame is then rendered with cones on and off through all four paths — `hw`, `vertex`, `sw` and `rt`, the first and last skipped by name on a device without them — and every id word and every depth must agree. The rigid ball must also lose clusters to the cone test, since a test that passed because the cones were off everywhere would be worth nothing. **On the unfixed shader the case failed** with 1,676 id words and 751 depths different of 2,639 covered pixels, identically in all four paths. It now passes with 0 and 0 in each, and cones on still take the frame from 48 visible pairs to 41.

**Shadow casters have three cases of their own** (`shadow_caster_tests.cpp`, [Shadows](#shadows)). In **`a cluster the cone test drops from the picture still casts its shadow`**, four casters (a single-sided card, a thin slab, a floating cube and an L) each stand between the sun and a ground plane with the camera on the dark side. Each is drawn in the shadow view three ways, through the mesh shaders and again through the vertex path: cones off, cones on with the casters dropped, and cones on with them kept. The two paths count drawn pairs in different words of their argument blocks and the casters in neither, so a change to how either counts cannot quietly take the casters with it. A CPU witness first shows that the cone test drops clusters of every caster from that camera, and all of the card's. The GPU half then requires the kept frame's shadowed ground to equal the cones-off frame's pixel for pixel. It requires the dropped frame to lose the card's whole shadow (521 pixels at 320×240) and part of the cube's (113 of 1,246). The two cones-on frames must draw the same pairs with the same ids, and drawn pairs plus casters must equal the cones-off cut. **`the ray path traces the casters' shadows and not the casters`** draws the card through `--raster rt`. Its ids are the same words with and without the casters in the structures, and its shadow comes back. **`the casters are on only where they mean something`** checks `resolve_settings` on a synthetic device: on by default with traced shadows, off with cones off, with the switch off, on the ray path without shadows, under templates, and without shadows at all. The two GPU cases skip by name where ray queries are absent (`unavailable_reason`'s sentence), which is every case on the TITAN Xp. The measurement on the Khronos samples is a fourth case, skipped by default (`-tc='renderer: shadow casters on the Khronos samples' -ns -s` in a release build, under the GPU lock).

**The ray tracing chain's compact index space has a CPU case** (`rt_capacity_tests.cpp`): drawn and caster entries share the same eligible-pair bound, an over-limit account drops casters without refusing traced rendering, and preliminary resolution defers admission. The shared-account case adds prefix, four ring reservations and a rounded tile floor, excludes static and untraced pairs, and verifies tile withholding before prefix refusal. **The ray tracing chain's capacity has three cases** (`rt_capacity_tests.cpp`, [The ray tracing chain's memory](#the-ray-tracing-chains-memory)). **`grows ahead, shrinks late, steps, and stops at the limit`** is the policy on the CPU: nothing moves inside a window, a whole window of small frames shrinks it, half the headroom eaten grows it to the demand plus the headroom in steps, a demand that swings between two cuts settles on the larger, and past the limit it stays at the limit. **`a chain sized by the frame draws what a chain sized by the scene draws`** flies a 3×3 grid of heightfields far, near, far, nearer and mid-way through the mesh path with traced shadows and through the ray path, beside a renderer whose chain keeps the whole union, with a four-frame window, no headroom and a 64-cluster step so it shrinks onto every cut and must grow for every larger one: every capture must be the same colour and the same ids, and the chain must have shrunk under the union and grown back (on the RTX 5090: 0 of 307,200 colour bytes and 0 of 230,400 id words differ at any of the ten captures, with 2 grows, 3 shrinks and a smallest capacity of 64 against a union of 6,453). **`past the budget a frame drops whole instances and costs only shadows`** gives the same grid a 1 MiB budget (163 clusters) under a cut that wants 400: the frames count their overflow and the instances they dropped, the capacity stays at the limit, the id channel is the full chain's word for word, and no pixel of the shadow view is in shadow that the full chain left lit. The records half of the rule is `domain/gfx`'s records test ([gfx](gfx.md)).

**The cascaded shadow maps have ten cases** (`shadow_map_tests.cpp`, over the casters' fixture, which `shadow_fixture.h` now shares with `shadow_caster_tests.cpp`; [Cascaded shadow maps](#cascaded-shadow-maps)). On the CPU: **the fit** covers every corner of every slice in every view (checked through each view's own inverse matrix, a second route to the corners), collapses an orbiting camera's framing to one cascade over the scene's bounds, starts the first slice at the scene's near side from outside and at a thousandth of the distance from inside, keeps every radius bit-identical while the camera turns on the spot, keeps every centre on its whole-texel grid while it moves, and holds a turned surround's corners too; and **the settings** resolve `csm` for `auto` without ray queries and `rt` with them, for an explicit `csm` on hw and vertex, never on direct, sw, auto or rt, with occlusion culling left on and the knobs clamped. On a GPU: **the maps cast what a CPU ray finds** — every caster, through the mesh path and the vertex path, each ground pixel whose ray to the sun (Möller-Trumbore in double precision against the caster's triangles) has the same answer for every pixel within two of it must be black or white accordingly: 0 of 33,456–34,740 interior pixels differ for any caster on either path on the RTX 5090, 304–921 of them shadowed, and the two paths' pictures are the same bytes. **A caster outside the camera's frustum casts**: the card above and beside a camera looking straight down at its shadow (a CPU witness first requires both of its clusters outside the frustum) shadows 61,997 interior pixels in the maps with 0 against the CPU ray — and, since 2026-10-18, under the rays too: a CPU witness requires both clusters inside the view's caster volume as well, and the traced shadow then differs from the maps' on 0 of 73,596 interior pixels (61,989 shadowed) and from the CPU ray on 0, with `shadow_casters` equal to the 38 pairs the CPU's own fit puts outside the frustum and inside the volume (the card's 2 and the ground's 36 beyond the view towards the sun); without the volumes (`off_frustum_casters` off) the traced shadow is 0 pixels and there are 0 casters, the old answer. **A point light's casters are its hull's**: with the stand-in lights on, the GPU builds the 40 casters the CPU's fit over the sun's volume and the lights' predicts (38 for the sun alone), and the sun's shadow is the same bytes with and without the lights' volumes, since a caster outside the sun's sweep cannot meet a ray from the view towards the sun. **A caster away from the light is not one**: the same card moved 0.85 units the other way, outside the frustum and behind the receivers as the sun sees them, is outside the volume on the CPU, and on the GPU the casters are the ground's 36 alone and nothing is shadowed — the case that says the volume is tight rather than the scene. **The volumes change no pixel's surface**: with them on and off, on the mesh, vertex and ray paths, the ids are the same words and the drawn pairs the same count, the normals view the same bytes, and only the shadow view differs (192,051 colour bytes, the card's shadow). The volume itself has a CPU suite of its own (`caster_volume_tests.cpp`): over 400 random cameras — any direction, field of view and aspect, a third of them asymmetric like a surround's side views, a fifth with a far plane — and lights including one along the view, against it, overhead and along a face, every point a ray sampled along the light finds in the sweep (45,317) and every sphere one of whose sampled points is (10,695) passes the planes, and every point the planes accept is in the exact sweep (per-plane intervals in the sweep's parameter) short of the cap; the same for a point light's hull over 280 lights outside the frustum. Without the silhouette planes the tightness half fails 36,384 checks. **The light-view cull never changes the shadow**: the cube and the L with the cascades' frustum test on and off, in the shadow view and the shaded one, and the 129 × 129 heightfield close in, plain and under `--deform wave` (which exercises the cascades' own pool blocks), give 0 differing colour bytes and 0 id words while the test culls 143 of 198, 145 of 201 and 336 of 792 pairs out of the maps (334 of 780 on the TITAN Xp, whose GCC build makes a slightly different heightfield). And **mapped and traced shadows agree** where both are defined: against the ray-traced shadow view of the same frame, 0 interior pixels differ on each caster, with 2,333–2,652 pixels in the band and 31–41 of them grey. On the TITAN Xp, through the vertex path, every count above that does not need rays is the same to the pixel. Another case, on a GPU, is the **traced shadow's offset** ([Ray-traced](#ray-traced)): the same casters on a ground one mesh 5 km across, 0 interior pixels against a CPU ray fired from the lifted point the offset rule gives, 0 of 2,322–2,637 band pixels either, 297–903 shadowed per caster; it skips where nothing traces, which is the TITAN Xp. The TITAN-Xp-like profile's case in `renderer_tests.cpp` checks that the default request draws maps there through the indexed draw with occlusion culling on, with the picture's ids unchanged. The measurement on the Khronos samples is an eleventh case, skipped by default (`-tc='renderer: cascaded shadow maps on the Khronos samples' -ns -s` in a release build, under the GPU lock; `ENGINE_SHADOW_SAMPLES`, `ENGINE_SHADOW_CASCADES`, `ENGINE_SHADOW_NORMAL_OFFSET`, `ENGINE_SHADOW_PICTURE_LOD_ONLY` and `ENGINE_SHADOW_NO_TIMING` narrow it). It asserts that at the picture's cut no interior pixel gets opposite answers from the maps and the rays, and it keeps the view that disagrees most as three PNGs in its kept scratch directory: the rays, the maps, and where they differ.

**The pool over the casters' run and the tail has five cases** (2026-10-18, roadmap R84; RTX 5090, `msvc-debug`). `renderer: a deformed caster outside the frustum casts its pose into the rays` (`shadow_map_tests.cpp`) is the off-frustum card under `--deform lattice` at two poses: the maps and the rays shadow 63,086 and 63,271 ground pixels at the first, 57,249 and 57,523 at the second, and differ on 0 of 73,596 and 0 of 71,852 interior pixels; the two poses' traced shadows differ on 9,576 pixels and the maps' on 9,693, and without the volumes the rays cast nothing, as every deformed card did before. `renderer: a deformed caster the pool has no room for casts nothing, not its rest pose` is the overflow rule under `--deform identity`, where the pose is the rest pose and so the two rules part only in what they cast: with room the rays shadow 64,017 pixels, with one KiB of pool (85 vertices) 0 — every caster of the card refused, 41 entries in all — and no pixel the roomy frame lights, the same ids, the same 38 casters culled; under the rest-pose rule it would have cast all 64,017. `clas records: a deformed caster reads its block, and one with none is not built` (`domain/gfx`) holds that rule entry by entry: of ten deformed casters, the five with a block are built from it byte for byte as the CPU writer has them, the five without are in no count and no record. `terrain shadows: the dunes behind the camera cast their traced shadows into the view` (`terrain_shadow_tests.cpp`) is the owner's picture: 64 m of moving dunes drawn through the pool's terrain stage, the sun 9° up behind a camera two metres over the sand; the rays differ from the maps on 0 of 37,465 interior pixels (23,601 shadowed), and without the off-frustum casters on 20,791 — 22,192 pixels of the view are shadowed by dunes outside it. `dynamic instances: a skinned loaded instance beside the tail draws through the pool` is B's: a bending two-bone bar among the loaded instances of a dynamic scene, a tail of six boxes, through no shadows, the cascaded maps and traced shadows — 0 id, 0 depth and 0 colour differences against the same instances loaded whole, with the tail and without it, the pool's entries the bar's alone, and a skinned instance in the tail refused by name with the scene unchanged.

**Depth ties have three cases** (`visibility_tie_tests.cpp`; the rule is [gfx](gfx.md)'s "The tie rule"). **`coincident copies resolve to the last one, every run, every rasterizer`** draws 24 copies of one box at one transform, so every covered pixel is a 24-way tie, six times through each of the mesh shaders, the indexed vertex draw, the capacity vertex draw (on a device opened without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader` and `geometryShader`, which is what selects it), the software rasterizer and the ray path. Every pixel must name the last copy, every repeat must equal the first, and the three hardware rasterizers must write the same words. **`a tie between the two occlusion passes resolves as one pass does`** gives the second of two coincident copies a large `bounds_padding`, which moves no vertex, and frames away and then toward them, so the padded copy is in the previous frame's cut and occlusion pass 1 draws it while pass 2 draws the other: the picture must equal the single-pass one, with the padded copy winning everywhere. **`back-to-back faces resolve the same way every run and with occlusion`** is the palms' case, a curved sheet and its reverse in one mesh with cones off. On the atomic-append id the first two failed — the last copy held none of the 2,857 covered pixels on any rasterizer or the ray path, and occlusion on and off differed at 2,356 — and the third passed. Every repeat matched its first there too: a fixture this small fills a handful of workgroups, whose appends land in the same order each time, so what the cases catch is the rule and the two passes, not run-to-run noise, which needs the flythrough's scale to show.

**The pass list.** The GPU buckets a frame's record carries (`scene::PassMs`, every flythrough line's `gpu_ms`) are named once, in `ENGINE_RENDERER_PASS_BUCKETS` in `scene_renderer.h` (2026-11-15, roadmap T85): `FrameStats` and `Stats` declare their `gpu_<name>` fields from it, `collect_slot` sums each frame's buckets into the run's and works out `unbucketed` (the total less the list's top-level buckets) by it, and `frame_record` writes each into the record's field of its name. Until then the list was kept by hand in four places, and a bucket added to one and not the others was missing from that output with nothing failing, which is how the summary came to lack 15 of 29 (T78); `Stats` lacked the chain's six zones, `tables` and `unbucketed`, which it now sums like the rest. A bucket the list has and the record's schema lacks does not compile; `flythrough: every pass bucket of the record comes from the one pass list` holds the other direction, failing by name for a schema field the list lacks. A new bucket is one line of the list, one field of `PassMs` in `schemas/`, and its zones in `collect_slot`.

## Performance notes

Nothing about the frame changed in the move, and the numbers in [apps](apps.md) and [gfx](gfx.md) still hold. Two allocations were added and both are outside the frame: the render graph is heap-allocated once (it is not default-constructible), and `capture()` allocates its staging buffers per call. The visibility buffer and the visible list gained `gfx::BufferUsage::TransferSrc` so a capture can read them; nothing in a frame copies from either.

**The fixed cost of a frame** — what it costs with nothing in view — is what [E9](../experiments/e9-multi-view.md) found dominates the owner's 11520×2160, and where the renderer's own passes were rebuilt.

- **The Hi-Z pyramid is folded, not built a mip at a time.** `Targets::hiz_dispatches` is `gfx::hiz_dispatch_count(mips)` and `add_hiz` records that many passes per view per build, each pushing one `gfx::HizParams` that names the source mip and how many folds to write; the shader does the rest in shared memory ([gfx](gfx.md)). The pyramid is bit-identical and the visible set is unchanged, which is the requirement: the Hi-Z is the input to a test that must not change the picture.
- **The resolve leaves the sky to the clear.** The resolve pass clears the colour target to the sky before it draws, so a pixel the scene does not cover is a fragment that would write the value already under it; `gfx::ResolveParams::sky_is_clear` says so and the shader discards instead ([gfx](gfx.md)). The renderer is entitled to set it because it owns both ends: `k_sky` in `scene_renderer.cpp` is the clear value **and** `ResolveParams::sky`, in one place, because two spellings of the same colour would make an uncovered pixel take whichever the clear said without anything saying so. **A scene that names a sky gives this up** ([The sky](#the-sky)): no clear value is the sky in every direction, so `sky_is_clear` is 0 there and every uncovered pixel is written; that cost is in the sky's own measurement.
- **The resolve does not read a 32×32 tile with nothing in it.** The last Hi-Z build of a frame leaves a coverage word per tile behind its pyramids in `Targets::hiz` — one per workgroup of its first dispatch, so it is free — and `ViewTarget::coverage_offset`/`coverage_pitch` are where each view's is. The resolve pass declares a `FragmentRead` of the Hi-Z buffer and `ResolveParams::coverage` points at it, **but only when `resolved_.occlusion` is set**, because that is the only arrangement in which nothing writes the visibility buffer between the last Hi-Z build and the resolve. The build after pass 1 writes no mask at all: it would be a truthful mask of a moment nothing reads.

**The rule that keeps the mask honest.** A pass added to `record_frame` that writes the visibility buffer *after* `add_hiz(1)` makes the mask a lie, and the failure is a 32×32 block of sky where a surface should be. Today the pass order makes that impossible — occlusion culling only runs in the two modes that have no software-raster pass and no ray trace — and `resolve.coverage` is gated on exactly that flag. Whoever changes the order changes the gate.

**Skinning adds nothing to the frame's allocations and one memcpy to its CPU cost.** [apps](apps.md) has the crowd numbers; two of them belong here. A thousand characters' matrices are **1.18 MB a frame**, one copy into a mapped buffer, which is what the 3×4 form was chosen for — the fourth row would make it 1.57 MB. And the pool pass costs the cut, not the scene: 1,325 visible clusters over 1,024 skinned instances deform in **0.132 ms** at 3840×2160, against 0.011 ms for a single instance's 8 clusters.

**What the pool pass costs, before and against E25's line** (RTX 5090, `msvc-debug`, 1920×1080, `--orbit 22`, `--deform wave --shadows off`, 240 frames; `before` is main's build with the per-instance pool, `after` is the per-frame suballocation, both measured back to back on the same machine). `alloc` is the suballocator, which did not exist before:

| Scene | cut (pairs) | `deform` before | `deform` after | `alloc` after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| heightfield `--grid 1025 --lod 1` | 373 | 0.0080 ms | 0.0084 ms | 0.0061 ms |
| heightfield `--lod 0.25` | 1,228 | 0.0090 ms | 0.0092 ms | 0.0113 ms |
| heightfield `--lod 0.06` | 4,352 | 0.0121 ms | 0.0116 ms | 0.0275 ms |
| 64 FlightHelmets `--lod 1` | 562 | 0.0093 ms | 0.0085 ms | 0.0085 ms |
| 64 FlightHelmets `--lod 0.05` | 24,131 | 0.0223 ms | 0.0206 ms | 0.1234 ms |
| 1,024 foxes, skinned, 3840×2160 † | 1,325 | 0.1341 ms | 0.1323 ms | 0.0103 ms |

† with `--anim-lod off`, because the default coarsens that crowd to LOD3 and a frozen instance hands the pool pass no bone matrices at all — which takes the same row to **0.024 ms**. That is the animation LOD doing its job rather than the pool's layout doing anything, and it is why the comparison above pins the flag.

Three things it says. **The pool pass itself did not move** — within ±5% at every cut size, which is what a layout change that touches only where a workgroup writes should look like, and E25's 9.4 µs fixed cost plus 0.9 µs per 1,000 visible clusters still describes it (here: 7.8 µs fixed, 0.53 µs per 1,000). **The skinned crowd's 0.13 ms is not the layout's fault and the new layout does not fix it**: at 1,024 instances a workgroup reads a different instance's bone-matrix array and a different `DeformDesc`, and the pass is latency-bound on those scattered reads rather than on the 1.6 MB it writes. Packing the blocks does not change which arrays a workgroup reads; what would is sorting the visible list by instance so that consecutive workgroups share a matrix array, and that is a change to the cull pass, not to the pool. **The allocator is the new cost, and it is serial**: one workgroup means about 5 µs per 1,000 entries, fine at an ordinary cut and 0.12 ms at a 24,000-pair one. A two-level scan — block sums in parallel, one serial pass over the block sums — keeps the exact cursor and removes it; it is the first thing to do here if a frame ever has that many deformed pairs in it.

## Not yet

Multi-view got the per-frame working set split ([above](#multi-view-a-viewset-over-one-scene)), so a second `SceneRenderer` on one `GpuScene` is no longer what §4.6 wants — one renderer draws the whole set. What is still open there: a per-view **internal resolution** and the shading-rate half of foveation (the `ViewQuality::shading_rate` stub), which need `VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate` in the RHI; peripheral LOD under the ray chain, which [one cut for every view](#one-cut-for-every-view) gives up (a coarser side monitor would need its own structures, or rays that leave its surface by the two cuts' difference); a filtered color-domain Panini resample; multi-window presentation and per-output HDR metadata (engine-view has one swapchain); and the screen-space passes §4.6 says run per view, none of which exist yet — there is no TAA, no denoiser and no upscaler to run per view. Changing `RenderSettings` without rebuilding the `GpuScene` and the `SceneRenderer`: the deformed-vertex pool and the ray tracing chain are sized by the settings, so engine-host rebuilds both and keeps only the `SceneData`, which is where the import and the clustering cost is. Streaming ([above](#geometry-streaming-the-gpu-half-of-pages-and-residency)) is built for geometry and **only** for geometry: the textures are still uploaded whole, the acceleration structures are sized by the frames rather than by a budget streaming shares ([The ray tracing chain's memory](#the-ray-tracing-chains-memory)) and their bucketing scratch is still four bytes for every pair in every view, and `04 §4.9`'s "one residency manager, three page types, one budget with per-type floors" is one page type with one budget. A page's bytes now come out of the `.clusters` container by range, so the budget bounds host memory as well as device memory — but only in the **steady state**: the load still materializes the merged streams and `attach_page_source` releases them afterwards, so the peak working set is what it always was. Making the load never read them needs `geometry::merge_paged_cluster_meshes` to take the merged vertex and triangle bases from the page table instead of from `mesh.vertices.size()`. Streaming also refuses a deformed or skinned scene and `--rt-templates`, for the reasons in that section, and a scene without a container behind every mesh keeps the in-memory source. The reference path tracer and the accept-or-reject loop's automation ([04 §4.8](../plan/04-renderer.md#48-reference-renderer-and-objective-optimization)) — `render.compare` is the metric half of it, and the integrator is Phase 2's.

**A moving terrain** ([The dunes in time-lapse](#the-dunes-in-time-lapse)): its scene grid is never re-based, so its coarse clusters' LOD errors are the rest pose's and grow stale by up to twice the level's padding as the time-lapse runs; rebuilding the grid's DAG at the current time in the background and swapping it in at a field boundary, where the surface is exactly a field, is the fix. A ring's chunks are re-based whenever a re-centre rebuilds them, and not otherwise: a ring the camera never leaves ages like the grid, and a re-centre asked for by the padding rather than the camera — every chunk rebuilt through the same swap — is the same fix there. Until 2026-10-03 engine-host's `render.*` methods accepted `time_rate` and built the terrain level, but nothing on the protocol side ran a `TerrainMotion` or built a ring set (`RenderSettings::terrain_rings` was not in the protocol's settings), so a moving terrain drawn through the protocol stood still at its rest pose (the terrain stage writes the rest pose for a level whose table names no field). **That is closed** (`c5a37706`, [One request, two hosts](#one-request-two-hosts)): engine-host holds a `MovingGround` for each scene, which lays out the rings or the world's tiles round the call's first camera and steps a `TerrainMotion` before every frame, and `terrain_rings`, `terrain_tiles`, `terrain_far_levels` and `time_rate` are fields of the protocol's `RenderSettings` and `ground_time_s` one of `render.load`'s. **The rings** ([The rings in the scene](#the-rings-in-the-scene)) are built at load on the calling thread; a first frame that waited for nothing would draw the grid alone and swap the rings in when they were built. A re-centre freezes the rings' pairs while the field worker carries them over, which at a week a second is a visible pause of the sand if a ring reaches its b meanwhile; carrying the pair over on the ring worker, beside the chunks, would leave only the frame that records the copies. The pool's allocator is still the one serial workgroup, and a terrain's cut is by far its largest tenant (the costs are in that section). The dark shards traced shadows drew on the far ground in the owner's surround, which this list had put down to the rings' sunken hole or skirts, were the views' different cuts in one structure and are closed (2026-10-09, [One cut for every view](#one-cut-for-every-view)); a single view's specks were rays from under fold-overs in the terrain's coarse clusters (the roadmap's F17, [Ray-traced](#ray-traced), 2026-10-10), which the LOD builder no longer makes (2026-10-11, [geometry](geometry.md#heightfield-levels-never-fold)).

**The world's tiles** ([The ground from the world's tiles](#the-ground-from-the-worlds-tiles), ADR-0050): a window's move freezes its level and drops the fields it had after b, so in a time-lapse at a day or a week a second the sand dips where a moved window's level waits for its next field (the model's window ratios of 4.9 and 11); carrying those fields over with the pair, or a window the fields wrap round (a clipmap's torus, where a move evaluates the strip it moved into for every field the level holds and freezes nothing), is the fix. A tile's rest pose is re-based only when it is rebuilt, as a ring's chunk is. A tile source serves heights, not maps: every tile samples the scene's baked maps in the grid's UV frame, clamped at the grid's edge, which past a scene's ridges and basins is the maps' edge texels and on a desert of plain sand is sand. The protocol's `render.*` built no tile set until 2026-10-03; it does now (`c5a37706`: `terrain_tiles` and `terrain_far_levels` in `settings`, laid out by `MovingGround` in both hosts, [One request, two hosts](#one-request-two-hosts)). Ground tiles beside streamed placements are refused (a dynamic scene has no pool). The far tier this paragraph used to lack (past the outermost ring nothing was drawn) shipped on 2026-10-03 (`2efc7749`, [ADR-0051](../adr/0051-the-far-ground-is-the-renderers.md); [Ground to the horizon](#ground-to-the-horizon), whose own text lists what is still open there); a ring whose tiles are a few cells a side still costs the world's ring a tile each. **Building the tiles is the cost**: at 100 m/s over `desert-endless` a frame rebuilt 33 tiles and offscreen that was 38 ms of host wall at the median ([the flight](../experiments/world-tiles-flight-2026-09-30.md)); rebuilds of what changed (2026-10-03, `4afee714`, [A rebuild costs what changed](#what-a-frame-waits-for)) halved it to 18.7 ms building the same tiles, and the windowed flight is measured — at 1080p at 100 m/s the finest ring is 22 m (11 frames) behind the camera at the median and 50 m at most, 2.5 m behind at 30 m/s, with no frame waiting for a tile ([the experiment](../experiments/world-tiles-window-2026-10-03.md), a shared machine, so upper bounds). **Still not measured: a windowed flight with the far levels in**, because the owner's session was locked and a locked session presents at about 4 Hz ([the far ground's page](../experiments/far-ground-2026-10-03.md)); offscreen a rebuild that covers kilometres costs about four times as much with them. A tile whose neighbour changes ring is still rebuilt whole where only its border moved.

**The sand close up** ([The sand close up](#the-sand-close-up)): the ripples' speed is a stylized `ripple_celerity` per m² of transport rather than the reptation flux over their height (the erg scenes' 2,000 runs them a hundred times faster than real ones, "Ripples that move"), and their flattening steps once an hour inside a storm's band; no glints off single grains; a footprint in the overlay does not break the ripples it lands in; no wet sand; the detail is never a sampled texture — a detail map or a grain atlas would bring back the edges this was built without. The filter's variance transfer is isotropic, where the ripples' slopes lie along the wind alone, and it does not model the ripples' self-shadowing at a grazing sun, which is what makes real ripples read at dawn; and, until 2026-10-03, the protocol's `render.*` handed a surface time to the detail of nothing, because nothing there moved a terrain (above): it now runs the same `TerrainMotion`, which is what sets the scene's surface time (`GpuScene::set_ground_time`), so a protocol call's detail reads the time its ground has reached as engine-view's does.

### Explicit flora motion traits (G86)

Species names and compliance now come from the geometry-level flora catalogue, shared with the
optional generator's profile IDs and diagnostics. Known species keep their existing four wind
coefficients. `flora_mesh` rejects an unknown species instead of silently applying a default;
`flora_stiffness` returns zero coefficients for that invalid name. This validates mesh ingestion,
not the per-frame hot loop. See [the profile audit](../experiments/tree-profile-audit.md).

### Sward contact compatibility (G90)

**Superseded for drawing by R95**: a `sward` mesh is now posed as a field on the GPU
([The field kind](#the-field-kind)) and the CPU poser never sees it; what follows still holds for
`flora_mesh` and `flora_part_poses` called on a sward table directly, which the regression keeps.
Sward uses a parentless non-woody motion part for each blade, including part zero. The CPU
compatibility poser permits those parts to receive the existing walker-capsule push when they
have a structural table and no load-bearing/collider flags. Tree roots keep their existing
policy. A regression checks contact, fixed roots, a distant unaffected blade and recovery.
This remains the existing 12-tick (0.2 s at 60 Hz) recovery, not persistent walked-track history.
The separately briefed field-motion path needs a quality-gated world-space contact/history
field before long-lived flattened paths can be claimed; the solver adds no such frame allocation.

## Sampling over time: the measurement rule

[ADR-0064](../adr/0064-every-measurement-is-native.md) (the owner, 2026-11-14): every budget,
cost pair, benchmark and walk is taken with reconstruction off at the output's own resolution, and
no cost is accepted because a reconstruction mode makes the frame rate acceptable. The renderer's
part of holding that is that **every record says what sampled its frame, and a record that is not
a native measurement has no cost in it**.

- `renderer::Reconstruction` (`settings.h`) is the state: the provider (`Off` until one is built,
  roadmap R158), whether the inputs below were on, and the internal and the output sizes.
  `Reconstruction::native()` is the rule: no provider, and drawn at the output's size.
  `SceneRenderer::reconstruction()` gives the renderer's, and every folded frame's `FrameStats`
  carries it.
- `renderer::frame_record` writes it as the record's `reconstruction` block
  (`engine.scene.Reconstruction`) and puts the frame's times in `gpu_ms` only when it is native;
  otherwise they go under `reconstructed.gpu_ms` and `gpu_ms` is null. `summarize_frames` holds a
  summary to the same rule over its records: one record that was not native and the summary has no
  `gpu_ms`, carries that record's block, and its markers' `total_ms` are zero.
  `renderer::measurement_keys` is the same rule for the summary line engine-view writes by hand.
  Both hosts' benchmark lines go through these, so neither can write a reconstructed figure where
  a cost is read.
- **The inputs alone are a native frame.** With `renderer.reconstruction.inputs` on and no
  provider the frame is drawn at an offset and costs the motion pass more; its record keeps
  `gpu_ms`, says `inputs: true`, and names the pass's time as `gpu_ms.motion`. That is ADR-0064's
  one exception, reconstruction's own cost, which is measured on and off at native size.
- The tools' half is `Get-ReconstructionRefusal` (`tools/lib/FrameBudget.psm1`), which
  `tools/frame-budget.ps1` (exit 5) and `tools/flythrough.ps1` (a row that says "refused") ask
  before they read a number ([bench](bench.md#frame-budgets), [apps](apps.md#flythroughs)).

What is not under the rule yet: `render.capture`'s and `render.load`'s statistics
(`engine.protocol.RenderStats`), which carry no block. Nothing can turn a provider on through the
protocol today; roadmap R159 adds the block there with the registration point.

## Sampling over time: the inputs

Roadmap R154, from [the design](../experiments/temporal-sampling.md#part-2-what-the-renderer-must-provide).
Every method that samples over time, the engine's own and any vendor's, reads the same things: a
frame drawn at a sub-pixel offset, where each pixel's surface was in the last frame, the depth, and
last frame's own state. This section is what the renderer makes of them. **One thing reads them**,
the engine's own accumulation ([below](#sampling-over-time-the-accumulation), roadmap R158, which
turns them on when it is on), and **all of it is behind one switch, off by default**:
`renderer.reconstruction.inputs` (a tunable read at load; `ResolvedSettings::reconstruction_inputs`,
never on the direct path). Off, the renderer holds a null pointer where the state would be: no
buffer, no pipeline, no pass, no offset, and the frame is the frame it always was to the byte,
which is what every other test of this module runs as. On, `src/motion_pass.h` (`MotionPass`) owns
everything below.

**The sub-pixel offset** is in one place, `ViewSet::update(camera, offset_x, offset_y)`: the
sample of every pixel sits that far from its centre, in source pixels, x right and y down, which
is a shear of the projection's third column. `View::view_proj` and `View::clip_to_ray` are made
from the sheared projection, so the rasterizers' pixels, the traced primaries' rays and the
resolve's reconstruction move together and a pixel still meets its triangle exactly; the depth a
pixel holds does not move. The sequence is Halton(2, 3) less a half (`sample_offset`), the phase
the renderer's own count of frames since the last reset modulo eight (`k_sample_phases`); a ratio
of n will take `ceil(8 n²)` (R160). **Not offset**: the LOD's scale (`proj_scale`, so the cut does
not change with the phase) and `View::view_proj_center`, the view-projection the offset was added
to, which is what motion is measured with. **Offset, where the design said not**: the cull's
frustum and its Hi-Z tests. They read `view_proj` like every other pass, and that is the right
matrix for them: the frustum that must hold every cluster the picture draws is the one the picture
was drawn through (the un-offset one would lose a cluster from a strip of edge pixels up to half a
pixel wide), and pass 2 tests the Hi-Z built from this frame's own offset depth, so the test and
the pyramid agree and occlusion still never changes the picture.

**Last frame's state.** `MotionPass` keeps last frame's un-offset view-projection per view and its
eye as a `WorldPos` (the eyes' difference between two frames is taken in f64 on the CPU and handed
to the pass inside a matrix: [ADR-0053](../adr/0053-world-positions-are-f64-and-the-gpu-sees-none.md)),
and **last frame's visibility buffer**: the renderer has two, and each frame draws into the one
the frame before last drew into (`swap_visibility`, at the top of `record_frame`), so the other
still holds last frame's words when this frame's passes run. Nothing reads it in this stage; it is
there for R158's history test, at 8 bytes a pixel. `FrameDesc::history_reset` (and
`SceneRenderer::reset_history`) is how a host says a frame has no frame before it, a camera cut, a
teleport or a load: its motion is measured from itself and the phase starts again. A resize resets
too.

**The moved instances.** `SceneRenderer::move_instances` hands the indices to `note_moves` before
the scene writes the new placements, and an instance that has ever moved keeps an entry in a table
