sorted by instance (`gfx::MovedInstance`: its cell and its 3x4), holding **last frame's**
transform: each frame's copy of the table goes into that frame slot's own buffer, and then every
entry takes the transform this frame draws. An instance that moved once and stopped is in the
table with the transform it has, so its vectors are the still scene's. The design flagged moved
instances in `gfx::InstanceDesc`; its `flags` word has no bit left (the hand-off's stamp takes the
top 22), so the pass searches the table instead, a binary search a pixel, and only in a frame
whose table is not empty. The table holds `k_motion_moved_capacity` (4,096) instances; one moved
past that is not followed (its motion is the camera's) and the renderer says so once. **Not
followed at all: an instance of a world's tail that moves between frames.** A tail's slots are
handed over whole (`set_dynamic_instances`) and an instance has no identity across two tails, so
the pass cannot know where one stood; its vectors are the camera's. A frame that changes a tail's
layout is one whose vectors the accumulation does not trust, and it holds every pixel's history to
the point's depth instead ([what holds a trail](#what-a-trail-is-and-what-holds-it), R194). A
game's actors are not that case: they are loaded instances the host moves, and a move does not
change the layout (R194; before it, a move in a streamed world's scene dropped every vector to the
camera's for that frame).

**A deformed vertex's last position: the pool pass writes each vertex twice** (the design's way
(c)). The deformed-vertex pool is suballocated per frame, so last frame's position of a vertex is
not at this frame's address. The pool pass's push block already names everything a stage reads
that changes from frame to frame (the deform table, the deformer's clock, the trees' part poses),
so the second write is **the same pipeline dispatched again over the same blocks**, into a second
pool of the same size, with last frame's values in those three fields (`MotionPass::previous`) and
no normal pool. No shader changed, and a stage a capability adds later gets motion by being run
twice. It is exact at a cut change (the blocks are this frame's) and costs the pool pass again
whatever the resolution or the number of views. What "last frame's" is good for: the clock is a
number, so wherever there was a last frame; the table and the part poses are regions of per-slot
buffers, so only while last frame's slot has not been rewritten (two or more frames in flight) and
the scene's tables did not change under them (a streamed world's tail). Where they are not, the
second write reads this frame's inputs and a deformed vertex's motion is its instance's and the
camera's. **Not in it: a moving terrain's levels**, whose second write reads this frame's table
(last frame's fields may already be on their way back to the scene), so a dune ground in
time-lapse has no motion of its own; and the shadow cascades' runs, which no pixel names. **Way
(a)**, keeping last frame's pool with its slots and a pair-to-entry table per view, was not built:
it would save the second dispatch and cost the pool again plus four bytes a pair a view (67 MB a
view on the forest's 16.7 million pairs), and is wrong for a frame wherever the cut changed. The
second dispatch's milliseconds are the most it could give back; they are `gpu_ms.motion` less the
motion pass, and the pair is R158's to fly on the forest.

**The motion pass** is `motion.slang`, one thread a pixel over the finished visibility buffer,
recorded before the resolve; [gfx](gfx.md#motion-from-the-visibility-buffer) has the block and
what each kind of pixel reads. It writes **a buffer, not an image**: a `u32` a source pixel, the
views back to back as the visibility buffer is, two half floats, the pixels the pixel's point
moved across the picture since the last frame with neither frame's offset in them. The design
asked for an image because a vendor's method wants one; the engine's own reads an address like
everything else here, and the copy into an image is the vendor adapter's (R161), as the depth's
is. Its declaration is in `record_frame` (the graph's handles are there) and its body is
`MotionPass::record`; the second pool write rides the existing "deform" pass. Zones "motion" and
"motion pool", summed into `FrameStats::gpu_motion`, `Stats::gpu_motion` and the record's
`gpu_ms.motion`.

**Reading it**: `CaptureChannels::motion` fills `CapturedFrame::motion`, two floats a pixel in the
target's pixels (a Panini view through the resolve's own map), zero where the point was behind
last frame's camera; refused, with a sentence, by a renderer without the inputs.

**What it keeps on the device** (`SceneRenderer::motion_bytes`): 4 bytes a source pixel of motion
and 8 of last frame's visibility buffer, the pool's bytes again where the scene has a pool, and
per frame slot the views' blocks (416 bytes a view) and the moved table (256 KB). At 3840 × 2160
that is 33 MB and 66 MB, and 8 MiB of pool by default (64 MiB at the owner's setting). The log
says it once at load ("sampling over time's inputs", `device_bytes`, `pool_bytes`): measured
100,063,744 bytes on the desert overlook (no pool) and 107,845,144 on the grove (7,781,400 of
pool).

**What it costs, measured** (R154 leg 1b, 2026-11-14, `msvc-release`, RTX 5090, 3840 × 2160,
`--raster rt --shadows rt`, the bounce on, the scene's camera path, 240 warm-up frames, three
repeats; others held 70 to 99 % of the CPU throughout). Off, a capture of 16 frames is the same
bytes as main's copied-out build (84f6d872) on both scenes, and the path's median total is
within the pair's noise: grove 4.489, 4.456 and 4.440 ms on main, 4.622, 4.461 and 4.583 on the
branch (the two high ones all in the resolve, 0.1 ms, on a frame whose bytes are main's; the
inputs-on flights less their motion pass come to 4.45 to 4.49); overlook 2.894 and 2.937 on main,
2.940 and 2.877 on the branch; the vertex tier on the grove (`--raster vertex`), 3.683 on main and
3.691 on the branch. On, `gpu_ms.motion` (the pass and the pool's second write) is 0.067 ms at the
median and 0.068 at p99 on the overlook (no deformed instance: the pass alone), 0.088 to 0.095
at the median and 0.119 to 0.124 at p99 on the grove, whose twelve swaying trees add the second
write, and 0.096 (0.106) on the grove's vertex tier. A frame's whole total moves by about the same.
Not measured: a scene with hundreds of moved instances (the moved table's search; no host moves
that many yet), the forest. **A flight's repeats each start the history again at their first path
frame** (`fly_camera_path` marks it `history_reset`), so frame f of every repeat is drawn at the
same phase: before, the offset differed from repeat to repeat, the cut with it, and an inputs-on
flight was never `deterministic`. Not at the warm-up's first frame: engine-view's warm-up runs for
at least two seconds, a different number of frames each repeat.

**Held by** `tests/motion_tests.cpp`: the offset moves a view's picture by exactly its pixels and
leaves the LOD's scale and the depth alone (no device); without the inputs the renderer keeps
nothing and refuses the channel; a camera turned and stepped reprojects every pixel of a still
scene and its sky within 0.02 px of the CPU's double arithmetic, at an offset, and a frame with no
frame before it measures zero; a rigid instance moved and scaled follows its two transforms within
the same, and stands still a frame later; a deformed surface (the procedural deformer) through the
two pools matches the still scene's vectors with its clock held, moves when the clock does and
stops when it does not; and, with two frames in flight over three frames so each reads last frame's
inputs out of the other slot's region, a skinned bar that bends further and steps each frame
(the bones and the moved table together, on the mesh path and again on the vertex tier's indexed
draw) and a young palm swaying in a wind, each against its deformer's CPU mirror (`anim::skin_positions`;
`gfx::flora_bend` over the poses `flora_pose_instances` gives a tree laid out as `GpuScene` lays
it out): 0.0032 px and 0.0024 px at worst under vectors of 4 px.

## Sampling over time: the accumulation

Roadmap R158, stage 2 of [the design](../experiments/temporal-sampling.md#part-4-the-plan-in-stages):
**the engine's own accumulation at native resolution**. A frame drawn at a sub-pixel offset is one
sample of every pixel; this pass blends it into what the frames before it accumulated, so a crown's
edge is the average of its samples and not whichever one this frame drew. It is **off by default**
(`renderer.reconstruction.accumulation`, `off`, `on` or `mean`, read at load;
`ResolvedSettings::accumulation`), **nothing of it exists when it is off** (a null pointer: no
image, no pipeline, no pass, and the frame is the frame it was to the byte), and **it is not a
default of any interactive session**: that is the owner's to decide after walking it
([ADR-0064](../adr/0064-every-measurement-is-native.md), decision 7). On, it turns
[the inputs](#sampling-over-time-the-inputs) on, the renderer's `Reconstruction::provider` is
`Engine`, and so every record of such a frame is a reconstructed one: its times are under
`reconstructed.gpu_ms`, its `gpu_ms` is null and the budget tools refuse it
([the measurement rule](#sampling-over-time-the-measurement-rule)).

**Where it runs.** It is a [frame pass](#frame-passes) of the renderer's own
(`src/accumulation_pass.h`, `shaders/accumulate.slang`), registered at a second stage,
`FramePassStage::Reconstruction`, which `add_frame_pass` keeps after every pass that composites
light whenever each was registered: a medium's light is in the picture before it is sampled over
time. So an accumulated frame resolves into the linear image and ends on the one encode, like any
frame with a pass. It writes **an image of its own**, which is both the frame's picture and the
next frame's history: two half-float images swapped each frame, and the encode reads the one just
written in the linear image's place (`FramePassReport::color`, which is also how a provider's
output at another size will reach the encode, R159). The context a pass is handed gained what it
needs and nothing of its own: the motion buffer's handle (`FramePassContext::motion`) and the
display's curve (`display_knee`, `display_ceiling`). `record_frame` grew by those lines and no
pass; the vertex tier runs it (it reads buffers and images, no rasterizer); nothing in it keys on
a generator, and an imported static mesh gets all of it.

**The frames are averaged as the display shows them.** Each sample goes through the display's
curve (`display_tone1` and its ceiling, what `display_output` applies before the transfer) before
it is blended, and the blend goes back through the curve's inverse into the image, so the encode
shows exactly the blend. A mean of radiance lets one sample past the display's white own its
pixel (measured on the test's heightfield: 11 codes brighter than the mean of the frames as drawn
on a glint's pixels) and is not the supersampled picture, which is a mean of what is seen; it is
also what Karis's weighting by luminance is for. With an SDR target and no sky the curve is a
clamp at 1.

**What a pixel's history is held to**, in the shader's order. The design's rule was "the same
instance at that place, else a disocclusion"; the build departs from it in the second step, and
says why.

1. **The motion of the nearest surface in the 3 × 3** (the largest reversed-Z depth; an empty
   pixel is the farthest). A thin feature's edge pixel takes the feature's motion, so the pixel a
   leaf has just left looks up where the sky behind it was a frame ago, not where the leaf was.
2. **Whether anything can have been uncovered there, and only then the names.** A history tap
   whose surface **was moving last frame as this pixel's surface is moving now** (last frame's
   motion buffer, which the accumulation has the inputs keep, within
   `renderer.reconstruction.motion_match` pixels, a quarter by default) is the pixel's own
   whatever it names: under a held camera, a turn of the camera, or a sway slower than the match,
   nothing has been uncovered, and the sub-pixel offset alone changes what an edge pixel names
   every frame. Past the match **the names decide, by membership and not by equality**: last
   frame's visibility buffer (kept by the inputs) names the instance the tap showed, through the
   scene's pair table, and the tap counts only if that instance, or the empty sky, **is among the
   instances this frame's 3 × 3 holds**. Not "the same instance at the same pixel": a crown's
   edge pixel names a leaf in one frame and the sky in the next, and a rule that strict would
   restart every edge pixel every frame, which are the pixels that hold nine tenths of the
   aliasing ([the measurement](../experiments/temporal-sampling.md#what-the-difference-holds)).
   And not the names alone, which is what this pass did first: on leaf-cards' crowns at 121 m,
   four trees against a sky, a still view after sixteen frames stood 12.6 codes from the
   reference where the plain mean of the same sixteen frames stands 6.0, because a leaf seen
   through a gap last frame is often not among the nine samples of this one. Membership
   keeps an edge's history and still drops a disocclusion's: what an instance that moved away
   leaves behind names an instance the neighbourhood no longer holds. **An instance the host
   moves is never taken by the match** (`SceneRenderer::move_instances`: the motion pass's moved
   table, searched only in a frame that has one): it may have stood still last frame and be
   somewhere else in this one, which the first build with the match showed as a trail where a
   moved instance had stood (16 codes left of 36, where the names leave 6). What the match lets
   through is a trail no longer than the match over the weight, two and a half pixels at the
   defaults. The grain is the instance,
   not the pair: a pair changes with the LOD cut, and a history thrown away at every cut change is
   a flash across a cluster. On a frame where the scene's tables changed (a streamed world's
   tail) last frame's pairs cannot be read through this frame's table, so the test falls back to
   covered against empty and the colours decide.
3. **The colours.** What is left is clipped towards the 3 × 3's mean, to its mean ± γσ in YCoCg
   (Salvi 2016), along the line to the mean so the hue holds, **only where the pixel's surface
   moved further than the match**: γ is `renderer.reconstruction.clip_moving` (1.25) there, and
   `clip_still` for the rest, which is 0, no clip. A pixel that hardly moved has a history that is
   its own, and the nine samples of one frame are a poor witness against it: where all nine miss
   a leaf the box has no width and the clip takes the leaf out of the picture, whatever γ. With
   the clip on everywhere (γ 3 still, 1.25 moving) the crowns' held view stood 10.6 and 10.4 codes
   from the reference, and 9.9 and 9.8 at γ 6; without it 6.2 and 7.3. What is given up: under a
   surface that does not move, light that changes (a shadow sweeping a still ground) follows over
   the blend's length and is not cut short; and inside one instance, a part that crosses another
   slower than the match trails by up to the match over the weight.

Then the blend: the new frame's share is one over the frames since the last reset while that is
more than `renderer.reconstruction.weight` (so the frames after a reset weigh alike), and the
weight after. A pixel with no usable history shows this frame's sample. A history value that is
not a number is never kept. **A reset** (`FrameDesc::history_reset`, a resize, a frame this pass
did not draw between two, such as a debug view) starts again: the frame after one holds nothing
of the frame before, to the byte. The cycle is `renderer.reconstruction.phases` offsets of
Halton(2, 3), sixteen by default (the inputs alone keep eight).

**`mean` mode is the converged frame as a function of the scene.** The plain running mean of the
frames since the last reset at the pixel's own place: no motion, no names, no clip. A
`SceneRenderer::capture` in `mean` mode draws **one whole cycle from a reset** (it drives the
phase itself: a capture is otherwise one frame), so its picture is the mean of the cycle's offset
frames and a test holds it to a reference with a bound that is rounding and not noise
(`accumulation_tests.cpp`: two codes, from the eight-bit frames and the half-float path). In `on`
mode a capture is one frame and continues the history, which is how a pan or a wind is measured a
frame at a time (`engine-view --capture-every 1`).

**What it keeps on the device** (`SceneRenderer::accumulation_bytes`): 16 bytes a pixel in the two
images and 104 bytes a view a frame slot, beside the inputs' 16 bytes a pixel (their 12 and last
frame's motion buffer, 4, which only the accumulation asks them to keep: `motion_bytes` counts
it) and the frame passes' linear image at 8: 133 MB, 133 MB and 66 MB at 3840 × 2160, 332 MB
together, where the design reckoned about 300. Since R194 the inputs keep 4 bytes a pixel more for
the accumulation, each point's depth a frame ago (33 MB at 3840 × 2160; `motion_bytes` counts it),
and a view's block is 152 bytes.

**What it closes on, measured** (R154 leg 2, 2026-11-15, 01:46 to 02:28 local, `msvc-release`,
RTX 5090; [the design's method](../experiments/temporal-sampling.md#how-it-was-measured) and its
crops: 512 × 512 at the 4K target's pixel pitch, `--raster rt --shadows rt --no-lights --lod 1
--dither off`, the bounce off, the trees swaying at 0.7; the reference is that page's 64 offsets
drawn again by this build with everything off, and as drawn is one of them; others stood in the
GPU's line and held 1 to 58 % of the CPU, and nothing in the table is a time). Display luma
codes, rms over the crowns' rectangles; the accumulated picture is one frame a capture
(`--capture-every 1`), with the clip off:

| | as drawn | accumulated | the reference's | the bound |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| leaf-cards' crowns at 121 m, held, the 16th frame against the reference | 29.2 | **6.2** | | 8 |
| the same at 411 m | 28.8 | **7.3** | | 8 |
| a conifer (tree-species' spruce at 120 m) | 11.1 | **2.1** | | 8 |
| a slow pan, 1/8 px a frame, frame-to-frame change: 121 m | 30.3 | **3.82** | 4.28 | 1.5 times: 0.89 |
| 411 m | 35.5 | **3.51** | 3.11 | 1.13 |
| the conifer | 11.7 | **1.50** | 1.94 | 0.77 |
| a wind with the camera held, 90 frames, frame-to-frame change: 121 m | 12.3 | **2.94** | 3.50 | 0.84 |
| 411 m | 11.8 | **3.07** | 3.40 | 0.90 |
| the conifer | 5.26 | **0.92** | 1.17 | 0.79 |

**Which build drew which row.** The table was flown with `clip_still=0,clip_moving=0` on the build
that had the motion match and not yet the clip's gate or the moved instances' exception. The
shipped rule differs from it only at a pixel whose surface moves more than a quarter pixel a
frame, which none does in the held rows or the pan's (an eighth). **Flown again as shipped** on
the final build (leg 2b, 2026-11-15, 03:25 to 03:38, the references drawn again by it), all nine
rows came back to the table's figures to the hundredth: the wind at 121 m, 411 m and on the
conifer moves no pixel more than a quarter pixel a frame either, so the clip never applies there
(the same numbers with `clip_moving` 2 or 3, or the match at a half or a whole pixel). The clip on
everywhere, flown before the gate, was 1.20, 1.34 and 0.95 times the reference's. Near leaves at
30 m are where it acts: 10.54 codes from each step's reference and 0.65 times its change, as
shipped, against 10.77 and 0.61 with no clip. The conifer is
the species gallery's spruce, drawn by its own needle geometry: that scene has no needle image,
and the forest's needle images were not used.

**What sixteen frames can reach.** The renderer's own `mean` of the first sixteen offsets stands
6.0, 7.0 and 2.1 codes from the reference on the three views, so the blend is at what its samples
allow; the mean of 64 Halton offsets stands 2.8, 3.8 and 1.1 from the 64 the camera path turned
through, which is how far the two ways of making a reference agree (a turn is a uniform shift only
to 1.9 % at the crop's edge).

**In motion the picture is steadier than the reference and less like it.** Against the reference
slid with the pan the accumulated crowns stand 10.9 and 8.7 codes (the conifer 5.1), and against
each step's reference in the wind 8.1 and 8.6 (2.7; as drawn 24.2, 26.9 and 8.2): the four-tap
read softens what moves by fractions of a pixel, and the blend's length lags it. **Near leaves in
a wind** (30 m, a leaf fifteen pixels long, the case the plain emulation left at 11.3 codes from
16.2): 10.8 with the clip off and 10.3 with it on everywhere, the shipped rule between them, and a
frame-to-frame change of 0.61 to 0.78 times the reference's. So it does not trail more than the
plain blend did, and it does not yet follow a leaf that really moves: what is left there is lag
inside one instance, which the names cannot see (every leaf of a tree is one instance) and which
the sharper read and a clip that knows a thin feature are for.

**What each guard is worth**, on the crowns' held view at 121 m and 411 m, the clip at γ 3 and
1.25 in all three: the names alone 12.6 and 12.7; with the motion match 10.6 and 10.4; and the
match with no clip 6.2 and 7.3. A weight of 1/16 or 0.08 for 0.1 moves the held view by under 0.4
and the pan's change from 1.21 to 0.88 and 1.03 times the reference's at 121 m: a longer blend is
steadier and lags more (the wind's error 10.9 for 10.2).

**What it costs** (the grove at 3840 × 2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt`, the bounce on, its camera
path, 240 warm-up frames, one lease, others holding 16 to 35 % of the CPU; the build with the
match): off, 4.433 ms at the median and 5.062 at p99; on, 4.888 and 5.550, and again 4.892 and
5.528. **0.46 ms more at the median, 0.49 at p99**: 0.32 the accumulation and the encode it
brings (`reconstructed.gpu_ms.frame_passes`), 0.09 the motion pass and the pool's second write,
and the rest the resolve into the linear image. The first lease, the names alone: 4.436 and 4.439
off (5.050, 5.059), 4.883 and 4.894 on (5.531, 5.545), and the inputs alone 4.546 (5.207). The
log's bytes at load: 132,712,064 the accumulation's, 66,355,200 the linear image, 141,022,744 the
inputs' (the second motion buffer and 7.8 MB of pool in it): 340 MB. **Not measured**: the
forest (free commit stood at 34 to 44 GB, at the floor a load needs, and no hillside was flown), a
surround, any other machine, a scene with a medium registered, the shipped build's own flight.

**Not built, and what follows from each.** A view that resamples a wider source (Panini) is drawn
as it was (its `mean` is still its mean). A point that crosses a seam of a surround is a
disocclusion (the taps outside a view's rectangle do not count). The history is read with four
taps, bilinear, so a slow pan softens the picture over the blend's length; a sharper read
(Catmull-Rom over sixteen) is the known answer and is not in. The cross-fade's hash does not take
the phase, so the screen door is not blended (the design's third content fault). An instance of a
world's tail that moves has the camera's motion only, so its history is looked up in the wrong
place; since R194 a depth test bounds its ghost ([below](#what-a-trail-is-and-what-holds-it)). Water's reactivity mask and a channel's flow are
not written, so a water pixel's history is its surface's. No lock for a one-pixel feature. The
shaders' hot reload does not rebuild this pass's pipeline.

**It allocates nothing in a frame.** The pass makes its images at load and at a resize, and
`engine_view.frame_loop` flies the desert overlook accumulating as well as plain (its records name
the `engine` provider): no engine allocation and no device buffer on the frame's thread in either
flight (R154 leg 2b, 2026-11-15, `msvc-release`).

**Held by** `tests/accumulation_tests.cpp`: off keeps nothing; a `mean` capture is the mean of the
cycle's offset frames within two codes and a second one is the same bytes; in `on` mode a held
view's error against that mean after sixteen frames is under half of one frame's, a replay from a
reset draws the same bytes, and the frame after a reset is the frame a fresh renderer draws; and
the pixels a moved instance leaves are, the frame after, within a quarter of what the mover's own
colour was from what they settle to (a blend that kept the history would leave nine tenths); and
the vertex tier (`RasterMode::Vertex`, which a card with mesh shaders takes when asked) accumulates
twelve frames to the mesh path's bytes.

### Leg 3: the sharper read, reactive surfaces and the fade turned with the phase

Roadmap R158, 2026-11-17. Three of the leg before's "not built", each behind a tunable read at load
and each only in a renderer that accumulates, so a frame drawn without the accumulation is the frame
it was to the byte (the fade's change is in the cull pass and the masked readers, and with no turn
it writes and keeps exactly what it did).

- **The history is read through Catmull-Rom** (`renderer.reconstruction.history_filter`,
  `catmull_rom` by default, `bilinear` the leg before's read). Karis's account of TAA names the
  blur a bilinear history read leaves, "reprojection diffusion": every frame of a pan the history is
  read between texels and a little softer, over the blend's length. Where the four bilinear taps all
  held (the names and the match above), the history is read from the 4 × 4 round them with the
  cubic through the inner two in each axis, and the result is held between the inner four's least
  and greatest so a hard edge does not ring; where a tap failed, or the 4 × 4 leaves the view, the
  validated bilinear read stands. A held view is untouched: its motion is zero, the read lands on a
  texel and both reads are that texel. Measured by its test (a pan of a tenth of a pixel a frame,
  32 frames, against a `mean` capture at the last camera): 1.15 codes rms with the bilinear read,
  0.95 with Catmull-Rom.
- **Reactive surfaces** (`renderer.reconstruction.reactive_weight`, 0.25). A pixel whose colour is
  not its surface's alone trusts its history less: today that is a water surface
  (`k_material_water`, read through the pair's material as the resolve reads it), whose reflection
  and refraction move with the eye and the waves while the motion pass follows the surface. Such a
  pixel is always clipped (`clip_moving`) and takes at least the reactive weight of the new frame.
  It is what the vendors' reactive and transparency masks are for, and Karis's account does the same
  for translucency with a stencil and "minimal feedback", which it says has to stay above zero or the
  jitter shows. A scene with no water material reads nothing for it. A medium's thick regions (the
  design's other reactive case) are not marked yet.
- **The cross-fade turned with the phase** (`renderer.reconstruction.fade_turn`, on). The screen
  door between two levels of a fading transition was a function of the pixel alone
  ([the cross-fade](#the-cross-fade)), so no number of frames could blend it: a pixel in the band
  drew one level for ever. Under the accumulation the cull pass turns each fading pair's two splits
  by `k * 65535 / n` on the hash's ring at phase `k` of `n` (`gfx::CullParams::fade_turn`,
  `turn_splits` in `cluster_cull.slang`; a turned interval may wrap the ring's end, which
  `fade_keeps` reads as two), so over a cycle a pixel's threshold takes n evenly spaced places and
  it is kept in its band's share of the frames. Both sides of a transition turn by the same amount,
  so their pixels stay complementary and the tie rule stands; the shadow rays and the cascades read
  the same table and turn with it. The fade table is written per pair per frame already, so it costs
  an add and a modulo per fading pair.

**Determinism.** The phase is the renderer's own count since the last reset, so all three are
functions of the frames since a reset: a flight from its first path frame (`history_reset`) draws
the same bytes twice, as before.

**Measured** (2026-11-18, 00:00 to 01:15 local, `msvc-release`, RTX 5090, the Windows session

### What a trail is, and what holds it

Roadmap R194, 2026-11-20. The owner turned the accumulation on in the forest at native 4K: better
overall, **but every movement left a trail**, animals and the view as they walked. A trail is
measured, not judged: `tests/trail_tests.cpp` flies a mover across a ground of the other brightness
for thirty frames with the accumulation on, draws the last frame again fresh (a reset: one sample,
nothing of the frames before), and takes the mean |accumulated − fresh| luma, in display codes, over
the pixels the mover left exactly 1, 2, 4 and 8 frames before the last and whose 3 × 3 does not show
it now (that is its edge's antialiasing, which the fresh frame lacks: a palm's leaflets left 7
codes of 91 there with no trail in the picture); the floor is the same over
pixels the mover never touched (a single fresh frame's own aliasing), the contrast the mover's mean
luma against the rest's. Each case holds every age to the floor plus a twentieth of the contrast.
256 × 144, rt off, no shadows, two frames in flight; `ENGINE_TRAIL_CAPTURES=<dir>` writes each
case's last accumulated frame and its fresh one as PNGs.

| codes at age 1, 2, 4, 8 (contrast) | main | this build |
|---|---|---|
| a box the host moves 0.25 m a frame, bright on dark, scene read whole | 8.8, 26.9, 2.0, 14.3 (145) | 0.00, 0.02, 0, 0.01 |
| the same, dark on bright | 3.7, 11.9, 0.8, 4.4 (175) | 0, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01 |
| the same in a streamed world's scene, bright on dark | **123.6, 109.0, 107.7, 84.6** | 0.00, 0.02, 0, 0.01 |
| the same, dark on bright | **75.1, 56.9, 51.4, 32.9** | 0, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01 |
| a tail's box placed again every frame (a game's prop), bright on dark | 121.5, 90.9, 100.5, 66.1 | 0.00, 0.02, 0, 0.01 |
| the same, dark on bright | 60.8, 40.4, 41.6, 21.9 | 0, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01 |
| a skinned walker stepping 0.25 m and swinging ±35° a frame, read whole | 68.4, 58.9, 21.2, 16.9 (144) | 0.01, 0, 0, 0 |
| the same in a streamed world's scene | **127.4, 103.9, 104.3, 84.1** | 0.01, 0, 0, 0 |
| the camera stepping 4 cm a frame past a dark post at 5 m before a bright wall at 25 m | 25.4, 25.4, 25.5, 10.2 (180) | 0.04, 0.03, 0.07, 0.09 |

Floors 0.2 to 0.65 codes. The table was taken before the case left out the pixels beside the
mover's present place (both columns the same measure); as committed, with them left out, this build
gives 0 to 0.06 codes in every row, and **a swaying palm** against the sky (a wind of 1.5, a fifth
of a second a frame, a scene read whole) 2.3, 1.2, 3.0 and 0.1 codes of 91, under the case's bound
of 4.6 (main's not flown on that measure). **Three causes**, in the order they cost:

1. **In a streamed world's scene a move made every vector the camera's.** A move rewrites its
   record in the table sets, and that marked the scene's tables changed exactly as a tail's new
   layout does (`GpuScene::mark_instance_written`); the motion pass then read neither last frame's
   names nor last frame's deform inputs, so a game's actors and every swaying tree had the camera's
   vectors, every tap matched the pixel's motion, and a still pixel is not clipped: the mover's
   colour stayed where it had been and faded at the blend's weight. The forest is such a scene, and
   its actors move every frame. Now the table update says whether the **layout** changed
   (`GpuScene::TableUpdate::layout`: a tail written, numbered again or grown) or only records in
   place (a move, a padding, a terrain chunk's corner), and only the first drops last frame's names
   and inputs (`MotionPass::Frame::tables_changed`).
2. **The nearest surface's vector carried a mover's colour into what it uncovered.** A pixel takes
   the motion of the nearest surface in its 3 × 3 (Karis 2014), so the ground just behind a moving
   post or animal looked itself up where the mover had been and kept that history; in the frames
   after, its own vector carried it on, and a far, slow surface is not clipped. **A pixel at a
   moving boundary** (its own surface's vector and the nearest one's differ by more than
   `motion_match`) is now looked up by its own vector, held to its own instance where the names hold
   and to its own depth where they do not, and clipped as a moving pixel.
3. **Nothing held a tap's depth.** A tap past the match counted if its instance was among the
   3 × 3's, so a mover still beside the pixel let its last place in. The motion pass now writes,
   beside each vector, the depth the pixel's point had a frame ago in last frame's clip space
   (`gfx::MotionParams::prev_depth`, `MotionPass::keep_depth`, only when the accumulation asks:
   4 bytes a pixel, 33 MB at 3840 × 2160), and a tap holds only if last frame's visibility buffer
   has that depth there, within half a percent and the surface's one-sided slope (`depth_holds` in
   `accumulate.slang`; the form is SVGF's, Schied et al. 2017, whose reference implementation in
   Falcor tests a reprojected depth against its screen derivative, read for this row). **A mover's
   history** (an instance the host has moved) past the match counts only where the pixel still shows
   that instance: standing on the ground its foot and the ground are one depth, and membership let
   its colour into the ground beside it, a streak along its path. **A frame whose vectors may be
   wrong** (the layout changed: a tail's mover has the camera's vectors, a tree its instance's) takes
   no tap on the match and no pixel on the nearest surface's vector: each is held to its own depth.

**What is kept.** A still camera on a still scene has every vector zero, no boundary and every tap
matched, so its history test is the one before R194 and its frames are the same bytes ("a still
view converges as before": the sixteenth frame's FNV-1a is 1718842243237908460 on main's code and
on this build, on the card and under the Titan Xp's profile). A crown's edge keeps its history wherever its vectors agree,
as leg 2 measured. **What is given up**: on a frame whose layout changed (a tile arriving, a prop
moved through the tail), no pixel is dilated and every tap is held to its depth, so a crown's edge
pixels that alternate leaf and sky take less history for that frame; and a moving boundary's pixel
no longer averages its neighbour's samples, so a mover's trailing edge is drawn at fewer samples.
**Such frames are most of a walk through a streamed world**: on the forest staging's grounded walk
(2,401 frames at 4.5 m/s) the tables were written on 1,880 frames, tiles arriving and leaving, so
it is there that the depth test does most of its work, and on each of those frames a swaying tree's
vectors are its instance's (the pool's second write reads this frame's inputs), so its leaves are
held to their depths and a crown takes less history while the view walks. What would give those
frames back their trust is per instance and not per frame: which slots a layout wrote, and a deform
table read through last frame's entries; R194's second leg built it
([what a layout change costs the accumulation](#what-a-layout-change-costs-the-accumulation)).
**Not done**: a tail's mover is held by its depth alone on the frames it moves, so one that slides
along a surface at that surface's depth (a decal, a flat prop) is not told from it; last frame's
pair table is not kept (a third table set, 134 MB of pairs on the forest), which is what names
across a changed layout would need (the second leg's section below says why the slots a change
wrote make it unnecessary for the changes a walk makes). The far forest's hand-off moved instances
without the moved table until the second leg.

**What it costs** (2026-11-20, 22:34 to 23:03, `msvc-release`, RTX 5090, the forest staging at
3840 × 2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt`, the bounce, micromaps, the accumulation on, the grounded
walk `walk-grounded.json`, 2,401 frames, one repeat, both flights deterministic; the Windows session
locked for both and the card's clocks at 2.9 GHz at each end, so the pair is comparable and neither
side is an unlocked figure; others held 24 % of the CPU on main's flight and 7 to 12 % on this
build's): the frame passes (the accumulation and the encode) 1.267 ms at the median, 1.586 at p95
and 1.969 at p99 on main's copied-out build (2de3230c), 1.362, 1.602 and 1.827 on this one; the
motion pass with the pool's second write 1.016, 2.283 and 2.395 against 1.066, 2.316 and 2.435 (the
depth's write); the frame 19.390 ms at the median and 24.884 at p99 against 19.538 and 24.950. So
about 0.1 ms at the median in the accumulation and 0.05 in the motion pass, and nothing past the
pair's noise at p99. Off it costs nothing: no buffer is made and no pass recorded.

**Held by** `tests/trail_tests.cpp` (the table above, `msvc-debug`, the RTX 5090 and again under
`ENGINE_GFX_TEST_DEVICE=titanxp`, whose vertex tier gave the same figures to the hundredth), and
`accumulation_tests.cpp` and `motion_tests.cpp` unchanged and passing on both.

### What a layout change costs the accumulation

Roadmap R194, second leg, 2026-11-21. The first leg's rule held **every** pixel of a frame whose
streamed tables changed their layout to its depth, and dropped every deformed instance's last-frame
inputs, and on the forest staging's walk that was 1,880 frames of 2,401. **Now a layout change
costs what it touched.**

**What a layout change rewrites, and how the frame knows.** A streamed world's tail is blocks, each
with its own run of instance slots and a reserved run of pairs
([instances that come and go](#instances-that-come-and-go)), so a tile that arrives, leaves or
changes writes its own slots (`SlotWrite`) and nothing else, and every other slot keeps its
instance, its first pair and with them every pair id it had — and a swaying tree its deform record,
which is per resident tree and handed between trees only through a written slot
([streamed trees sway](#streamed-trees-sway)). So the change already knows exactly what it touched:
`GpuScene::write_slots` notes each written run (`note_fresh`), with the slots past a tail that
shrank, and the next frame's `prepare_tables` hands them over sorted and merged
(`GpuScene::TableUpdate::fresh`, a few runs a tile and at most `k_fresh_capacity`, 1,024). The motion
pass copies them into its frame slot's table (`gfx::MotionParams::fresh`, 432 bytes a view now), and
the accumulation reads the same (`renderer::AccumulateParams::fresh`, 176 bytes with the census
below). Then:

- **An instance in a fresh slot is new to it**: its vector is its own transform's and the camera's
  (the motion pass skips the pool's second write for it, whose record held another tree's pose or
  none last frame), and its pixels, and any pixel whose nearest surface is one, are held to their
  depth alone, as the first leg held a whole frame.
- **A name of last frame's that this frame's pair table puts in a fresh slot names nothing**: the
  pair belonged to a tile that left, or to another before the slot was written. Such a tap is not
  among any 3 × 3's instances, and **the match proves nothing for it**: a tile that left was as still
  as the ground it stood on, so last frame's motion there matches the ground's, and without this the
  ground it uncovered kept its colour ("a tile that leaves leaves none", which fails without the rule).
- **Every other pixel keeps all it had**: its vector, the nearest surface's dilation, its names, and
  a swaying tree's last-frame inputs (`MotionPass::prev_inputs_` stays on).
- **What still falls to the whole frame** (`TableUpdate::whole`): pairs numbered again (T154's tight
  layout moves the first pair of slots it did not write, so a pair of last frame's may now be
  another slot's), a growth of the stride or the instance capacity, a relayout (the deform and pose
  tables made again), and a change past the table's room. `renderer.reconstruction.layout_follow`
  (on) set false is the first leg's rule, for a measurement's other side.

**Last frame's pair table is not kept, and need not be.** Keeping it (a third table set, 134 MB of
pairs on the forest) would name last frame's pixels across any layout; the slots tell the same for
every change that wrote slots and moved no pair, which is the change a walk makes. A tight layout's
numbering is a few shift runs over slots (`change_shifts_`), so following it is a map sized by the
change too: last frame's pair ranges per shift run and their offset, which the accumulation would
search like the fresh runs. Not built: it is rarer than the frames it would give back
(2 frames of the staging's walk of 2,401, a growth and a compaction's, against 1,870 that wrote slots), and it is a row of its own if the census says otherwise. **A tail's prop placed
again every frame** has no identity across two tails (the same slot may hold another instance of
its mesh, from another tile), so it is not followed: its slot is fresh and it is held to its depth,
as the first leg measured ("an instance of the world's tail placed again every frame").

**The far forest's hand-off says what it moved** (`SceneRenderer::set_dynamic_instances`,
`GpuScene::mark_instances_new`): each far tile's instance jumps between its tile's corner and its
parking place under the ground, a move the frame was not told of, so its vectors were the camera's
as if it had stood there, and a name of it from last frame (a stand-in that went to its parking
place) still named it. Its slot is now one of the frame's fresh runs, as a written slot is: the
stand-in that comes in where its tile's trees left is held to its depth (where the trees stood at
its depth it takes their history, a hand-over), and nothing of last frame keeps the one that left.
Not the moved table (`MotionPass::note_moves`), the first leg's proposal: a jump has no path to
follow, and that table's membership is for good — it would hold 4,096 instances, and each far
instance in it would lose the match test at its silhouette against the sky for the rest of the
session, which is where a distant crown line shimmers.

**The census** (`AccumulationPass::Census`; the frame record's `history_pixels`, `history_taken`,
`history_trusted`, `history_fresh`, `history_runs`, `history_whole`, `FrameRecord` version 24):
per frame, counted by wave in the accumulation pass under `renderer.reconstruction.census`, the pixels with a history to read, those that
took one, those that took one with their own vectors trusted, and those of instances new to their
slot.

On the forest staging's grounded walk (2,401 frames at 3840 × 2160, `--raster rt --shadows rt`,
the bounce, micromaps, 2026-11-21 02:04 to 02:07, `msvc-release`): the tables wrote slots on
1,870 frames (a median of 2 runs, at most 8), and on those frames **a median of 97.07 % of the
pixels took a history with their vectors trusted** (5 % of frames under 93.0 %, the least 60.4 %),
against 97.12 % on the 528 frames that wrote none; under the first leg's rule every one of the
1,870 frames trusted no pixel at all. The pixels of instances new to their slots were a median of
0 % of a frame and at most 2.1 % (a tile arriving near the eye). Two frames fell to the whole frame
(a growth and a compaction's numbering). The far forest has 4,754 tiles: more than the moved table
holds.

**The census is a measurement's switch** (`renderer.reconstruction.census`, off). Its block is host-visible, so every add crosses the bus: four words cost the frame passes 3.93 ms at the median where the first leg's took 1.36 (the same walk an hour apart, quiet frames and layout frames alike), and 64 buckets by workgroup 7.08, more lines across the same bus. A device-local block copied out once a frame would make it free; until then it is on only for a flight that wants the numbers above, and the census fields are zero otherwise.

**Shimmer on a crown** (`trail_tests.cpp`, "a crown shimmers no more for a layout change elsewhere"):
the young palm with no wind, a camera stepping a millimetre a frame, a tail of one palm behind the
camera placed again every frame or once; the mean over the crown's edge pixels of luma's standard
deviation over frames 16 to 47. Each frame drawn fresh: **17.4** codes over 3,712 pixels; accumulated with the tail placed once: **6.50**; with it placed again every frame: **6.50**, the same to the last digit (the frames are the same bytes); with it placed again every frame under the first leg's rule: **25.5**, worse than no accumulation at all, because an edge pixel held to its depth takes its history on the frames its tap shows the leaf and refuses it on those it shows the sky, so the blend jumps between a long history and one frame (`msvc-debug`, the RTX 5090 and the titanxp profile alike).

**Not done.** A tile that leaves leaves a faint outline where its antialiased edge was: an edge
pixel whose last frame showed the ground keeps a history that holds some of the tile's colour from
the frames before, and a still pixel is not clipped (the case's figures: the 744 pixels the box
covered are at the floor, 0.007 codes, and 41 pixels of its edge are 94.8 codes from the fresh
frame a frame later), as on main and on the first leg. Clipping every pixel whose last 3 × 3 held a
name that left would end it, at a read of last frame's 3 × 3; a row of its own. The far forest's
hand-off has no case: one was written ("the hand-off leaves no trail of a stand-in under the
accumulation") and deleted at the join (2026-11-21). At its view only 13 pixels of a stand-in's
ground were left, all beside the near tiles' new trees; with the trail cases' exclusion of every
pixel whose fresh 3 × 3 holds a tree, at 640 × 360, 11 were left, 5.28 codes from the frame drawn
fresh against a floor of 0.03 and 14.65 for a kept history, the same on both tiers: a third of a
kept history over too few pixels to say whether it is a trail. A fixture with more of a
stand-in's ground in view is a row of its own.

**What it costs** (2026-11-21, the forest staging's grounded walk as above, census off, `msvc-release`, RTX 5090, the session locked; the first leg's tip flown 02:30 and this one 03:45, between other rows' GPU runs, never beside one): the frame passes 1.359 ms at the median, 1.592 at p95 and 1.749 at p99 on the first leg's build, 1.574, 1.852 and 1.922 on this one; the motion pass 1.088 against 1.087; the frame 19.643 ms at the median and 25.232 at p99 against 19.791 and 25.349. So about 0.2 ms at the median in the accumulation, which now takes the trusted path (the dilation, the match, the sharper read on the pixels whose four taps held) on the 1,870 frames that took the depth path before, and the fresh runs' searches; the motion pass's cost is unchanged. The walk's frame records allocate as the first leg's did (3,247 after frame 200 against 3,257: the streamed world's own).

**Held by** `trail_tests.cpp`: "a layout change elsewhere costs the picture nothing" (the swaying
palm in a streamed scene under a camera stepping a centimetre a frame, with a tail placed again
every frame behind it, draws every frame to the byte as with the tail placed once; under the first
leg's rule 39 of the 40 frames differ, the last 0.83 codes a pixel), the shimmer case above, "a tile that leaves leaves none", and every case
of the first leg, on the card and under `ENGINE_GFX_TEST_DEVICE=titanxp`.

## Sampling over time: a reconstruction provider

Roadmap R159, stage 3 of [the design](../experiments/temporal-sampling.md#part-4-the-plan-in-stages):
**the registration point** a reconstruction method plugs into, as a sky provider registers its
model ([ADR-0048](../adr/0048-the-sky-is-a-providers-model-drawn-by-the-renderer.md)) and a frame
pass its light. `systems/renderer/reconstruction.h` is the whole contract: a provider is a name
and five functions (`create`, `destroy`, `resize`, `record`, `device_bytes`) over a state of its
own, registered once at start-up (`register_reconstruction_provider`) and chosen by name at load
(`renderer.reconstruction.provider`). Each frame it is handed one struct, `ReconstructionFrame`:
the frame pass's context (the graph, the linear colour image, the views, the visibility buffer
whose high words are the depth, the display's curve), the motion buffer and last frame's
visibility buffer and motion per view, this frame's sub-pixel offset and phase, and whether the
frame before is this one's history; it returns one image, which the encode reads in the colour
image's place (`FramePassReport::color`). So a provider is a frame pass at
`FramePassStage::Reconstruction` (`src/reconstruction_pass.h` is the adapter), declares its reads
and writes through the graph, and records no barrier of its own.

**Two are built in.** `engine` is the accumulation above (the renderer makes it from its own
passes, so it is not a desc; naming it is `renderer.reconstruction.accumulation=on`), and `null`
hands its input on: a frame drawn through it is the inputs' own frame through the linear image and
its encode, which its test holds to a code. Naming any other turns the accumulation off and the
inputs on; a name nothing registered refuses the load with a sentence. **The engine links no
vendor's provider**: one comes from a capability its consumer builds against an SDK it supplies
(roadmap R161, [ADR-0064](../adr/0064-every-measurement-is-native.md) decision 4), and registers
itself the way a sky provider does. Every frame drawn through a provider is a reconstructed frame:
`Reconstruction::provider` is `Registered`, `Reconstruction::registered` its name, and the record's
`reconstruction` block names it and carries no cost ([the measurement rule](#sampling-over-time-the-measurement-rule)).

**Not built.** `engine.protocol.RenderStats` does not carry the block yet: the protocol is another
row's to change. A provider is handed no reactivity mask and no exposure scalar as such (the
engine's own reads the material table and the display curve directly); a vendor's adapter will
need both, and the depth as a float image, and those are its row's. Internal sizes below the
output's are R160's: `output_width` and `output_height` are the frame's own until then.

**Held by** `tests/accumulation_tests.cpp`: the built-in names cannot be taken and a name is
registered once; the null provider's frames are the inputs' own within a code, and the renderer
says it drew them through a registered provider.
